chapters.title: Chapter 301: It’s Over [5]
paragraphs: "...show me what you’ve got."

’...Is this guy stupid? Or is he really crazy?’ Aeshvin stared at Soren, the corner of his mouth twitching. He almost laughed at the absurdity of it. After everything, this man was actually giving him an opening. ’No, wait... Could it be... he has some kind of trump card too?’
The thought gave him pause, but only for a moment.
’No... It doesn’t matter.’
His twisted smile returned, blood still staining his teeth. Even if the crazy bastard had a trump card, he would tear it apart and take it for himself. This was the moment everything would change.
’Moron, you should have killed me when you had the chance!’

"Since..." Aeshvin opened his mouth to speak, to mock, to unleash everything he had left. However, the words came out broken, barely audible through his cracked lips. "Y-you... want... to... die... s-gh!"
Soren’s fist slammed into his face.
"W-Wai-"
Another punch.
"S-Sto—!"
Another.

Each blow landed before Aeshvin could even finish a word, his head snapping back and forth, blood spraying from his mouth and nose. The world blurred, and through the swelling and the pain, he could only watch as Soren pulled out another potion and forced it down his throat.
’W-What the hell is wrong with him?!’
The wounds began to close, the pain fading just enough for him to think again. But the relief was short-lived as the beating started all over once more.
’He’s insane... He’s completely insane!’

Aeshvin knew he was insane himself. He had done terrible things and enjoyed most of them. But being on the receiving end of this cruelty made him realize there were different kinds of madness. His own was born from greed and amusement. This... this was something else.
There was no joy or thrill in the bastard’s eyes, only chilling patience, as if breaking him were no different from a task that had to be finished.
"What? Are you angry?" Soren paused, his bloodied fist still raised. "Angry because there’s nothing you can do?"
’Since you wanna die so badly...’
"How does it feel to be the one who’s completely helpless?"
’Then I will grant your wish.’
"You’ve tormented so many people like th-
"DIE!"
Aeshvin’s voice cracked as the word left his mouth.
In that instant, the air around them shifted, and both bodies went still. Soren’s eyes rolled back, and he slumped to the cave floor, his body limp.
Aeshvin’s head dropped back against the stone, the light fading from his eyes as his heartbeat slowed... and then stopped.
The cave fell quiet.
’Where... am I?’

Aeshvin opened his eyes, but there was nothing but darkness. It stretched in every direction, swallowing any sense of place or direction. His body felt weightless, like he was suspended in a void with no beginning or end.
’Did I... fail?’
However, as he checked his surroundings more thoroughly, his lips curled up.
’No, I made it!’
This was the bastard’s soul space. And now that he was inside, it was only a matter of time before it belonged to him.
’Even though I hate you... I should still thank you for blessing me with such a perfect body. So thank you, bastard. I’ll make sure to use it well~.’
His grin widened at the thought of soon owning the body.
’Let’s start, shall we?’

He stretched his senses outward, searching for the core of Soren’s soul. Fortunately, it didn’t take long. Somewhere in the distance, a faint light flickered, small but stubborn against the endless black.
’Found you!’

Aeshvin laughed and attacked immediately, with no time to waste. Once the original soul recovered and woke up, the battle would become far more dangerous. A soul defending its own body was never an easy opponent, no matter how strong the invader. So he would end this before the bastard even had the chance to open his eyes.

His form surged through the void, dark tendrils lashing out one after another toward that small, flickering light. Years of training, countless treasures, and the souls of everyone he had ever devoured had gone into forging his power. Every strike was backed by all of it, a relentless assault meant to snuff out the bastard’s soul before it could even stir.
’Don’t blame me,’ he thought as he closed in. ’You’re the one who let me in.’
’Now, die!’
The first wave of attacks landed.
Boom-!
Flicker~.
The light dimmed under the onslaught as his tendrils tore into it. Aeshvin pressed harder, pouring more of himself into each strike, determined not to give the bastard even a second of reprieve.
But a moment later, the light brightened again.
’W-What? T-This must be a self-defense mechanism!’

He guessed and attacked again, faster this time, his form twisting and coiling around the soul like a serpent. He struck without pause, each blow carrying enough force to shatter the soul into fragments. The light wavered, nearly vanishing under the pressure... and then flared back to life, perhaps a bit stronger than before.
’No... No, no, no!’
Aeshvin’s confidence cracked, just a little.
’This must be an illusion! My eyes must be playing a prank on me!’
He consoled himself and then threw even more power into the next barrage, his attacks growing wilder and more desperate. But...
’...How is he still not dead?!’
No matter how many times he thought he had won, no matter how close the light came to dying, it always returned, and each time, it came back brighter, more powerful, and more intense than the last.

On the other hand, his own form kept getting weaker as he poured more and more of his essence into each attack. What had started as an invasion was slowly turning into a losing battle, and he could feel it slipping through his grasp.
’No... I can’t... I can’t lose like this! It’s not over yet!’
He gritted his teeth. But deep down, he realized that if he kept going at this rate, he would burn himself out before the bastard’s soul even woke up, let alone break.
’I... I have to gamble... I need to use everything I have in this last strike!’

chapters.title: Chapter 302: It’s Over [6]
paragraphs: Aeshvin gulped and started drawing on every soul he had ever devoured, every scrap of power he had left, and putting it all into one last desperate attack.
’If this doesn’t work, I’m finished. But if it does...’
Aeshvin’s eyes locked onto the light, still pulsing calmly as if mocking him.
’Then everything will be mine!’
He aimed and released the attack. It shot forward, tearing through the void like a falling star and struck the light dead center. And for a single breathless moment, everything went still.
Then the whole soul space began to tremble violently.
Rrrrumble-!

’!’ Aeshvin’s eyes lit up as the light started flickering, shrinking, collapsing in on itself. He watched as it dimmed further and further, fading into a tiny dot, a dying ember about to go out. ’I did it! I finally did it!
Aeshvin clenched his fists, his chest swelling with triumph. This was it! The body, the power, everything was about to be his! But just as the light was about to vanish completely... it exploded.

A blinding radiance erupted from that tiny dot, flooding the soul space with light so intense that it even swallowed the whole black void. The darkness he had gathered around himself peeled away, scattering like ash in the wind. The light pressed against him from every side, burning away what little remained of his soul.
’No... NO!’
His body began to disintegrate, the light tearing through the very core of his being until there was nothing left to resist.
’Nooo...’
’W-What... happened?’
’D-Did I... die?’
’If so... where am I?’
’...Why can I... still... think?’
His thoughts scattered before he could hold onto them. Everything felt distant, like he was drifting through fog.
Then, slowly, Aeshvin forced his eyes open.
’Urgh... I... I can’t... see...’
His vision was a mess of light and shadow, his eyelids heavy as stones. He tried to move, but his body barely responded. He felt hollowed out, like an empty shell that had been left to rot.
Just then, he noticed something familiar.
’It’s... that light...?’
At first, it was a tiny dot, but as it drew closer and closer, it grew larger, and its features became clearer.
Aeshvin recognized the figure instantly. There’s no way he would mistake it, since he had tried to make it his own just moments ago, only to be reduced to this pitiful state.
’...I failed... huh...’
Strangely, he felt nothing. He wasn’t panicked, nor did he have the desperate urge to fight back as before. Perhaps it was because he was too broken, his soul drained to the limit.
He silently stared back at the face of demise.
"Thank you for doing exactly what I thought you would." Soren’s voice cut through the silence. "I’ve been stuck at a bottleneck for a while now. You gave me the push I needed to break through."
"...I... You... used me?" Aeshvin managed to utter these words. "H-How...?"

"Well, you could say that I did," Soren replied. "But of course, I’m not some kind of genius mastermind. I just had more information on you and your group, and enough time to think and prepare. You, on the other hand, didn’t know much about me. You probably thought of me as a weak chef, lucky to have married Ethea and to have a powerful magic beast on his side. You probably didn’t even bother to check what I, my bond, and... my wife were really capable of. And that confidence... No, that arrogance of yours... it cost you everything."
’...’ Aeshvin went silent. "...I... see..."

To think he had been played from the very beginning. All his schemes, all his careful planning, all the years he had spent building his power... and in the end, he had walked right into the palm of someone he dismissed as prey.
A bitter smile tugged at his cracked lips.
’...I... I forgot my... past... my rules...’
’...How laughable.’

He had always been careful before. Thorough in everything he did, never underestimating an opponent no matter how weak they seemed. But somewhere along the way, after so many victories and so many bodies under his feet, that caution had started to fade. He had stopped seeing people as threats and started seeing them as toys.
And now...
That mistake had cost him everything.
’Haha...’
’She was right...’
He recalled what Ethea told him.
’It was already over...’
Perhaps... It would have been much better if he had surrendered... At least he would be alive that way.
’...No. It’s... too late... to regret now...’
Aeshvin stared at Soren and whispered.
"...Kill... me... please..."
"..." Soren stared back at him and replied. "I was going to do it even if you didn’t ask me."
Then, he raised his hand and flicked his fingers. A thin blade of light shot forward and pierced through Aeshvin’s remaining soul.
Aeshvin’s body stiffened for a moment, but he managed a faint, broken smile as his consciousness started to slip away.
"...Thank... you..."
Piece by piece, he scattered until there was nothing left of him.
"...It’s over," Soren whispered and fell silent.
Honestly, he didn’t feel anything at all, despite this being the first time he killed someone with his own hands.
Perhaps it was because Sevihan had been too far gone to be called human anymore. Or perhaps it was because Soren had already made peace with what needed to be done long before this moment came.
’...Let’s go back and finish the rest.’
With that thought, he closed his eyes. A moment later, he opened them and found himself back in the cave.
’...Urgh.’
He noticed he was lying on the ground, with half of his body on top of Sevihan’s corpse. So he quickly tried to stand up and distance himself.
"Urgh..."
However, no matter how hard he tried, his body refused to listen.
’...The side effects must have kicked in.’

He didn’t know how much time had passed since they were in his soul space, but Limit Break’s duration was about to end in a few minutes, so this level of exhaustion wasn’t strange. Not to mention how much he had abused Amplification this whole time. His body had been pushed far beyond its limits, and every inch of him felt like it was being held together by sheer will.
Honestly, he should be grateful he was still alive and in one piece.
But...
Even through the haze of exhaustion, one thought kept pressing against his mind.
’Malakor...’ He called out in his mind. ’Is... Ethea safe?’

chapters.title: Chapter 303: Urgh...
paragraphs: ’Is Ethea safe?’
’Don’t worry, Master.’ Malakor replied almost immediately. ’Nothing happened to her. I was watching everything, and she handled the situation on her own so well that I didn’t even have to step in.’
’I see,’ Soren replied, his heart finally settling.
’It was quite a sight to witness, honestly.’ Malakor added, recalling what he witnessed earlier. ’Even without her past powers, she carried herself like a true Empress. She truly deserves the title.’
Soren let out a faint breath, the ghost of a smile tugging at his lips. ’That’s my wife.’
’...Do you want to see her?’ Malakor asked.

’...No, let me rest a bit first.’ Soren replied after a moment’s thought. ’I... I don’t want her to see me like this. And I should at least recover enough to move freely. I also need to wash up and wear some clothes before showing up in front of her.’
’...I understand,’ Malakor replied, realizing Soren didn’t want Ethea to feel responsible for his injuries or worry more than she already had. But...

’Master... She’s already seen everything that needed to be seen...’ Malakor decided to reveal the truth and told Soren what had transpired earlier in that room. ’I think you don’t need to worry too much.’
’...Alright. But I still need a little rest.’ Soren replied. ’Can you... tell her that I’m safe for me then?’
’...Leave it to me.’
’W-Wait. Before that, can you teleport me back to our room?’
’Yes. However, what should we do with the corpse?’
’...’ Soren fell silent. He then tilted his head and looked at the dead body of Sevihan. ’Just leave him buried here.’
Malakor didn’t question the decision. ’Understood. I’ll collapse the cave as well, so no one stumbles upon it.’
Soren gave a faint nod. ’Good. Then take me back. And... please put me in the bathroom.’

A moment later, shadows coiled around him, and the cold air of the cave disappeared. When Soren opened his eyes again, he was sitting on the tiled floor of the luxurious bathroom, his back resting against the wall.
’Thank you.’
’Rest well...’
Malakor left, and Soren began reviewing everything that had happened while his constitution and abilities did their work.
He analyzed his fights, his plan, where he made mistakes, where he’d been reckless, and where he’d made the right call. He also thought about what to do next. Soon he recovered enough to move.
"Urgh..."
He slowly stood up, using the bathtub’s edge for support. Then, he filled the tub with warm water and stepped in. The warmth relaxed his muscles, easing the knots and cleansing away blood and dirt.
He spent more than half an hour inside the bathroom.

But when he came out, there was no trace of the bloodied mess from before. His hair was still a little damp, his clothes clean and neat. The only signs of what he’d been through were the faint cuts and bruises that hadn’t fully healed yet, but even those were hard to notice unless someone looked closely.
He looked at himself in the mirror and nodded in satisfaction.
’Although I won’t be able to fool her, at least she won’t have to see me looking like a corpse.’
With that thought, he reached out to Malakor and asked him to teleport to where Ethea was. A moment later, he found himself in front of a door. He took a deep breath and spoke.
"It’s me, dear."
"...Wait a moment."

Ethea’s voice came from inside, and Soren caught the faintest hint of relief and happiness in it. A few seconds later, the door opened, and there she was, sitting in her wheelchair with her hands folded in her lap.
Her expression was calm, but the moment she saw him, her eyes lit up, and a lovely smile spread across her lips.
"Welcome back, dear."

She then raised her arms toward him, and Soren’s heart gave a quick, unexpected beat. However, he pushed the feeling down and crossed the room in a few steps. Kneeling in front of her wheelchair, he wrapped his arms around her and pulled her into a careful embrace.
"I’m back."
Ethea hugged him back, her arms slipping around his neck and holding him close. Her grip was gentle but firm, as if she was afraid he might disappear if she let go.
"I was... worried."
Soren closed his eyes, letting the warmth of her presence ease the last of the tension from his body.
"I know," he said quietly. "But it’s over now.
"Mm..." Ethea hummed, pulling back just enough to look up at him. Her eyes were soft, glistening faintly under the light.
"Thank you," she whispered sweetly. "You... You were amazing out there. I... I’m proud of you."
Soren blinked, caught off guard for a moment. Then a small smile tugged at his lips.
"Thank you." He whispered back. "I am proud of you too. I couldn’t have done it without you."
Ethea’s eyes curved into soft crescents as she gazed deep into his eyes.
"Dear..."

Soren felt himself sinking into her gaze, the world around them slowly losing its edges. He didn’t notice when his body started leaning closer, drawn by an invisible thread that seemed to pull them together.
Their faces inched nearer, breaths mingling in the small space that remained. Eventually, the pull between them grew too strong to resist, and just as they gave in—
"Urgh..."
A low groan echoed from the nearby sofa, cutting through the silence like a dropped glass.

Soren and Ethea’s eyes widened at the same time, and they pulled apart as if a cold wind had swept between them. Soren straightened, his heart racing, while Ethea turned her face away, her cheeks tinted pink.
Thump! Thump! Thump...!
Soren’s chest heaved as his pulse raced out of control.
’What was that...?’ he thought, still feeling the ghost of her breath on his lips. ’D-Did I... just... k...ki...’
His brain short-circuited, freezing mid-thought.
’...’ Ethea pressed her hands firmly into her lap to hide the subtle shake in her fingers while her heart kept fluttering in a way she hadn’t felt in a long time. ’We... We almost... k-k-kissed...’

’It was quite a sight to witness, honestly.’ Malakor added, recalling what he witnessed earlier. ’Even without her past powers, she carried herself like a true Empress.
She truly deserves the title.’
Soren let out a faint breath, the ghost of a smile tugging at his lips. ’That’s my wife.’
’...Do you want to see her?’ Malakor asked.
’...No, let me rest a bit first.’ Soren replied after a moment’s thought. ’I...
I don’t want her to see me like this.
And I should at least recover enough to move freely.
I also need to wash up and wear some clothes before showing up in front of her.’
’...I understand,’ Malakor replied, realizing Soren didn’t want Ethea to feel responsible for his injuries or worry more than she already had.
But...
’Master...
She’s already seen everything that needed to be seen...’ Malakor decided to reveal the truth and told Soren what had transpired earlier in that room. ’I think you don’t need to worry too much.’
’...Alright.
But I still need a little rest.’ Soren replied. ’Can you... tell her that I’m safe for me then?’
’...Leave it to me.’
’W-Wait.
Before that, can you teleport me back to our room?’
’Yes.
However, what should we do with the corpse?’
’...’ Soren fell silent.
He then tilted his head and looked at the dead body of Sevihan. ’Just leave him buried here.’
Malakor didn’t question the decision. ’Understood.
I’ll collapse the cave as well, so no one stumbles upon it.’
Soren gave a faint nod. ’Good.
Then take me back.
And... please put me in the bathroom.’
A moment later, shadows coiled around him, and the cold air of the cave disappeared.
When Soren opened his eyes again, he was sitting on the tiled floor of the luxurious bathroom, his back resting against the wall.
’Thank you.’
’Rest well...’
Malakor left, and Soren began reviewing everything that had happened while his constitution and abilities did their work.
He analyzed his fights, his plan, where he made mistakes, where he’d been reckless, and where he’d made the right call.
He also thought about what to do next.
Soon he recovered enough to move.
"Urgh..."
He slowly stood up, using the bathtub’s edge for support.
Then, he filled the tub with warm water and stepped in.
The warmth relaxed his muscles, easing the knots and cleansing away blood and dirt.
He spent more than half an hour inside the bathroom.
But when he came out, there was no trace of the bloodied mess from before.
His hair was still a little damp, his clothes clean and neat.
The only signs of what he’d been through were the faint cuts and bruises that hadn’t fully healed yet, but even those were hard to notice unless someone looked closely.
He looked at himself in the mirror and nodded in satisfaction.
’Although I won’t be able to fool her, at least she won’t have to see me looking like a corpse.’
With that thought, he reached out to Malakor and asked him to teleport to where Ethea was.
A moment later, he found himself in front of a door.
He took a deep breath and spoke.
"It’s me, dear."
"...Wait a moment."
Ethea’s voice came from inside, and Soren caught the faintest hint of relief and happiness in it.
A few seconds later, the door opened, and there she was, sitting in her wheelchair with her hands folded in her lap.
Her expression was calm, but the moment she saw him, her eyes lit up, and a lovely smile spread across her lips.
"Welcome back, dear."
She then raised her arms toward him, and Soren’s heart gave a quick, unexpected beat.
However, he pushed the feeling down and crossed the room in a few steps.
Kneeling in front of her wheelchair, he wrapped his arms around her and pulled her into a careful embrace.
"I’m back."
Ethea hugged him back, her arms slipping around his neck and holding him close.
Her grip was gentle but firm, as if she was afraid he might disappear if she let go.
"I was... worried."
Soren closed his eyes, letting the warmth of her presence ease the last of the tension from his body.
"I know," he said quietly.
"But it’s over now.
"Mm..." Ethea hummed, pulling back just enough to look up at him.
Her eyes were soft, glistening faintly under the light.
"Thank you," she whispered sweetly.
"You...
You were amazing out there.
I’m proud of you."
Soren blinked, caught off guard for a moment.
Then a small smile tugged at his lips.
"Thank you." He whispered back.
"I am proud of you too.
I couldn’t have done it without you."
Ethea’s eyes curved into soft crescents as she gazed deep into his eyes.
"Dear..."
Soren felt himself sinking into her gaze, the world around them slowly losing its edges.
He didn’t notice when his body started leaning closer, drawn by an invisible thread that seemed to pull them together.
Their faces inched nearer, breaths mingling in the small space that remained.
Eventually, the pull between them grew too strong to resist, and just as they gave in—
"Urgh..."
A low groan echoed from the nearby sofa, cutting through the silence like a dropped glass.
Soren and Ethea’s eyes widened at the same time, and they pulled apart as if a cold wind had swept between them.
Soren straightened, his heart racing, while Ethea turned her face away, her cheeks tinted pink.
Thump!
Thump!
Thump...!
Soren’s chest heaved as his pulse raced out of control.
’What was that...?’ he thought, still feeling the ghost of her breath on his lips. ’D-Did I... just... k...ki...’
His brain short-circuited, freezing mid-thought.
’...’ Ethea pressed her hands firmly into her lap to hide the subtle shake in her fingers while her heart kept fluttering in a way she hadn’t felt in a long time. ’We...
We almost... k-k-kissed...’

chapters.title: Chapter 304: Request
paragraphs: "Urgh..."
Roya’s eyelids fluttered weakly before she forced them open, her vision blurry and unfocused at first. She blinked a few times to adjust to her surroundings.
"W-Where... am... I?"
She muttered as the details slowly sharpened, the shapes around her turning into walls, furniture, and two familiar figures standing a short distance away.
"...E-Ethea?"
She called out weakly.

In an instant, the woman in the wheelchair and the man turned in her direction, their eyes lighting up, filled with relief and a hint of eagerness mixed with awkwardness that Roya, in her groggy state, completely missed.
"P-Princess!"
"S-Senior Sister!"
’They,’ Roya blinked again, her thoughts still sluggish, ’look... so happy to see me...’

Her lips curled up as she tried to sit up. However, her body refused to listen to her. It felt heavy and disconnected, like her limbs belonged to someone else. A strange numbness clung to her, and for a moment she didn’t know what to do.
"Princess, are you ok?"
Ethea’s husband asked worriedly.

"A-Ah, yes..." Roya replied awkwardly, gritted her teeth, and forced herself to move again. Slowly, the strange feeling began to disappear, and strength returned to her arms bit by bit. After some struggle, she managed to sit upright on the sofa.
As she looked forward and saw the couple looking at her worriedly, warmth bloomed in her chest, pushing aside the lingering embarrassment she felt.

She straightened her posture, smoothing the creases of her dress as best as she could, and gave the couple a subtle grateful nod. "Thank you... for worrying about me." She paused, collecting her thoughts. "But... can you tell me what happened while I was unconscious? Who saved me?"
"Wait..." Ethea hesitated for a moment before speaking. "Do you remember anything? Before you lost consciousness?

Roya nodded. "After I received the signal from you, I immediately sent my secret guard team to help. But not long after they left..." She lowered her head, recalling the moment. "Three black-robed figures ambushed me. I... I couldn’t even put up a proper fight. One of them used a powerful mental attack, making my head dizzy, but I still managed to cast a spell. But... it didn’t work, and... everything went dark after that."
"I..." She looked back up at them. "I just woke up since then."
Ethea and Soren exchanged a glance, understanding crossing their features.

A moment later, Soren spoke. "In that case, I will leave you two alone and help with the clean-up outside. Ethea will explain everything you want to know. And please... don’t leave this room until I return."
Roya nodded, though her expression indicated that she approved of Soren’s considerate move. "Thank you."
Soren nodded and turned back to Ethea. "I’ll come back soon. Stay safe."
"Be careful and don’t push yourself too hard," Ethea replied.
"Mm, I promise." Soren smiled, and with another nod to Roya, he turned to leave.
Roya was a little confused by their exchange but stayed silent until the door clicked shut. Then she turned to Ethea, her brow furrowed. "What exactly happened back then? Were you ambushed as well?"
"Mmm," Ethea nodded, looking back at Roya. "It’s a long story."
"It doesn’t matter. Please, tell me everything in detail." Roya said with a serious expression.
Ethea nodded and started. "...Everything started after the semi-final..."
"Excuse me, Mr. Everly. Can I have a moment of your time?"

"Hmm?" Soren paused. He had taken only a few steps from the room when someone called for him. He turned around and found a woman standing there, clad in full black armor that seemed to swallow the light around it.
His body tensed on instinct, but after recognizing her as one of the knights who had fought beside them earlier, he relaxed slightly while keeping his guard up.
"You are?" He asked while using Advanced Appraisal on her.

"It’s an honor to meet you, Mr. Everly. I’m Her Highness Roya’s personal knight. You may call me Knight Aya." The woman introduced herself. "I wanted to thank you for helping us save Her Highness. You put both yourself and your wife at great risk, and the Empire does not take such sacrifices lightly. If there is ever anything within reason that you need, you only have to ask. I will personally see to it that your request reaches the right ears."
"The honor is mine, thank you. And..." Soren paused as he finished analyzing her status. Looking at her mental state, he could tell she was being honest, so he let himself relax a little more.

"She’s safe now, and that’s what matters," he said. "But... I won’t pretend I did it out of pure goodwill. It was my wife who asked me to help, and I couldn’t say no to her. If it had been up to me alone, I would never have put her in danger." He paused, looking calmly at the woman to make his point clear. "But of course, I would still have helped in other ways. After all, she did send us help when we were in trouble."

"I know." The woman smiled behind her mask and nodded. "And... it was you who discovered criminal Lucent’s real identity and came up with the plan after all. Without your help, we probably wouldn’t have succeeded. Even if we did, the casualties would be too great to bear." She paused, her voice softening. "So please, if there’s anything you need, don’t hesitate to ask."
Soren nodded in acceptance and pondered for a moment.

"There is one thing..." He met her gaze. "I am sure you have already found out my and my wife’s real identities. All I ask is that you keep it to yourself and help make sure it doesn’t spread. We don’t want any more attention than necessary."
The woman blinked, caught off guard for a second. Then she nodded, her posture straightening. "Understood. I will do my best to fulfill your request."
"Then, I am going to take my leave." Soren gave her another nod. "Take care."
"Take care." The woman bowed and watched Soren turn and continue on his way.

’...I think you were greatly mistaken about him, my lady. He is a man more than worthy to stand beside Lady Ethea.’ She thought as Soren disappeared down the corridor. ’...I should tell her to apologize properly later.’

chapters.title: Chapter 305: What If...
paragraphs: ’...I really hope she fulfills her promise,’ Soren thought as he walked away. ’However, the princess herself might end up spilling it... I hope Ethea can talk her into keeping quiet.’

The moment Ethea crossed his mind, the image of their faces so close together followed right after. His steps slowed, and a strange warmth rose to his cheeks before he could stop it. His heart gave a sudden, traitorous thump.
’W-What am I even thinking about right now...’ He rubbed the back of his neck and forced his legs to keep moving. ’Focus, Soren. There’s still work to do.’
’...But... What if... What if the princess didn’t interrupt us?’ His face burned even hotter, and he quickened his pace as if he could outrun the thought. ’Would I have actually... kissed her...?’
An image of Ethea’s face, her lips slightly parted and her eyes half-closed, surfaced in his mind before he could block it.
’Urgh!’ He quickly shook his head, trying to scatter it before it could take root. But it clung stubbornly, replaying over and over like a scene he couldn’t escape.
’...But... I haven’t even confessed to her yet...’ he reminded himself, his fingers twitching at his side. ’If I... If I had actually gone through with it... wouldn’t that have been too sudden?’
Another thought followed quickly.

’But... We have been married for three months now... and... at that moment, it felt... natural.’ His steps slowed as he recalled her warmth, her closeness, and the way she leaned in closer, as if drawn by the same pull he had felt. ’...W-Wait.’
’Does that mean... she... she loves me too?’
The thought sent a jolt through him, and his heart responded with a wild rhythm. He stopped walking altogether and pressed a hand against his chest, as if that would calm it down.

’No, no... I’m getting ahead of myself.’ He shook his head and started moving again, faster this time. ’Maybe she was just caught up in the moment. We both were. It doesn’t have to mean anything... right?’
But even as he tried to convince himself, the memory of her expression refused to fade. Her eyes, her smile, the way she had looked at him like he was the only one in the world.
’...Or maybe it does.’
He stopped again.
’...Maybe I’m just making excuses because I’m scared to admit it...’
The silence of the corridor pressed in around him, and for once, he didn’t try to escape it. He simply stood there, staring at the floor, while his heart continued its restless pounding.
’...If she... If she really does feel the same way about me... then what?’
The answer came on its own.
’Wait... What am I even worried about? If she likes me too... isn’t that a good thing?’

He laughed at his own foolishness. However, realizing that the woman he had married, the woman he had spent months protecting and growing closer to, and had slowly come to love, might actually feel the same way about him certainly made him feel like he had won something far greater than any battle.
A smile tugged at the corner of his lips.
’...I should tell her soon.’ He decided, his fingers curling into a loose fist at his side.

He had spent too long holding back, convincing himself that he needed to be certain, that the timing wasn’t right. But after everything they had been through, after nearly losing her more than once, he didn’t want to keep waiting. If there was one thing today had made painfully clear, it was that tomorrow was never promised.
’No... Iwillconfess to her. Iwilltell her how I really feel...’

Soren relaxed his fingers, straightened his posture, and started walking again, his steps lighter than before. There was still much to do, but now he had another reason to look forward to the end of this long day.
"Lord Asad," Soren called out.
"Hmm?" Lord Asad turned around, and for a second, his eyes narrowed as if trying to place the face. Then recognition settled in. "Oh, it’s you."
Soren nodded. "I was wondering if we could talk privately for a moment."
Lord Asad studied him for a brief second, then gave a short nod. "Follow me."
He turned and ordered the nearby officials to continue without him, then led Soren toward a secluded place. He also set up an invisibility and sound-blocking barrier around them.

"Mr. Everly, are you alright?" He asked as he gave Soren a quick once-over, his gaze lingering on the traces of the battle. "We were really worried since you suddenly disappeared. I sent my men to search for you, but none of them could find a trace. Can you tell me what happened? Did you leave by yourself? Or did someone take you against your will?"

"Sir, please calm down." Soren raised a hand to ease the man’s worry. "I am fine, and I left on my own. And I’m sorry for not noticing you beforehand; it was important that I moved quickly." He paused, meeting Lord Asad’s gaze. "I went after the Puppeteer, the one pulling the strings. And... It’s over now. He won’t be hurting anyone else."
Lord Asad stared at him, processing the words. His expression shifted from worry to something more serious.
"You mean... you killed him?"

"...No. I mean I didn’t do it alone." Soren shook his head. "It was my bond who did most of the work. I only lent him a hand where it was needed. Besides..." Soren paused. "I was already at my limit after the fight in the arena. If I had gone after him alone, I wouldn’t be standing here right now."

"I see..." Lord Asad nodded in understanding. "But... Are you certain he’s really dead? And do you have any proof? But please don’t misunderstand; it’s not that I doubt you. It’s just that fellow was far too slippery. I wouldn’t put it past him to fake his death and crawl out of some hole later."
’I guess I can’t blame him for being cautious,’ Soren thought. After everything Sevihan had done, it was only natural for the City Lord to want confirmation.
"I understand, Sir." He gave a small nod. "But you can rest assured. I saw him die with my own eyes. However..."

chapters.title: Chapter 306: Bagdad’s Savior
paragraphs: "...I can’t give you physical proof," Soren explained. "The battle happened deep in an underground cave, and the whole place collapsed after the fight. His body is buried under tons of stone now."
"...Is that so?" Lord Asad raised a brow.

"If you want, we can use the Truth-Seeking Orb to verify my words later." Soren met his gaze without flinching. "I have nothing to hide, and I understand the need for certainty in a matter like this."

"Thank you for understanding, and..." Lord Asad said, his voice softening. Then, without warning, he lowered his head and bowed deeply toward Soren. "On behalf of the city and everyone in it, I offer you my deepest gratitude."
Soren’s eyes widened slightly. "Lord Asad, there’s no need-"

"No," Lord Asad raised his head, his expression firm but still full of gratitude. "This city, no, I owe you a debt that can’t be repaid with words alone. If not for you, Bagdad City would have suffered a tragedy far greater than any of us could imagine. The lives of my people, my city’s future... all of it was saved because of you."
"Come on, it wasn’t that serious," Soren replied, but after seeing Lord Asad’s serious expression, he added. "Or... did you figure something out?"

"...Yes." Lord Asad replied with a dark expression. "We managed to catch another accomplice of theirs while you were fighting with the Hollow Pair. She turned out to be a half-elf and a new member of the Outcasts. At first, she refused to speak, but after some... persuasion, she revealed everything."

"I can’t tell all the details, but their plan was to cause friction between the elves and the Empire. They wanted to manipulate things and make it so that we would blame the elves, and they would blame us, and before anyone realized the truth, both sides would be at each other’s throats." Lord Asad paused and laughed coldly. "And the Puppeteer... framed it as a way of welcoming her into the Outcasts."

"I see..." Soren muttered, realizing the half-elf must have suffered some kind of cruel treatment from the elves. And this must have been their way of helping her get revenge. But... "What about the competition, then?"

"Well, as for that ridiculous show," Lord Asad explained. "It was their young master Lucent’s idea. It seems like he found out about their plan and offered to act as a distraction. That whole performance in the arena was meant to keep everyone’s attention on him while the real plan moved in the shadows.

"Hmm..." Soren nodded as he listened. However, if he had to guess, Lucent probably did that because he wanted to, since he seemed to love cooking. He must have framed it as a distraction to convince the others, but in truth, he just wanted a stage to show off his skills. The passion Soren had seen in his movements back then wasn’t fake. In fact, it was the one honest thing about him. "Then, I’m glad you managed to stop it before it was too late."

"Right. However, it was many times easier than what you did." Lord Asad chuckled. "Honestly, I am ashamed of myself for being unable to fight despite being the lord of the city and an Emperor. While you, Commander Ervin, and others were risking your lives in the arena, I could only run around giving orders."

"Don’t sell yourself short, Sir. Didn’t you manage to catch the hidden enemy and uncover their real plan? Besides, there had to be someone to organize the city’s defense and keep order while the rest of us were fighting. If not for you, the chaos would have spread far beyond the arena."
Soren knew the live broadcast was shut down before he initiated the plan, and the citizens were protected.
"You really know how to put things into perspective, Mr. Everly." Lord Asad chuckled as some of the guilt eased from his face. "I suppose we all played our part."
"That’s right." Soren nodded and, after a pause, asked. "Sir, what will happen now? I mean, what are you planning to do with them?"

Lord Asad’s expression grew serious again. "The Outcasts will be handed over to the Empire. They’ll face trial for their crimes, though I doubt they’ll see anything but execution." He paused. "As for Lucent... that’s more complicated. After all, his father is the leader of the Outcasts and a powerful Sovereign."

As much as they hate to admit it, Lucent’s background made him a valuable hostage. Executing him outright could provoke his father into a full-scale war, and the Empire wasn’t ready for that kind of conflict. On the other hand, letting him go was out of the question. That means...
"They’ll use him as leverage?

"Most likely." Lord Asad nodded grimly. "The Empire will want to negotiate first. Use him to force his father to the table, or at least buy time while they decide their next move." He let out a heavy sigh. "It’s not ideal, but it’s the reality of politics."
"What about the half-elf you caught?" Soren asked curiously.

"Hmm... I am not sure about her either." Lord Asad muttered, rubbing his chin. "But I think the elves will try to negotiate to take her back. A half-elf from their side involved in a plot against the Empire is a delicate matter. If the Empire punishes her too harshly, it could strain relations just as the Outcasts intended. But if the elves take her and sweep it under the rug, it might look like they’re protecting a criminal."
He sighed. "Either way, she’s become a political piece now. Her fate will be decided by people far above my station."
"However, you don’t have to worry about them." Lord Asad spoke in a reassuring tone. "They will all get the punishment they deserve."
"I hope so." Soren nodded with a smile.

"And you will be rewarded accordingly!" Lord Asad grinned. "Even if the other parties drag their feet, I will personally see to it that you’re honored for what you’ve done." His grin widened, pride evident in his eyes. "After all, you’ve truly become Bagdad’s Savior today!"
"About that..." Soren rubbed the back of his neck. "I have a request, if you don’t mind."
"Please, tell me. I will do everything in my power to grant it."

chapters.title: Chapter 307: Hidden Enemy
paragraphs: "I’d like to keep my name out of it as much as possible," Soren said with a serious expression. "The competition already drew enough attention, and I don’t want to be paraded around as some kind of hero. If possible, take all the credit yourself or give it to Commander Ervin and others."

He paused, thinking for a moment. "Also, please announce that I was seriously injured during the incident and will need three or four months to recover. That should explain why I’ll be staying out of the public eye."
Then, as if remembering, he added, "Right, and I’ll officially forfeit from the competition as well. The injury excuse should cover that too, so it won’t look strange."

Lord Asad blinked repeatedly, clearly caught off-guard. "W-Why? You were the one who defeated the Outcasts! You practically won the championship too! If you’re worried about the danger, I can assure you we’ve inc-"

"It’s not about the danger," Soren cut him off gently. "Well, partly it is. But mostly, it’s due to personal reasons. I was going to leave yesterday anyway if all this hadn’t happened, you know. So this outcome doesn’t change much for me." He paused, offering a small shrug. "I just want to go back to a quiet life with my wife."

"S-Still..." Lord Asad struggled for words, clearly not expecting this. Almost anyone else would have jumped at the chance to be hailed as a hero, to claim glory and rewards, to have their name carved into the city’s history. Yet here was the man who had fought harder than anyone and contributed the most to their victory, and all he wanted was to be erased from the story.
It was both baffling and admirable.
’But I guess that is also why he’s in a disguise...’ The pieces clicked into place as he studied the man before him. ’He must have planned this before meeting me.’
"Then... don’t reject the rewards, at least." Lord Asad sighed. "I understand wanting to keep a low profile, but there’s no harm in accepting a private token of gratitude."
"...In that case, can I ask for something myself?" Soren said after pretending to think it over for a moment.
Lord Asad’s expression brightened. "Of course! Name it. As long as it’s within my power, I’ll grant it without question."

"Then... I’d like to receive some magic ingredients," Soren said. "There are a few rare ones I’ve been looking for everywhere but couldn’t find. I understand they’re hard to come by, but with the city’s resources, maybe it’s possible?"

Lord Asad nodded readily. "I’ll see what I can do. Once you give me the names, I’ll have my men search every corner of the city. If they can be found, they’ll be delivered to you." He looked at Soren expectantly. "Is there anything else?"
Soren paused for a moment. "I’d also like to use the teleportation gate without any trouble. We will be leaving soon, so I’d rather avoid unnecessary complications."

"R-Right, you have to leave soon..." Lord Asad trailed off as if in deep thought. "Can you tell me when you’re planning to depart? I’ll make the necessary arrangements in advance so you won’t have to wait.
"This evening," Soren answered. "Around 7 pm."

"Alright, consider it done." Lord Asad nodded firmly. "I’ll have everything prepared and make sure the gate is ready for you by then." He paused, then added, "I’ll also assign someone to escort you, so there won’t be any delays or unwanted attention."
"Thank you for your help, Sir." Soren smiled. "I’ll put together the list of ingredients and have it sent to you as soon as possible."

"Good." Lord Asad reached into his pocket and pulled out a card, handing it to Soren. "You can send the list to this number. If anything else comes up before you leave, feel free to reach me there as well."
Soren accepted the card, glanced at the number, and slipped it into his pocket. "Got it. See you later then."
He turned to leave.
"Ah, wait." Lord Asad’s voice stopped him. "One more thing."
"Hmm?" Soren looked back in confusion.

"The elves have been searching for you too. Especially Chef Nuelia. She asked me to notify her the moment I found you." Lord Asad explained. "She said she wanted to thank you personally for everything you did. She looked really anxious too. So I suggest meeting her before you leave. It might help put her at ease."
Soren thought for a moment, then nodded. "Alright. I’ll make some time before we depart. Thank you for letting me know, Sir."
"Of course. Take care, Mr. Everly.
"You too, Sir."
With that, the two parted ways.
As he walked, Soren reached out to Malakor. ’The half-elf is called Monie, right? Can you tell me what you learned about her?’

’Yes.’ Malakor replied after a moment. ’She is actually a relative of Nuelia, but... her story is a tragic one. Her mother was an elf noble who was promised to another, but she ran away with a human man. When she returned, she was already pregnant with Monie.’
’...’ Soren listened silently, thinking his earlier guess might have been correct.

’The scandal brought shame to the family. Monie’s mother was confined, and when Monie was born, they treated her as an outsider in her own house. Most of the elves saw her as nothing more than a mistake, and... they made sure she knew it every single day.’
’...I see. But how did she end up in this situation?’ Soren asked curiously.

’She ran away from her home a year ago, and after hearing about the Outcasts, she sought them out. It was Sevihan who found her first. He was also the one who gave her a place to belong, a purpose, and in return, she became one of his pawns.’
’...Willingly?’

’...Yes, she wanted to take revenge on the elves who made her life a living hell. So she did everything she was asked to, including giving all the information she knew about the elves. She was the biggest reason why they could kidnap Nuelia so easily.’
’You mean...’
’She played the role of a hostage and tricked Nuelia into surrendering. Nuelia was one of the only elves who treated her kindly, and she used that kindness against her.’
’...It makes sense now.’ Soren muttered, recalling how Nuelia reacted when Monie’s name came up. She must have realized then that she had been betrayed. ’...Where is she now?’

chapters.title: Chapter 308: Forgiveness
paragraphs: "Mr. Soren?"
"Yes, it’s me." Soren nodded as Nuelia turned around to face him. Her eyes widened for a moment before relief flooded her expression. "I heard you were looking for me."

"Y-Yes!" Nuelia nodded enthusiastically. "I was so worried when you suddenly disappeared. Your state was... really bad. You had so much blood and so many injuries on you." Her voice trembled as she spoke. "Are you alright now?"
She didn’t wait for an answer and quickly pulled out a few vials, extending them to him.
"Please, drink these. They will help with your recovery."
Soren looked at the bottles, then back at her anxious expression. "Thank you, but I’m really fine now. I’ve already been treated." He paused. "Still, I appreciate the thought."

"P-Please, just take it," Nuelia insisted, pushing the bottle closer. "It will also help restore the vitality you lost during the fight. Even if you’re healed, your body still needs to recover its strength."
Soren let out a soft sigh. There was no winning against that earnest look. He reached out and accepted the bottle. "Alright. Thank you."
The moment he took it, Nuelia lowered her head and bowed deeply.
"I’m sorry."
Soren blinked. "What for?"

"For everything," she said, her voice shaking. "Because of me, you and your wife were dragged into this. If I had been more careful... if I hadn’t been so naive... none of this would have happened." She kept her head down, her hands clenched at her sides. "I put you in danger. I put everyone in danger. And I... I don’t know how to make up for that."
"..." Soren looked at her, realizing the betrayal must have cut deeper than she was letting show. "...I accept your apology, so please raise your head.
Nuelia hesitated before slowly straightening. Her eyes were glossy, but she held back the tears.

Soren met her gaze. "But you really didn’t need to apologize, Miss Nuelia. You didn’t do anything wrong." His voice softened. "If anyone should apologize, it’s your subordinates who attacked us without confirming the situation first. And of course, the Outcasts who caused all of this."
"!" Nuelia froze. ’I... I almost forgot about that!’

"U-Umm... I... I apologize for that too!" She shouted as she bowed deeply once more, her eyes squeezed shut in shame. "I-I heard everything earlier and have already scolded them for it! They should never have done that. It was reckless and rude, and they had no right to treat you and your wife that way."
She kept her head lowered, her voice growing smaller. "I know an apology from me won’t erase what happened, but I promise I’ll make sure they reflect on their actions properly."

"...I’m sorry, but I can’t forgive them," Soren replied coldly, making Nuelia’s heart sink. "They didn’t just threaten me. They pointed their blades at my wife and said things they had no right to say." He paused, his tone darkening even further. "Furthermore, they never bothered to apologize themselves. Despite the time that had passed since the incident, not a single one of them has come forward to admit their mistake... If they can’t even do that, then they don’t deserve forgiveness."
"..." Nuelia’s head lowered even further, her hands still trembling at her sides.

"..." She opened her mouth to defend them, but no word came out. Because she knew he was right. Her people neither apologized nor tried to make amends till now. Even if they did later, it would only be because she forced them to, not because they truly understood what they had done wrong.
That thought made her chest tighten with a mixture of shame and frustration.
"I... I’m... really sorry..."
"...Sigh." Soren let out a long breath, his cold expression softening just a little. "Don’t think too much about it. I know you’re a good person, and that’s enough for me."
He paused, studying her for a moment before continuing. "As for the others, let’s just consider this matter closed. I won’t hold a grudge against all elves because of a few fools."
Then his tone turned more serious. "But even if it might sound presumptuous of me, since I’m an outsider, I’d still advise you to teach them properly. Or... replace them entirely if necessary.
Nuelia looked up at him in surprise.

"Not everyone is as patient as I am," Soren explained, meeting her gaze evenly. "If they offend the wrong person, the consequences won’t be so light. They might even end up staining the reputation of the whole elven race, or worse... get themselves and you killed."

Nuelia’s breath hitched, her fingers curling into fists. She knew he wasn’t saying it to scare her or insult them. He was saying it out of concern for her and perhaps for the elves. And that made the weight of his words sink even deeper.

She took a deep breath and forced herself to calm down. "Thank you. I will keep everything you said in my mind. And..." She paused as she straightened her posture, and though the guilt still lingered in her eyes, there was a resolve in them now. "I will make sure they receive the punishment they deserve."
Soren didn’t comment on it and just smiled.

"...However," Noelia added after hesitating for a moment. "I still don’t feel right leaving things like this. You and your wife went through so much because of me, and I haven’t done anything to repay you."
"I told you-" Before Soren could finish his words, her eyes lit up, and she quickly pulled something out from her ring. It was an intricately carved wooden pendant.

"Please, take this," she said, holding it out to him. "It’s an artifact that can protect the wearer from spirits. It’s not as powerful as some of the greater relics, but it can block up to three attacks from a Spirit King. It should give one enough time to escape or counterattack."
She pressed it into his hand before he could even think of refusing. Not that he would, considering its nature and how much time he had been looking for such an item.
"...I know it’s not much compared to what you’ve done, but I hope it can be some help to you or your wife in the future." Nuelia finished, her hands clasped in front of her.
"..." Soren looked at the pendant in his hand, quickly analyzing it. He then looked up at her and nodded. "Then I will gratefully accept it."
"!" Nuelia’s eyes lit up, her expression brightening in an instant. "Thank you!"

"Thank you, but I’m really fine now.
I’ve already been treated." He paused.
"Still, I appreciate the thought."
"P-Please, just take it," Nuelia insisted, pushing the bottle closer.
"It will also help restore the vitality you lost during the fight.
Even if you’re healed, your body still needs to recover its strength."
Soren let out a soft sigh.
There was no winning against that earnest look.
He reached out and accepted the bottle.
"Alright.
Thank you."
The moment he took it, Nuelia lowered her head and bowed deeply.
"I’m sorry."
Soren blinked.
"What for?"
"For everything," she said, her voice shaking.
"Because of me, you and your wife were dragged into this.
If I had been more careful... if I hadn’t been so naive... none of this would have happened." She kept her head down, her hands clenched at her sides.
"I put you in danger.
I put everyone in danger.
And I...
I don’t know how to make up for that."
"..." Soren looked at her, realizing the betrayal must have cut deeper than she was letting show.
"...I accept your apology, so please raise your head.
Nuelia hesitated before slowly straightening.
Her eyes were glossy, but she held back the tears.
Soren met her gaze.
"But you really didn’t need to apologize, Miss Nuelia.
You didn’t do anything wrong." His voice softened.
"If anyone should apologize, it’s your subordinates who attacked us without confirming the situation first.
And of course, the Outcasts who caused all of this."
"!" Nuelia froze. ’I...
I almost forgot about that!’
"U-Umm...
I apologize for that too!" She shouted as she bowed deeply once more, her eyes squeezed shut in shame.
"I-I heard everything earlier and have already scolded them for it!
They should never have done that.
It was reckless and rude, and they had no right to treat you and your wife that way."
She kept her head lowered, her voice growing smaller.
"I know an apology from me won’t erase what happened, but I promise I’ll make sure they reflect on their actions properly."
"...I’m sorry, but I can’t forgive them," Soren replied coldly, making Nuelia’s heart sink.
"They didn’t just threaten me.
They pointed their blades at my wife and said things they had no right to say." He paused, his tone darkening even further.
"Furthermore, they never bothered to apologize themselves.
Despite the time that had passed since the incident, not a single one of them has come forward to admit their mistake...
If they can’t even do that, then they don’t deserve forgiveness."
"..." Nuelia’s head lowered even further, her hands still trembling at her sides.
"..." She opened her mouth to defend them, but no word came out.
Because she knew he was right.
Her people neither apologized nor tried to make amends till now.
Even if they did later, it would only be because she forced them to, not because they truly understood what they had done wrong.
That thought made her chest tighten with a mixture of shame and frustration.
I’m... really sorry..."
"...Sigh." Soren let out a long breath, his cold expression softening just a little.
"Don’t think too much about it.
I know you’re a good person, and that’s enough for me."
He paused, studying her for a moment before continuing.
"As for the others, let’s just consider this matter closed.
I won’t hold a grudge against all elves because of a few fools."
Then his tone turned more serious.
"But even if it might sound presumptuous of me, since I’m an outsider, I’d still advise you to teach them properly.
Or... replace them entirely if necessary.
Nuelia looked up at him in surprise.
"Not everyone is as patient as I am," Soren explained, meeting her gaze evenly.
"If they offend the wrong person, the consequences won’t be so light.
They might even end up staining the reputation of the whole elven race, or worse... get themselves and you killed."
Nuelia’s breath hitched, her fingers curling into fists.
She knew he wasn’t saying it to scare her or insult them.
He was saying it out of concern for her and perhaps for the elves.
And that made the weight of his words sink even deeper.
She took a deep breath and forced herself to calm down.
"Thank you.
I will keep everything you said in my mind.
And..." She paused as she straightened her posture, and though the guilt still lingered in her eyes, there was a resolve in them now.
"I will make sure they receive the punishment they deserve."
Soren didn’t comment on it and just smiled.
"...However," Noelia added after hesitating for a moment.
"I still don’t feel right leaving things like this.
You and your wife went through so much because of me, and I haven’t done anything to repay you."
"I told you-" Before Soren could finish his words, her eyes lit up, and she quickly pulled something out from her ring.
It was an intricately carved wooden pendant.
"Please, take this," she said, holding it out to him.
"It’s an artifact that can protect the wearer from spirits.
It’s not as powerful as some of the greater relics, but it can block up to three attacks from a Spirit King.
It should give one enough time to escape or counterattack."
She pressed it into his hand before he could even think of refusing.
Not that he would, considering its nature and how much time he had been looking for such an item.
"...I know it’s not much compared to what you’ve done, but I hope it can be some help to you or your wife in the future." Nuelia finished, her hands clasped in front of her.
"..." Soren looked at the pendant in his hand, quickly analyzing it.
He then looked up at her and nodded.
"Then I will gratefully accept it."
"!" Nuelia’s eyes lit up, her expression brightening in an instant.
"Thank you!"

chapters.title: Chapter 309: Soft-Hearted
paragraphs: ’...He definitely is a trustworthy person. You did a good thing befriending him, Nue.’ A voice echoed in Nuelia’s mind as she watched Soren go. ’Although I think it would have been even better if you had invited him to visit your house.’
’...I thought about it, but I didn’t want to come off as too forward,’ Nuelia replied, a hint of regret evident in her tone. ’He would probably have refused it anyway.’
’True, but it’s more about the intention. It shows your sincerity and leaves the door open for the future.’ The voice explained gently. ’And I have a feeling this won’t be the last time we see him.’
’Huh? What do you mean?’ Nuelia asked in confusion. ’Aren’t we gonna meet in the real finals?’

’Sigh... Didn’t you realize it yet? He is leaving the city, which means he won’t be participating in the competition anymore. As for what I exactly meant...’ The voice paused. ’...You’ll understand it when the time comes.’
’...You’re saying I’m too stupid to understand it right now, right?!’ Nuelia realized and pouted at the voice.
’...’ The voice stayed silent, which was also kind of an answer.

’Urgh!’ Nuelia became irritated, but as she recalled what she experienced in the past two days, her expression became downcast. ’Yeah... I’m stupid... I... I trusted the wrong person and almost got everyone killed because of it.’ Her voice trembled as the weight of her mistake pressed down on her again. ’If it weren’t for Mr. Soren and the others, I don’t even want to think about what would have happened...’

’Everyone makes mistakes, Nue,’ The voice said gently. ’What matters is that you learn from them so you won’t make the same ones again. Be kind, but don’t let that kindness blind you. Trust, but don’t give it away too easily. That’s how you protect yourself and the people who rely on you.’
Nuelia remained quiet for a moment, letting the words settle in her heart. Then she nodded slowly. ’You’re right... I won’t let something like this happen again.’
’That’s more like it.’ The voice said. ’But what do you plan to do next?’
’I’ll contact Grandpa and report everything that happened here,’ Nuelia replied. ’And... I think I’ll forfeit from the competition too.’
’Oh? Why is that?’

Nuelia hesitated for a moment before answering. ’I already lost earlier, even if the situation was different. And...’ She paused, her voice growing quieter. ’I don’t want to continue if Mr. Soren isn’t participating. It just doesn’t feel right anymore.’
’...’ The voice let out a soft hum. ’I see... It’s your decision. Just make sure you’re doing it for yourself, and not because you feel guilty.’
’I know.’ Nuelia said. ’But this is what I want. Besides, I have more important things to deal with now.’
’Like what?’

Nuelia’s expression firmed. ’Like making sure our people understand what they did and learn from their mistakes. And making sure Monie...’ She trailed off, her voice faltering. ’...Making sure she faces justice. But also... I want to know why. Why she did this to me.’
’Do you think she’ll tell you?’
’...I don’t know.’ Nuelia admitted quietly. ’But I have to try. She was almost like a sister to me. If there was even a small part of her that cared, I need to hear it from her own mouth.’
The voice was silent for a long moment. ’Then go. But prepare yourself, Nuelia. The truth might not be what you want to hear.’
’I know.’ Nuelia took a deep breath and stood up straighter. ’But I can’t run away from it. Not anymore.’
With that, she turned and started walking. Whatever answers waited for her, she was ready to face them. She hoped so, at least...
’Master, can I ask you something?’ Malakor asked as Soren sat down at a small table near the window of a quiet cafe.
’Sure.’ Soren asked as he opened his phone. He wanted to write and send the list to the City Lord before going back to pick up Ethea. ’What is it?’

’Why didn’t you ask for better rewards?’ Malakor said, his tone curious. ’I am certain that she would have given you anything you asked for without a second thought. You could have used that to get the recipes you wanted or another useful treasure.’
Soren’s fingers paused over the screen. He glanced at the table where two items rested along with the ice cream he purchased.

One was the wooden pendant Nuelia gifted him, and the other was a thick, leather-bound book with elven script embossed on its cover. It was a book about spirits, and Soren managed to get it from her after their conversation drifted from the pendant to the nature of spirits themselves.

When the topic shifted, Soren seized the opportunity, voiced his interest in learning more, and asked if she had any books on the subject, even basic ones. He’d been ready to buy or trade, but Nuelia had refused any form of payment, insisting he take it as a gift instead. In the end, he accepted, but he gifted a recipe to her in return.
’As you can see, I already got what I wanted,’ Soren replied, his gaze shifting between the pendant and the book. ’Asking for more would have been taking advantage of her gratitude.’
’I see...’ Malakor trailed off, his thoughts turning inward. ’I must have forgotten what kind of person he is.’
In his opinion, Soren was smart but also a fool. No, not exactly a fool. He was too sharp for that.
’Perhaps ’soft-hearted’ is a better word...’
A man who could have seized far greater rewards yet chose not to, all because of something as intangible as principles.
’Well, at least he’s not entirely refusing to accept rewards. He... just prefers to gain them on his own terms. Yeah...’

That thought settled better. Soren wasn’t naive. He simply valued different currencies than most. Trust, goodwill, and genuine connections had their own worth, and in the long run, they often yielded far more than gold or treasures. Malakor could respect that, even if he would have handled things differently himself.
’Still... if he ever wavers, I’ll be there to make sure we don’t lose out too much.’ A sly glint passed through Malakor’s consciousness. ’That’s my ’role’, after all.’
’To be his shield and his shadow. To do what he cannot bring himself to do...’

chapters.title: Chapter 310: Investment detected... [1]
paragraphs: With Malakor going silent, Soren continued to write the list. He made sure not to go overboard and write things he really needed. Just as he finished and hit the send button, a familiar sound echoed in his mind, along with a series of messages.
Soren’s eyes lit up, but since he was expecting it, he managed to control his expression. He adjusted his position so it would still look like he was using his phone and started reading.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Nuelia vue Althara]
[Analyzing Investment...]

[Investment: You played a pivotal role in the target’s rescue and survival during a high-risk abduction crisis. You also gave her an elixir and guided her through critical moments of the competition, teaching her the fundamentals of cooking with open fire and without reliance on mana. Additionally, you advised her on her people’s discipline and conduct, helping her recognize their flaws and the importance of accountability.]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target survived a life-threatening crisis and has regained a sense of stability following the traumatic events. She has developed genuine respect and trust in you, seeing you as both a mentor and a dependable figure. Your guidance has sparked a new awareness within her, igniting her desire to become more self-reliant and to lead her people with greater wisdom and strength. Her gratitude and admiration have deepened considerably.]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: SUPREME]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Sovereign Vitality Elixir x3]
[2. Ability Evolution: Life Force Resonance (B-Rank) -> Vital Harmony (A-Rank)]
[3. Ability Evolution: Perceptive Eyes (C-Rank) -> Nature’s Eyes (B-Rank)]
[4. Cooking Mastery +1]
[5. Life Force Restoration Soup Recipe]
[6. Basic Elven Culinary Book]
[Integration initiated...]
Soren tapped as soon as the integration started.
Perhaps he was already in the 4th circle and had just broken through to the 3rd stage in his mental cultivation; he didn’t feel any discomfort. Or perhaps he had long become used to the sensation.
Either way, the process passed smoothly, and within moments, the notification message appeared.
[Integration complete!]
"Huff..."

Soren let out a long breath as he felt the changes settle into his body and mind. The world around him seemed clearer now, alive in a way that was hard to describe. His senses stretched easily, encompassing almost the whole street in a moment. He could also pick up faint pulses of life energy from nearby plants and people.
’This must be the new effect of the evolved Nature’s Eyes ability.’ Soren guessed as he played a bit more before deactivating it.

In short, this ability now granted him superior eyesight and night vision, and it further strengthened his existing ability to sense emotional baselines and sincerity. The new effect he’d just used was called Life Sense, and it let him perceive the flow of life energy around him. With it, he could detect living beings within a certain range and even gauge their general condition without needing to see them directly.
’This was definitely a good evolution.’ Soren thought as he barely stopped himself from grinning. ’It is much easier to sense malicious intent as well.’
He was more than satisfied with the returns he got from this investment.
’I got two extra for using one elixir on her. And improved my cooking knowledge, got a new recipe, and another elven book.’

However, the best return he got from this investment was undoubtedly the newly evolved Vital Harmony ability. Previously, Life Force Resonance had improved his stamina, accelerated his natural recovery, and continuously strengthened his overall life force. But now, those effects had grown significantly, and on top of that, it came with a new effect called Life’s Resonance.

It granted him an affinity to life force energy itself. He could now draw on ambient life energy and manipulate it to a certain extent. It also improved his recovery in natural environments and increased the effectiveness of any life force related skills, spells, or techniques he used.
’More importantly, I can easily learn and cook those life force-related dishes now!’
Fortunately, he wouldn’t have to ask Nuelia for another recipe, since he had already gotten one yesterday and one just now.
’All I need is time and practice.’
He knew he wouldn’t be able to succeed the first time, especially given the fact that he had yet to learn how to control his new affinity.
’...Come to think of it, I’ve received two affinities from returns so far, although one was indirect. But does that mean I can ’awaken’ even more affinities, or even upgrade or evolve them?’
That must definitely be possible; however, he would probably have to make the right investment and meet the conditions, if there were any.
’Let’s check my status while we’re at it...’
He hummed inwardly and summoned his status after closing the investment messages.

chapters.title: Chapter 311: Investment detected... [2]
paragraphs: Soren scanned his status and stopped at the mental power line.
’Hmm... I gained almost twenty thousand mental power after breaking through to the Soul-Tempered Core Stage... That’s pretty good.’

However, he knew the reason too. It was probably related to how he broke through and how long he had been stuck at the peak of the Intent Foundation Stage. Either way, he was satisfied with the improvement.
’Although I wonder what happens when Ethea breaks through this time...’
Since he was the first to advance, would he receive something else in return? Like some amount of mental power?
With a few theories in mind, he continued his inspection, stopped at affinities, and saw that Life Force affinity was already added, and as a B Rank at that.
’Although it’s a tier lower than Vital Harmony itself, B Rank affinity is still high, especially given how rare it is.’
Well, at least among humans.
’Anyway, let’s see how many investments are ongoing...’
He scrolled to the bottom of the screen and opened the Ongoing Investments tab.
’Oh... There are five of them!’
One was for Princess Roya, two were for Ethea, another was for Sister Zoe, and finally one for...
’...Bagdad City?’ Soren paused as he stared at the words. ’...It really is Bagdad City.’ He thought to himself as he re-read it a few more times. ’But does that mean... I can invest in cities?’

No matter how you looked at it, it sounded strange. However, based on what he had learned about investing so far, an investment was supposed to be about putting something of value into a person, a cause, or a venture with the expectation of future returns.

His Authority had always applied that principle to people and bonds, but there was no reason it couldn’t extend to something larger. A city was more than just walls and roads. It was its people, their livelihoods, and their future. If he had invested his strength and effort into protecting all of that, then perhaps the Authority simply recognized the city as a collective whole rather than listing every individual separately.
’That would make sense,’ he thought. ’It’s not the buildings I invested in. It’s everyone inside them... But if so, I wonder what type of returns I will get.’

He thought about it for a moment and decided not to waste time overthinking it. The Authority had never let him down before, and whatever came from this investment would reveal itself when the time was right. He just had to wait, probably not for long, though.

His gaze shifted back to the two investments under Ethea’s name. One of them had been ongoing since they departed from Kalmira. While the other was added today. This was the second time he had two separate investments running for the same target at once.
’I wonder if they’ll merge this time, or if they’ll be calculated separately...’ He mused for a moment before shaking his head. ’Well, no use thinking about it now.’
Just as he closed the status window, Malakor’s voice echoed in his mind. ’Master, Lady Ethea has finished talking with the princess.’
’Alright. Let me finish this first.’ Soren set his phone down and picked up his ice cream, taking a few slow bites as he let the day’s tension ease just a little.
[Ding!]
The familiar sound made him pause mid-bite, and a new set of messages appeared in his vision.
[Investment detected...]
[Analyzing Investment...]
[Target: Roya Sol-Temur]

[Investment: You cooperated in the target’s rescue, playing a major role in freeing her from the enemy’s control once and for all. You aided in her mental recovery, helping stabilize her mind after the ordeal. Your actions also helped resolve the incident, indirectly assisting the target in completing her mission and preventing further political fallout between the Empire and the elves.]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target was safely rescued and has expressed deep gratitude toward you and your wife. She had previously viewed you as unworthy of your wife, but after learning the truth of what you did, her perception has completely shifted. She now regards you with the highest respect and feels deeply indebted to you, as well as ashamed for having looked down on you before.]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: SUPREME]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Mental Power +30,000]
[2. Sovereign’s Clarity Elixir x3]
[3. Ability Evolution: Intimidation (B-Rank) -> Overlord’s Aura (A-Rank)]
[4. Knowledge Unlocked: Basic Imperial Etiquette]
[Integration initiated...]
[Integration complete!]

’...Tasty.’ Soren took another slow bite of his ice cream, savoring the cool sweetness as it melted on his tongue. He then adjusted his posture, straightening his back and shifting his grip on the spoon to match the etiquette knowledge now present in his mind. His movements became more refined, more composed, and for a moment, he looked like someone born into true nobility.
He glanced at his reflection in the window and nodded slightly. ’Not bad... but not my style either.’

He preferred to be free and relaxed, not stiff like those nobles who spent half their lives worrying about appearances. Still, the knowledge wasn’t useless. There would come a time when he’d need to act the part, and when that day came, he wouldn’t have to waste time to learn it.

Loosening his shoulders, he returned to eating normally and finished the rest of his ice cream. The mental power boost and the elixirs were good returns. Unfortunately, only Intimidation had evolved this time, but he wasn’t disappointed. The new effect it came with was called Aura Suppression. It allowed him to consciously suppress or release his aura at will. When released, it pressed down on those around him, making it easier to control a room or force weaker opponents to hesitate. When suppressed, it made him nearly unnoticeable, allowing him to move without drawing unwanted attention.
’Not bad,’ he thought with a small smile. ’I can think of a few ways to use this.’
It especially made a good combination with Pebble Among the Stars.
’It will be even more amazing if I learn a concealment type of ability or spell...’

However, now was not the time to get lost in theory. He paid for his ice cream and bought a few more for take back with him. The cool evening air greeted him as he stepped out of the cafe, the streets already beginning to settle after the chaos of the day.
’Let’s go pick up Ethea and prepare to leave.’
