chapters.title: Chapter 312: Two Hearts, One Step Closer
paragraphs: With Malakor’s help, Soren arrived back in front of the secret room. Knight Aya was standing guard outside. He greeted her, and once Ethea opened the room, he entered.

As soon as he stepped inside, Princess Roya rose from her seat and bowed her head slightly. "Mr. Soren... I want to thank you for everything you’ve done. And... I owe you an apology as well. I misjudged you before, and I’m ashamed of it."

Soren blinked, as if confused by her words. "Apology? I’m not sure what you mean, Your Highness." He offered a polite nod, putting the etiquette he had just learned into use. "But I accept your thanks. I’m glad you’re safe."
Roya opened her mouth as if to say more, but Soren had already turned to Ethea with a gentle smile. "Shall we take our leave, dear?"
Ethea smiled back and nodded.
"Please excuse us," Soren said to the princess.
"...Take care. I hope we’ll meet again."
After getting a reluctant farewell from the princess, Soren stepped behind Ethea’s wheelchair and wheeled her out of the room.
As they walked back into a corridor with no one else, Malakor teleported them back to their room, saving them the hassle of walking around.

Then, Soren helped Ethea with her afternoon routine. By the time they were done, the room was enveloped in a sweet aroma. He settled her back into her wheelchair near the small dining table and began drying her damp hair with a towel.
"Are you hungry?" He asked softly.
Ethea took a moment to answer. "Not much. But I can eat a little."
Soren smiled. "Then let’s have something light."
’And I’ll tell you everything while we are at it,’ he added inwardly.
’Actually...’ Soren started by sharing his full plan with her and how it went while Ethea listened silently.

From the beginning, he had left Malakor outside the arena, hidden in the shadows since he knew he wouldn’t be much of use in Nullifier’s anti-mana zone. His task was to watch over the entire city and its people, searching for any sign of the Puppeteer’s real body while Soren and the others kept the Puppeteer and other Outcast members distracted. Since Malakor could move unseen and sense things beyond normal perception, he was the perfect counter to an enemy who relied on misdirection.

Soren had also predicted that the Puppeteer would come for Ethea. After yesterday’s clash and their shared history, it was clear he saw her as both a threat and an obsession. That was why Soren had wanted her to remain in the secret room. But Ethea had understood the risk and still chose to join the plan. If the Puppeteer came for her, she would hold him there, trapping his consciousness long enough for Soren and Malakor to act.
Soren also asked Malakor to secretly protect Ethea and watch out for other suspicious people. After all, as Ethea said, there might have been more members of the Outcasts.

Fortunately, it had worked. The Puppeteer not only underestimated Soren but also Malakor, dismissing him as nothing more than a normal magic beast. He had no idea of his mental and phantom nature, and that single mistake had cost him everything. The countless barriers and traps he made to protect his real body were no threat to Malakor. He was Kalmira’s Nightmare after all.

As for the Hollow Pair, Soren had intended to provoke them and lower their guard after learning their personalities and fighting styles from Ethea. By fighting recklessly and taking hits, he made himself seem weaker than he actually was. Then, when they least expected it, he struck back.
That plan had also worked.

The Leech had been easy to provoke, his pride making him sloppy and quick to anger. It didn’t take much for Soren to push him into losing his cool, which only made him more predictable. But the Nullifier had been a lot more difficult since he was far more level-headed than his partner, and no matter how much Soren baited him, he refused to lose focus. Only after being beaten to the brink did Soren manage to create the opening he needed.
And it had nearly cost him his life. If he hadn’t used Limit Breaker and stacked Amplification on top of it, he wouldn’t have been able to defeat him.

Once he finished explaining everything, Ethea let out a slow breath. Although she had already figured out most of his strategy during the battle, hearing the full picture from him made her realize just how much he had gambled.
"Your plan was solid, and you executed it well. But next time... please make a plan that doesn’t involve you almost dying."
Soren scratched the back of his head like a guilty child. "I’ll do my best."

Ethea’s expression softened into a gentle smile. "Good. Because I don’t want to go through that again." She paused, then added, "But thank you. You saved so many people and also helped me take care of one of my old enemies... and you gave me a chance to be part of it. That meant a lot to me."
Soren chuckled. "You did an amazing job too. If it weren’t for your timely attack, Sevihan might have slipped away before we could reach him. You’re the reason he couldn’t escape in the end."
"I guess we make a good team then?" Ethea laughed softly.
Soren grinned. "The best."
Ethea’s smile lingered for a moment before she tilted her head. "By the way... what did you do after you left earlier? You didn’t get bored waiting for us, did you?"
"No, not at all. I took care of a few things while you were talking with the princess," Soren said. "Wanna hear about it?"
Ethea nodded, settling more comfortably on her chair.

Then, Soren told her about his meeting with Lord Asad, his request for privacy, and the arrangements for their departure. He also mentioned meeting Nuelia, her apology, the pendant she had gifted him, and the book he managed to get.
"You did well." Ethea smiled, relieved he spent his time productively and hadn’t been bored waiting around.
"Mm." Soren set the last plate down and sat down. "Fortunately, it all worked out in the end."
"Right..." Ethea replied, pausing as if recalling something. "Dear, I also received something from Her Highness."
"Oh, it must be something useful," Soren guessed, placing the ice cream he’d bought earlier on the table.

Ethea nodded. "It’s a free pass that allows us to travel through the Empire without going through the usual procedures. As long as we show it at any gate or checkpoint, we’ll be allowed through without issue." She paused, a small smile on her lips. "It should make our journey much smoother."
Soren’s eyes lit up in surprise. "That’s more than useful! It saves us a lot of trouble, especially with the teleportation gates."
Ethea hummed in agreement. "She wanted to give more, but I told her this was enough. Besides, she got kidnapped because she sent us help. I couldn’t ask for more after that."

"You made the right choice," Soren said as he helped her eat. "Actually, I talked with her guardian knight too, and had a little talk. She thanked me for helping with the rescue and said the Empire wouldn’t forget what we did. She also agreed to help keep our identities hidden."
"That’s good." Ethea took a small bite of her meal before continuing. "Her Highness also promised to keep our secret. She said she would never reveal who we really are without our permission."
Soren nodded, satisfied. "Then there’s nothing to worry about. With both of them on our side, our identities should stay safe.
"...Have you received any messages from Ryan yet?" Ethea asked a moment later, shifting the conversation.
"Not yet. I plan to contact him once we arrive at our destination. However, according to our last conversation, they will probably arrive at the empire in a few days."
"That’s good then." Ethea sighed in relief. "We still have time to make our preparations."
"True." Soren chuckled. "We will also have time to tour the city. And..." He paused, his expression softening as he met her gaze. "...Let’s go on a date."
Ethea blinked, clearly caught off guard. "A... date?"
Soren nodded, a hint of nervousness in his smile. "We’ve been through so much already. I think we deserve a little more time to just enjoy ourselves. What do you say?"
Ethea stared at him for a moment before a warm smile curved her lips. "I’d like that."
"Good!" Soren’s smile widened, and he leaned back in his chair. "Then it’s settled. We’ll take tomorrow to rest, and the day after, we’ll go out on a date."
Ethea tilted her head slightly. "Do you already have something in mind?"
Soren scratched the back of his neck. "N-Not exactly. But I’ll think of something before then. Leave it to me."
Ethea laughed softly. "I’ll look forward to it."
"Mmm. I promise it’ll be a day you won’t forget." Soren said, meeting her eyes.
’I’ll confess to her then,’ he added inwardly. ’Whatever her answer is, I’ll accept it. But I won’t hide anymore.’
Ethea’s smile softened, and she gave a small nod. "Then I’ll hold you to that."
"Hehe, I’ll definitely do my best."
"..." Ethea smiled and continued eating.

Actually, she already guessed why he even suggested a date. And honestly, she was happy he was taking the lead again. She had wanted to do the same for a while now, but every time she tried, the words would catch in her throat, and she would tell herself it wasn’t the right time.
But after what had almost happened earlier, she knew he felt the same way. There was no more room for doubt. He was preparing to face those feelings, and she would do the same.
Even if he didn’t end up saying what she thought he was going to say, she had already made up her mind.
’...I’ll confess to him. Say that I love him...’

She thanked me for helping with the rescue and said the Empire wouldn’t forget what we did.
She also agreed to help keep our identities hidden."
"That’s good." Ethea took a small bite of her meal before continuing.
"Her Highness also promised to keep our secret.
She said she would never reveal who we really are without our permission."
Soren nodded, satisfied.
"Then there’s nothing to worry about.
With both of them on our side, our identities should stay safe.
"...Have you received any messages from Ryan yet?" Ethea asked a moment later, shifting the conversation.
"Not yet.
I plan to contact him once we arrive at our destination.
However, according to our last conversation, they will probably arrive at the empire in a few days."
"That’s good then." Ethea sighed in relief.
"We still have time to make our preparations."
"True." Soren chuckled.
"We will also have time to tour the city.
And..." He paused, his expression softening as he met her gaze.
"...Let’s go on a date."
Ethea blinked, clearly caught off guard.
"A... date?"
Soren nodded, a hint of nervousness in his smile.
"We’ve been through so much already.
I think we deserve a little more time to just enjoy ourselves.
What do you say?"
Ethea stared at him for a moment before a warm smile curved her lips.
"I’d like that."
"Good!" Soren’s smile widened, and he leaned back in his chair.
"Then it’s settled.
We’ll take tomorrow to rest, and the day after, we’ll go out on a date."
Ethea tilted her head slightly.
"Do you already have something in mind?"
Soren scratched the back of his neck.
"N-Not exactly.
But I’ll think of something before then.
Leave it to me."
Ethea laughed softly.
"I’ll look forward to it."
"Mmm.
I promise it’ll be a day you won’t forget." Soren said, meeting her eyes.
’I’ll confess to her then,’ he added inwardly. ’Whatever her answer is, I’ll accept it.
But I won’t hide anymore.’
Ethea’s smile softened, and she gave a small nod.
"Then I’ll hold you to that."
"Hehe, I’ll definitely do my best."
"..." Ethea smiled and continued eating.
Actually, she already guessed why he even suggested a date.
And honestly, she was happy he was taking the lead again.
She had wanted to do the same for a while now, but every time she tried, the words would catch in her throat, and she would tell herself it wasn’t the right time.
But after what had almost happened earlier, she knew he felt the same way.
There was no more room for doubt.
He was preparing to face those feelings, and she would do the same.
Even if he didn’t end up saying what she thought he was going to say, she had already made up her mind.
’...I’ll confess to him.
Say that I love him...’

chapters.title: Chapter 313: Goodbye Bagdad, Hello Adamery
paragraphs: Soren and Ethea arrived at the Teleportation Gate on time. Surprisingly, the City Lord was already there, with a small group of guards stationed nearby.
"Mr. Everly, Mrs. Everly," He greeted them with a warm smile as they approached. "I’m glad I could see you off personally."
"Lord Asad," Soren and Ethea returned the greeting with polite nods. "Thank you for coming all the way here."

"It’s the least I could do." Asad waved a hand before stepping closer. He reached into his coat and pulled out a simple spatial ring, holding it out to Soren. "Here. Everything you requested is inside, along with a few extra supplies for your journey."
Soren accepted the ring and slipped it on his finger. "Thank you. Truly."

Asad shook his head. "No thanks needed. You saved this city. I should be the one thanking you." He paused, glancing at Ethea with a respectful nod. "Take care on your journey, both of you. And remember, Bagdad will always welcome you with open arms."
Ethea smiled from her wheelchair. "Thank you, Lord Asad."

After a few more words and farewells, Soren bent down and gently lifted Ethea into his arms. Her wheelchair was stored away safely, and with one last nod to Asad, he stepped into the Teleportation Gate. The light flared around them, and in the next moment, they were gone.
"..." Lord Asad continued staring at the portal before turning to his right. "You can come out now, Your Highness."

A moment later, the air where he was looking shimmered, and a figure materialized in front of him. It was Princess Roya, her expression unreadable as she watched the space where Soren and Ethea had just disappeared.

Lord Asad wanted to ask why she hid in the first place and didn’t see them off like him, but knowing her circumstances and the weight of her position, he chose to keep the question to himself. Some farewells were easier from a distance.
"...Let’s go." She muttered after some time, already turning around to leave. "We still have a lot of work to do."
"Yes, Your Highness."
Lord Asad nodded and followed after her.
It seems like the City Lord had already made arrangements on the other side. As soon as Soren and Ethea emerged from the portal, a staff member was waiting to greet them.
"Welcome to Adamery City." The staff member bowed politely. "Are you both feeling alright? No dizziness or discomfort from the teleportation?"
Soren shook his head. "We’re fine. Thank you for asking."
"Glad to hear it." The staff member smiled and motioned toward the counter. "Please proceed to the checkpoint. Your identification will be processed there."
Soren and Ethea moved through the basic procedures smoothly. With their documents in order and Lord Asad’s prior arrangements, the process was quick and without issue.
As they stepped outside, Soren finally got his first real look at the streets of Adamery City.

The city carried a similar energy to Bagdad, but its style was vastly different. The buildings were taller, and their designs reminded him of the ancient architectural style with stone pillars, carved archways, and tiled roofs that curved upward at the edges.

And yet, the modern style was woven into them seamlessly as well. Holographic signs floated beside old-fashioned storefronts, mana-powered lamps lined the streets, and sleek vehicles glided past buildings that looked like they had stood for centuries. Well, they had, but only for over a century. Still, in the current dangerous world, it was a miracle that any structure survived that long without being destroyed by monsters, wars, or the constant march of time.
Soren exhaled slowly as he took it all in. "This place... is really something else.
"This is just the outer district," Ethea said with a small smile. "The inner city is even more impressive. You’ll see it properly when we go to the academy."
Soren chuckled. "Then I’m looking forward to it. For now, let’s head to the hotel and rest."
Ethea nodded. "Let’s go."

With that, they made their way through the streets until they reached their hotel. The check-in process was smooth, and before long, they were in their room. Soren collapsed onto the bed with a long sigh after helping Ethea settle into a comfortable position beside him.
"Goodnight, dear."
Soren whispered as he gently embraced Ethea.
"Goodnight, dear..."

Ethea closed her eyes and leaned into his warmth. The day had been long, but this moment made it all worth it. With his arms wrapped around her and his heartbeat steady beside her, she let herself drift off with a small smile on her lips.

A little over two thousand refined mana without lifting a finger. It wasn’t a massive amount, not compared to what he could earn from a single gate or a day of cultivating, but it was still amazing. If only he could add more Threads, it would be even more rewarding. But for now, he was satisfied.

He dismissed the messages with a thought, and his gaze drifted to the woman beside him. Ethea was still asleep, facing toward him, her breathing soft and even. The soft glow from the window fell across her face, tracing the gentle curve of her jaw and the dark sweep of her lashes.
His lips curled up on their own. ’...Beautiful.’

He then gently tucked a stray strand of hair behind her ear, his touch light so as not to wake her. But even in sleep, she seemed to lean into the warmth of his hand, her expression softening. chapters.title: Chapter 314: Borrowed Time
paragraphs: ’...’ Soren fell silent as he analyzed her status. He was both relieved and worried to see her so close to breaking through. Once it hit the limit, she would break through, and with it would come both opportunity and risk.
But this time, things were different. They had already arrived at their destination, and if something really went wrong, they had Etenia Academy to turn to for help. That eased some of his concern.

Besides, they still had Malakor with them. He might not be as strong as Sir Hector to easily handle a 7th circle Gate, but when it came to escaping or hiding, Malakor’s abilities made their chances of survival almost certain.
And after the last incident, Soren doubted their enemies would try the same trick again so soon.
’We’ll be fine,’ he told himself. ’We just need to be prepared.’
Nodding inwardly, he continued, and his eyes lit up.
’Nice!’ He exclaimed inwardly. Her core condition had recovered by 3%, and her mana pathways had improved by 4%. Her chronic pain was also as low as 3, thanks to Soul-Binding Symbiosis.

Unfortunately, he still wasn’t able to uncover anything else related to the curse. He guessed it would take another Authority Advancement to be able to see more details about it or meet some kind of requirements/conditions. Perhaps he would have to become an Emperor or a Sovereign.
’...Let’s not overthink it.’ He chuckled but paused as he saw the estimated survival time.

It was a good thing he managed to improve and keep it as high as possible. Back when he first appraised her, the range had been eight to fourteen months. About three months had passed since then, and now it stood at nine to ten. As for the one month that was lost, it had likely been because of the incident where she almost died due to the curse’s activation. Even so, the lower estimate had still gone up instead of falling.

That alone was proof that his efforts weren’t wasted. But he also knew it still wasn’t enough. Nine months sounded like a long time, but in reality, it would pass in the blink of an eye. He needed more than borrowed time. He needed a cure. And he wouldn’t stop until he found one.
With a determined expression, he dismissed her status and gently moved to stand up, careful not to wake her. Ethea stirred slightly but didn’t open her eyes, and Soren let out a sigh of relief.

After casting a sound-blocking barrier around her, he made his way to the bathroom. He washed up and changed into fresh clothes. Once he was done, he headed to the small kitchen area of their room and started preparing breakfast, thinking about what to do on their date.
By the time he finished setting up the table, Ethea woke up on her own. She blinked sleepily at the empty space beside her before her gaze drifted toward the source of the noise.
"Good morning," she called out, her voice still laced with sleep.
"Morning." Soren turned and smiled. "Wait a moment. I’ll be done soon."
Ethea smiled back and replied. "Mm..."
Soren sped up, finished in a few minutes, and helped Ethea with her morning routine. Half an hour later, the two of them were sitting side by side in front of the table.
"Lord Asad told me the news would be announced today; let’s see how they reported it." Soren reached for the remote and turned on the TV, switching to a news channel.
Sure enough, the screen was already showing a special report on the Harvest Festival incident. Or more like the Golden Ladle Championship.
"Tragedy at Bagdad’s Harvest Festival: An Evil Plot to Kidnap the Princess!"
"The Harvest Festival Crisis: How a Group of Terrorists Almost Destroyed a City!"
"Bagdad’s Darkest Hour: The Attack That Nearly Sparked a War!"
The headlines flashed across the screen one after another, each more dramatic than the last. Soren and Ethea exchanged a glance as the reporter began explaining the details of what had happened.
"...The media really likes to blow things up." Soren shook his head with a dry smile.

Still, he was relieved. Lord Asad had kept his promise. The reports mentioned the rescue, the villains, and the city’s response, but there was almost no information about him or Ethea. A few vague mentions of "unnamed heroes" and "brave citizens" were all that appeared.
Soren turned back to Ethea and continued eating while listening to the broadcast. So far, everything was going as planned.
"...Is that you?"

Ethea’s voice made him pause. He looked up at the screen and saw the footage playing. It showed the final moments of the live broadcast before it had been cut off. The camera had caught Soren walking toward Lucent with a friendly smile, the handshake, and then the sudden move that brought Lucent to his knees with Soren’s hand around his throat.
The footage ended right there, just as the two hooded figures charged toward him.

The reporter’s voice grew more animated. "...And here we have the moment that changed everything! This is the contestant known as Soren, a chef who stood up and initiated the operation that saved the princess, the elf guest, and the city. Witnesses say he moved so fast that no one even saw it coming. His actions are being credited as the starting point of the entire crisis..."
Soren watched for a moment longer, then let out a small sigh. "Yeah... that’s me."

He knew he couldn’t be entirely erased from the story, especially with concrete proof like this. But seeingthatmoment replayed on TV felt strange. If the reporter hadn’t explained the context, many people would have mistaken him for the villain. Grabbing someone on stage like that, in front of millions of viewers... it didn’t exactly look heroic.
Ethea glanced at him, noticing his slightly awkward expression, and smiled. "You looked cool, though."
Soren blinked, then let out a short laugh. "Thanks."

Then they continued watching. The reporter covered the entire incident as detailed and as interesting as possible. They highlighted Commander Ervin, City Lord Asad, elf Loriel, and a few more people as the key figures who led the defense and rescue efforts. However, they didn’t explicitly mention who exactly defeated the villains.
Soren guessed the City Lord didn’t want anyone specific to take the credit. Even if he wanted to stay hidden, letting someone else claim the credit wouldn’t have sat right with Lord Asad.
’Yeah, that is probably it.’ Soren mused. ’Or... The others must have refused to take credit for something they didn’t do...’

chapters.title: Chapter 315: Shocking News
paragraphs: Soren and Ethea listened in silence as the story unfolded on screen.
And as expected, it was really strange to hear it from an outside perspective. The danger, the chaos, the fear - all of it had already passed, but seeing it again made the memories feel fresh.

"...And so, thanks to the combined efforts of our brave knights, city officials, and a few courageous individuals, what could have been a tragedy beyond measure became a story of survival and hope. Bagdad City remains standing, its people safe, and the perpetrators behind this vile plot have been brought to justice. We express our-!"
The reporter paused, placing a hand over their earpiece before their expression shifted.
"Wait... we are receiving new information related to the incident. We’ll be right back after this short break with more on this developing story."
The screen cut to a commercial break, leaving Soren and Ethea in a brief silence.
"...What do you think it could be?" Soren asked first.
Ethea tilted her head, thinking for a moment. "Probably something about the Outcasts. Or maybe the Empire is making an official statement. Either way, we’ll find out soon."

"Right." Soren nodded with a smile and brought a spoon of cake to her lips. Honestly, he wanted to know about the casualties. Yesterday, when he had gone to testify about Sevihan’s death, he had asked the City Lord about it, but he said they were still calculating, and fortunately, the losses weren’t too high, and most of the damage was limited to the destroyed arena.
But Soren knew there were many injured people, suffering from being controlled, beaten, knocked unconscious, and caught in the chaos. Even if they had survived, the scars would remain.
’Well, at least nobody died this time...’

He knew that might not be the exact truth, that there could be deaths that weren’t reported yet, or people whose injuries were worse than they seemed. But he wanted to believe it was true, that no lives had been lost.
He let out a slow breath and turned his attention back to the table. The two of them continued eating, the TV still playing in the background.
A minute later, the news resumed. The reporter appeared again, his expression more serious than before.

"We have two important updates regarding the Bagdad City incident. First, the Imperial Family has officially issued a statement. They confirmed the safety of both the elven chef and Princess Roya and thanked all those who played a role. And... The captured members of Outcasts will be transferred to the Imperial Capital to stand trial. Due to the severity of their crimes, the Empire has added that the trial will be made public and... at least two of them are expected to receive the death penalty. Their identities have not yet been released to the public, but we suspect it’s the two hooded figures who started the attack during the competition..."
Soren’s expression didn’t change much as he had already talked about it with Lord Asad yesterday. However, he was curious if the other update was something he didn’t know.

"...Now, for our second update," the reporter continued, adjusting his posture. "It’s actually about the Golden Ladle Championship. We have just received a few rather shocking details from the organizers."
He glanced down at his notes before looking at the camera.

"It has been confirmed that the dark horse of the tournament, the contestant hailed by many as Bagdad’s Savior, Soren Everly, was severely injured during the incident and has officially forfeited the competition. According to our sources, it will take him a few months to fully recover... We wish him the best and hope for his speedy recovery."
Soren’s eyes finally lit up. "He really fulfilled his promise!"
Ethea nodded. "It seems like the City Lord is truly a great person."
Soren nodded in agreement, and they turned back to the TV since the reporter looked like he had more to say.

"But that’s not all. In a stunning turn of events, the other two finalists have also forfeited from the competition. And what’s more..." He paused, his eyes widening slightly. "They both nominated Chef Soren as the winner!"

The screen displayed a graphic with all three contestants’ faces, and the word "FORFEITED" stamped across each one. However, the next moment, Soren’s image was pushed to the center, and the word changed to "CHAMPION!" in bold golden letters.
Soren blinked. "...Wait, what?"
Ethea was equally surprised; however, she quickly recovered and looked at Soren with a smile. "You won, dear. Congratulations!
Soren stared at the screen, still processing the shocking news. "T-Thank you, dear... But why?"

"That’s right, folks." The reporter continued, his voice carrying a mix of amazement and amusement. "With all three finalists stepping down, the judges and organizers were left with an unprecedented situation. And after reviewing the footage, the performances, the participants’ opinions, and the public vote, they have decided to award the championship to none other than Bagdad’s Savior - Soren Everly!"
"..." Soren let out a sigh and ran a hand through his hair. "This is not how I expected things to go..."

Why did Nuelia and Damir forfeit anyway? Nuelia, he could understand. She was clearly an emotional person, and after everything that had happened, she probably didn’t have the heart to continue. But Damir? That was unexpected.
"Why did they nominate me..."
He trailed off and glanced at Ethea, only to find her already looking at him with a knowing smile.
"...What?" He asked helplessly.
"It’s not that complicated. They both must believe you deserve it the most; that’s why they did it," she said softly. "And... they’re not wrong."
"...Is that so?" Soren murmured, still half doubtful.
Then he paused, remembering something. He pulled out the spatial ring Lord Asad had given him yesterday. He hadn’t had time to check its contents since then.
As he scanned through it, his body suddenly went still.
"What is it?" Ethea asked curiously.
Soren didn’t answer right away. He slowly reached into the ring and pulled out a familiar object. The shiny surface reflected the sunlight, casting a warm golden glow across the table.
It was the Golden Ladle.

chapters.title: Chapter 316: Another Acquaintance
paragraphs: "...They must have decided it yesterday." Ethea voiced her guess as she looked at the Golden Ladle. "The other two must have met the City Lord, or he learned from his subordinates."
"...Yeah," Soren whispered, still not entirely sure how to feel about it.

He turned his attention back to the spatial ring and inspected its contents more carefully. Inside, he found everything he had requested: the rare ingredients, neatly packed and labeled, along with a few extra supplies Lord Asad had mentioned. But there was more.

Tucked beside the ingredients were several items he hadn’t asked for. A large amount of high-grade mana stones, a set of finely crafted cooking tools, and a sealed envelope with the official seal of Bagdad City. He opened it and found a formal certificate declaring him the winner of the Golden Ladle Championship.
Soren stared at it for a moment before muttering, "This must be the entry ticket to the Grand Magic Chef Tournament."
"...Will you participate?" Ethea asked curiously while calculating the timeline in her mind.

They were planning to stay here for at least two months, and then head to the Tower of Apocalypse. They had researched this tournament out of curiosity a few days ago, and it would be held each year in October. The host nation would be announced a month in advance, giving participants a month to travel and prepare.
Soren thought about it for a moment. "I’m not sure yet. It depends on where it’s held and how our schedule looks." He glanced at the ticket again. "But having the option is nice."
Ethea nodded in agreement.

If the tournament were to be held on another continent or somewhere too far from their route, it would be difficult to attend without disrupting their plans. But if it happened to be nearby, or along the way to the Tower of Apocalypse, then it might be worth considering.
"We’ll figure it out when they announce the location," she said.
"Mm." Soren put the ring away and picked up his spoon. "Let’s take care of what we can for now. It’s not that important anyway."

If anyone else had heard him, they would have thought he was insane. After all, the Grand Magic Chef Tournament was a worldwide event. Chefs spent their entire lives dreaming of earning a spot, and some never even got close. To brush it off so casually was unthinkable for most.

But Soren wasn’t most people. It wasn’t that he didn’t understand the value of the opportunity. He did. He simply had other priorities. Ethea’s safety and health came first. If the tournament happened to align with their path and didn’t put her at risk, he would consider it seriously. If it could even help in finding a cure for her curse, then it would be worth pursuing. But until he knew that, it remained a distant option.
He shook his head, clearing the thoughts away. "Should we contact the academy today?"
Ethea nodded. "...It’s better to get it done early. The sooner we handle the formalities, the more time we have to settle in."
"Alright." Soren stood up and began clearing the table. "Let’s get ready and head out."

"Wait," Ethea said, stopping him. "Let’s contact my acquaintance first. We should learn the current situation and make an appointment before showing up unannounced. And while we’re at it, we can ask about your sister too."
Soren paused at the mention of his sister. A brief flicker of something crossed his face before he nodded. "...Alright. Let’s do that."
He then picked up her phone and helped her connect with her acquaintance. The contact was saved simply as "Zura".

The line rang twice before a lively female voice answered. "Ethea?! Is that really you? Oh my goodness, it’s been so long! How have you been? Where are you? Wait, don’t tell me you’re actually in the city?!"
"It’s me," Ethea replied shortly. "I arrived yesterday."
"Seriously?! Why didn’t you tell me earlier? I would have-"
"I need to ask you something." Ethea cut her off calmly. "Are you free today? I’d like to meet."

There was a brief pause on the other end, then a warm laugh. "Straight to business as always, huh? Some things never change. Do you remember? Back when we were still students, you used to do the same thing. Everyone was too afraid to appro-"
"Are you free or not?" Ethea cut her off again, colder this time. But from the blush on her cheeks, Soren could tell she was just embarrassed and didn’t want her friend to spill her ’dark’ past.
Zura laughed again before replying. "I’m sorry, but I only have time after lunch. Is it alright with you?
"Yes..." Ethea paused and, recalling that she hadn’t visited Ademary for a long time, added, "You can pick the place and time."
"Deal!" Zura said cheerfully. "Any preferences? Wait! Let me guess... Peaceful and quiet, right? And private too!"

"Hehe, I knew it. Some things really never change." Zura laughed. "Alright, leave it to me. I’ll text you the address. And... Let’s meet at six. I’ll treat you to dinner." She paused. "By the way, are you coming alone?"
Ethea fell silent for a moment, glancing at Soren. Then her eyes suddenly lit up, her lips curling up as if she was scheming something.
"No," she replied, her tone a bit playful. "I’m with my husband."
The other line went completely silent for exactly ten seconds. And then-
"W-WHAT?!"
"..." Soren could hear the shout through the phone even from where he was standing.
"H-HUSBAND?! YOU? ETHEA? THE ICE EMPRESS?" Zuhra sounded completely dumbfounded. "You really got married? Since when?! Who is he? Why-"
"We’ll talk later." Ethea cut her off again and hung up quickly. Almost immediately, her phone rang again. She stared at the incoming call, then laughed softly. "Hehe."

Soren watched Ethea and noticed the way her eyes crinkled at the corners, the way she laughed without holding back. There was a lightness to her expression that he rarely saw. It became clear that Zura was more than just a simple acquaintance. She was definitely a close friend, someone Ethea trusted enough to tease and be teased by.
’...It’s good to see her like this.’

chapters.title: Chapter 317: A Familiar Face
paragraphs: With the meeting scheduled for six in the evening, they had the rest of the day to themselves.
"We should find a hotel closer to the academy," Soren said, already pulling up a map on his phone. "It’ll save us time later, and it’s better to settle in before we start handling formalities."
Ethea nodded in agreement. "We can tour the city after that, too."

With the day also planned, they started browsing the hotels and chose a relatively close hotel with expensive but luxurious accommodations. With all the money Soren had earned from his investments and gate diving, they weren’t worried about the cost.

Once the booking was confirmed, they packed up their belongings and checked out of the previous hotel. Fortunately, they had teleported next to the academy district, on the eastern side of the Ademary City, so they didn’t have to travel far.
About half an hour later, they arrived at their new accommodations. The lobby was elegant, with polished marble floors and soft lighting that made the space feel inviting.
Soren approached the front desk while Ethea waited nearby. "Reservation under Everly."
The receptionist checked the system and nodded with a polite smile. "Yes, Mr. Everly. We have you in a deluxe suite on the twelfth floor." She handed him two key cards. "Please enjoy your stay."
Soren pocketed the cards and walked back to Ethea. "Twelfth floor. Let’s go."

They made their way to the elevator, and when they arrived, Soren pressed the button, and the doors slid open. He wheeled Ethea inside and turned the wheelchair around just as the doors began to close.
But in that brief moment, two figures emerged from the other elevator: a man and a woman, walking side by side.
’!’ Soren’s eyes widened.
For just a split second, he caught a glimpse of the woman before the doors shut — long red hair cascading past her shoulders, sharp brown eyes, and a familiar face he hadn’t seen in a long time.
The elevator began to rise, but Soren remained frozen, his gaze fixed on the closed doors.
Ethea immediately noticed his abnormality. "Dear? Are you ok?
Soren didn’t answer right away as his mind was still processing what he had just seen.
"..." Ethea, although still worried, chose to stay silent till he recovered.
A long moment later, Soren shook his head, muttering, "I thought I saw someone I knew."
Ethea studied his expression. "Someone you knew?"

"...Maybe," Soren exhaled slowly, still not entirely sure himself. After all, her hair color was different from what he remembered. It could have been his eyes or mind playing tricks on him, or she might have just dyed her hair.
’But those eyes...’ He couldn’t forget them. That piercing gaze and the way she carried herself, even in that brief glimpse, felt too familiar to be a coincidence.
But he shook his head, not to make Ethea worry. "It’s probably a mistake. Let’s not think about it for now."

Ethea nodded, though she made a mental note to keep an eye out. She had a guess as to who it might be, but like Soren, she didn’t want to jump to conclusions without more information. More importantly, she didn’t want their mood to be ruined because of them, especially with the long-awaited day just around the corner. If necessary, she would use her connections to take care of the matter quietly.
For now, she pushed the thought aside and focused on the present.

The elevator dinged, and the doors slid open on the twelfth floor. They stepped out and glanced down the corridor. Soft lights lined the walls, and the floor was carpeted in deep blue. Their suite was at the far end, marked by a small golden plaque that read 1208.

Soren unlocked the door and wheeled Ethea inside. The suite was spacious and well-furnished, with a large bedroom, a separate living area, a small kitchenette, and a private bathroom. A few windows stretched across one wall, offering a clear view of the academy district below.

He set their bags down and began unpacking the essentials. Since they had booked the room for a month, it made sense to settle in properly. Ethea helped where she could, directing him on where to place certain items.

Once everything was organized, they changed into fresh clothes and put their disguise items back on. Soren adjusted the collar of his summer jacket and glanced at Ethea, who had already concealed her features with a magic mask. They both looked like an ordinary couple with ordinary appearances.
"Ready?" he asked, raising his sunglasses with his finger.
Ethea nodded. "Let’s go.
[A few minutes earlier.]
"..." Sevrin stopped and looked at his wife, who was glancing around with squinted eyes. "What’s wrong, dear?"
She stopped and looked at him. "It’s nothing. I just felt someone was looking at me just now."
Sevrin let out a light chuckle. "Perhaps they were simply captivated by your beauty. It wouldn’t be the first time." A dark glint passed through his eyes as he spoke, there and gone in an instant.
His wife stared at him for a moment, then snorted coldly. "Spare me the useless flattery."
Sevrin ignored her tone and continued walking. "...Remember to control yourself later. She shouldn’t notice any abnormalities."
"I know." Her reply was flat and sharp. "And... How many times do I have to say it? I know it better than you. There’s no need to remind me again and again."

Sevrin didn’t respond, only offering a faint smile as they left the hotel. A car was already waiting for them outside. A gray-haired old man in a crisp black suit stood by the rear door, his posture straight and his expression neutral.
"My Lord. My Lady." He bowed slightly and opened the doors for them.
Once they were seated, the old man moved to the driver’s seat and started the engine. He glanced at them through the rearview mirror.
"Where to, My Lord?"
"Aldric, take us to the Academy," Sevrin ordered. "We’re going to see Nura."
"Understood." Aldric nodded and pulled the car smoothly into the flow of traffic, heading toward the Etenia Academy.

He set their bags down and began unpacking the essentials.
Since they had booked the room for a month, it made sense to settle in properly.
Ethea helped where she could, directing him on where to place certain items.
Once everything was organized, they changed into fresh clothes and put their disguise items back on.
Soren adjusted the collar of his summer jacket and glanced at Ethea, who had already concealed her features with a magic mask.
They both looked like an ordinary couple with ordinary appearances.
"Ready?" he asked, raising his sunglasses with his finger.
Ethea nodded.
"Let’s go.
[A few minutes earlier.]
"..." Sevrin stopped and looked at his wife, who was glancing around with squinted eyes.
"What’s wrong, dear?"
She stopped and looked at him.
"It’s nothing.
I just felt someone was looking at me just now."
Sevrin let out a light chuckle.
"Perhaps they were simply captivated by your beauty.
It wouldn’t be the first time." A dark glint passed through his eyes as he spoke, there and gone in an instant.
His wife stared at him for a moment, then snorted coldly.
"Spare me the useless flattery."
Sevrin ignored her tone and continued walking.
"...Remember to control yourself later.
She shouldn’t notice any abnormalities."
"I know." Her reply was flat and sharp.
"And...
How many times do I have to say it?
I know it better than you.
There’s no need to remind me again and again."
Sevrin didn’t respond, only offering a faint smile as they left the hotel.
A car was already waiting for them outside.
A gray-haired old man in a crisp black suit stood by the rear door, his posture straight and his expression neutral.
"My Lord.
My Lady." He bowed slightly and opened the doors for them.
Once they were seated, the old man moved to the driver’s seat and started the engine.
He glanced at them through the rearview mirror.
"Where to, My Lord?"
"Aldric, take us to the Academy," Sevrin ordered.
"We’re going to see Nura."
"Understood." Aldric nodded and pulled the car smoothly into the flow of traffic, heading toward the Etenia Academy.

chapters.title: Chapter 318: My Little Star
paragraphs: "Mother! Father!"
Nura cheerfully called out.
"Sweetie!"
"Nura..."
Her mother opened her arms, and Nura ran into them without hesitation. The two embraced warmly, while her father stood nearby with a satisfied nod.
"You came again today!" Nura said, looking up with bright eyes.
"Of course. We missed you," her mother replied, brushing a strand of hair from Nura’s face. "How are your studies? Are you eating well?"
"Yes, yes, everything is fine. You worry too much." Nura laughed.
Her father stepped forward and placed a hand on her shoulder. "Keep working hard."
"I will, Father."
They talked for a while longer, the conversation light and warm. But eventually, it was time to go.

"Don’t forget about our appointment." Her father said, his tone carrying a hint of seriousness beneath the warmth. "I really want to treat you to a proper meal before we leave the city. It’s been too long since we’ve eaten together as a family, too."
Nura’s eyes lit up again. "I won’t forget. I promise!"
"Good." Her father smiled and playfully ruffled her hair. "I also promise to buy you anything you want!"
"Hehe, then I will order the most expensive thing on the menu," Nura teased. "You can’t complain later."
"I wouldn’t dare." Her father chuckled.
Her mother watched the exchange with a faint smile, though her eyes held something unreadable. "We really should go now."
Nura nodded and hugged her mother one last time. "See you later~.
"See you later, sweetie."

With that, they parted ways. Nura watched as they left, her fists clenched slightly. She then turned to her personal maid. "Sister Grace, can you bring a meal from outside again? I wanna eat something sweet."
The maid nodded. "I’ll be back as soon as possible."
"Thank you! And remember to buy ice cream too!"
"As you wish." She bowed and walked away, leaving Nura alone. Nura watched her leave and slowly made her way back to her room. Her steps were unhurried, a smile playing on her lips. But...
As soon as she stepped inside and the door clicked shut behind her, the smile vanished.
"Huf..." She took a deep breath and opened her fists, staring at her palms. The reddish marks lingered on her skin, faint but unmistakable. She fell silent, her expression turning complex.

It was because these reddish marks came from her mother’s hair. She had run her fingers through it when they hugged, and the faint residue of dye had stained her skin. She had used a special spell she learned from a friend to confirm it, and the results were clear as day.
’...She...’ She muttered inwardly. ’Is she really my mother?’
That single doubt, buried deep for so long, now began to surface.

The mother in her memories always had red hair. She was sure of that. But no matter how hard she tried, she couldn’t remember her face clearly. It was always blurred, like a portrait left out in the rain.

She had tried to sharpen that image, to recall the warmth of her smile and the exact shade of her eyes. But every time she reached for it, every time her face began to take shape in her mind, it would blur and slip away, leaving behind only a vague silhouette and a faint sense of longing.
And now... this woman who claimed to be her mother had dyed hair.
It could be a coincidence since many people dyed their hair. Perhaps she used to dye her hair back then too, and now she was just doing the same or was covering up her graying hair.
But... the doubt had already planted itself, and it refused to be uprooted. Because that wasn’t the only thing that felt wrong.
Her mother used to call her ’my little star.’ Not ’sweetie’ or ’dear’. In all of the memories she could recall, it was always ’my little star’.

Nura had told herself it was a childish thing to cling to, a pet name that didn’t prove anything. But the woman who visited her today had never once called her that. Logically, to help her remember, her mother should have used it, right?
But more than the name, it was the absence of something else that bothered her. She didn’t feel any connection with this woman. It was hard to describe, but something felt missing.

Sure, she sounded and acted like her real mother, and Nura really felt happy when she was with her. However, that happiness never truly reached her heart. It stayed on the surface, like a reflection on water. When they parted, it faded quickly, leaving behind a strange emptiness she couldn’t explain.

She wanted to believe it was because of her lost memories. That the connection would return in time if she just kept meeting her. But it hadn’t. If anything, the distance between them only seemed to grow with each visit.

What frustrated her even more was that her father was the same as in her memories. She couldn’t remember every detail, but what she did remember matched the man who visited her today. His face, his voice, and his stern personality.
So why wasn’t it the same with her mother?
...Who was her mother? Was she overthinking? Or was this mother her father’s new wife? If so, what happened to her real mother?

’...’ She sank to the floor, her back against the door, her mind spinning in circles. The questions kept coming, each one heavier than the last. She pulled her knees to her chest and buried her face in her arms, her breath coming out in short, uneven bursts.
She snapped out of her thoughts only after she heard a knock on the door.
She quickly wiped her face and forced herself to stand. Taking a deep breath, she smoothed down her clothes and opened the door.
Standing there was a girl with short purple hair and a sweet smile on her face. "Hello, Nura! I was just heading to the cafeteria. Want to eat lunch together?"
Nura’s expression turned awkward as she shook her head. "Ah... sorry, Sister Grace already went to get me something."
"Oh." The girl’s smile faltered slightly, but she nodded in understanding. "That’s fine. Maybe next time then."
"...Wait!" Nura called out just as the girl took her third step. "Actually... do you want to eat with me instead? I’ll tell Sister Grace to add another portion on the way."
The girl’s eyes lit up. "Really? Are you sure?"
"Mm." Nura nodded. "Just consider it a thank you for the spell you taught me. It... really came in handy."

chapters.title: Chapter 319: Dinner With A Friend [1]
paragraphs: "Is this the place?" Soren asked as he stared at the building before them.

It was a large structure built with tall pillars made of stone-like material, carved wooden beams, and a sweeping turquoise dome that reflected the evening sun. The arched entrance was framed with intricate geometric patterns, and the walls were decorated with tiles in shades of blue and gold.

What surprised him the most was the moving mural along the walls. It shifted and flowed like a living painting, and at its center was a golden deer, its antlers glowing faintly as it moved gracefully through an endless garden of silver leaves.
"Yes," Ethea replied with a smile, recognition crossing her features. "Zura said she’d meet us here."
"She picked an amazing place," Soren said, smiling back, and pulled out his phone. "Let me take a few pictures before we go in."

Since there were a few others doing the same, likely tourists, he didn’t feel out of place. He snapped a few shots from different angles, capturing the dome, the mural, and the enchanting entrance. He actually wanted to take a few pictures with Ethea, but since they were wearing disguises, he decided against it. It would be better to take them once they could walk around freely.
Still, he was satisfied with what he got.
"Let’s go in." He pocketed his phone and pushed Ethea through the arched entrance.

Inside, the place was just as impressive as the exterior. Warm lighting filled the space, reflecting off polished floors and casting soft shadows across the intricately carved walls. The same golden deer motif appeared here and there, woven masterfully into the decor. A soft melody played in the background, a magical tune that seemed to lift their already bright mood.
A hostess approached them with a warm smile. "Welcome to the Golden Deer. How may I help you?"
"We’re meeting someone," Soren replied. "Her name is Zura Ayun."

"Let me see." The hostess nodded and tapped on the tablet in her hands. After a moment, she looked up with a polite smile. "Yes, Miss Ayun has already arrived. She’s waiting in private room seven. Let me escort you there."
Soren nodded and wheeled Ethea after her while mentally communicating with her. ’No wonder there are only golden deer motifs everywhere. The place is called the Golden Deer.’

After observing closely, he noticed them even on the cups, the plates, and the small carvings along the wooden frames of the doors. Every detail was consistent, as if the entire establishment had been built around that single symbol.
’Have you been here before?’

’I have,’ Ethea replied. ’And there’s actually a story behind this place. The owner was once an ordinary hunter, and during one of his adventures, he accidentally ended up inside a Golden Gate. However, he soon found himself badly wounded, barely clinging to life. And just when he thought he was going to die, a golden deer appeared before him. It saved his life and even led him to a treasure. So, after he returned, he opened this place in honor of that deer. He considers it his lucky charm and his savior.’
’Oh! A Golden Gate?’ Soren exclaimed inwardly. He never expected to hear about a fellow Golden Gate survivor so soon. ’I wonder what he went through there.’
’Unfortunately, he hadn’t revealed the details.’ Ethea replied. ’Perhaps he just wanted to keep the good part of the memory. Or... It all could have been a lie too.’
’Wait... You mean...’ Soren instantly understood what Ethea implied.

’Yes. Some people make up stories about Golden Gates to build their reputation. The owner might have genuinely been inside one, or he might have just used the legend to create a theme and draw in customers.’ Ethea explained. ’But I might be just overthinking it too.’
’Mm...’ Soren nodded inwardly.
Just then, the hostess stopped in front of a door marked with a small golden plaque that read "Room 7." She turned to them with a polite smile.
"Here we are. Miss Ayun is waiting inside."
She knocked twice, then slid the door open.

There, seated at a low table in the center of the room, was a woman with short black hair tied back neatly. She wore a soft lavender summer dress that was modest yet elegant, complemented by a distinctive silver bracelet on her wrist. Her delicate features, bright hazel eyes, and rich dark brown skin gave her a refined yet friendly presence.
The moment they entered, her eyes landed on Soren, then quickly shifted to Ethea, and her face lit up with a bright smile. "Lea! You are here!

’...Lea, huh.’ Soren speculated either Ethea told her or she figured it out after seeing them in disguise. Neverthless, she was sharp. That much was clear. ’As expected of an Etenia Academy instructor, I guess.’
He then thanked the hostess for her help. She bowed slightly and took her leave, sliding the door shut behind her.
Meanwhile, Zura moved around the table, her steps light and eager. She stopped in front of Soren first and gave him a polite bow. "Good evening, Mr. Everly. It’s nice to finally meet you."
Then, without waiting for a reply, she turned to Ethea and threw her arms around her in a cheerful hug.
"Ethea! It’s been so long!"
"Mmm. Long time no see," Ethea replied with a smile, hugging her friend back.
They stayed like that for a while before Zura reluctantly let go and stood up.

"I’m glad to finally meet you." Soren used the opportunity to greet and introduce himself. "I’m Soren, Ethea’s husband. Thank you for making time to see us on such short notice. I know you must be busy with your work at the academy."
"No need to thank me. I’m Zura Ayun." She nodded back and introduced herself with a slight smirk. "And I’m this cold beauty’s best friend. The only one, actually, if I remember correctly."
Soren let out a faint smile. "Is that so?"
"Zura..." Ethea stared at her, her expression unreadable.
"Hehe~" Zura chuckled and gestured toward the table. "Come, have a seat. It’ll be more comfortable to talk this way."
Soren nodded, wheeling Ethea to the table, and after positioning her, he sat down next to her.
Zura watched them with a smile and added after they both took their seats. "I already ordered some tea and snacks, but feel free to order whatever you like. Dinner’s on me tonight."

chapters.title: Chapter 320: Dinner With A Friend [2]
paragraphs: After the initial greetings, the trio quickly grew comfortable with each other. Soren also used Advanced Appraisal on Zura while she was busy catching up with Ethea.
Name: Zura Ayun
Race: Human
Age: 22
Status: Healthy
Rank: 6th Circle (Mid Stage)
Current Mana Level: 1,858,400
Mental State: Relaxed, Curious
Abilities: Infernal Bloom, Phoenix Tear
Affinities: Fire (Grade 8 - SS Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Heart’s Insight
Potential: 8th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: SUPREME
Seeing her affinity and abilities, his eyes lit up. ’I think I now know how Ethea could learn so much about Nura.’

If he guessed correctly, Zura might be Nura’s teacher, or hold a high position at the academy to be privy to that kind of information. Either way, she was definitely the best person who could help them.
However, he wasn’t in a hurry, as they had just met. So, he just sat back and watched as the two women talked.

Zura asked about Ethea’s condition, her tone shifting from cheerful to genuinely concerned. Ethea answered without hesitation, sharing more than she usually would with anyone else. She spoke about her recovery, the treatments, and even some of the difficulties she faced. Zura listened intently, her expression softening with each word.
’I guess they really are best friends,’ Soren thought, a small smile tugging at his lips.

After a while, Zura leaned back and clapped her hands together. "Enough about that. Now, tell me..." She looked between the two of them with eager eyes. "When did you get married? And how did this even happen? With your personality, I was sure you were going to remain single for the rest of your life."
Ethea let out a small sigh, doing her best to ignore her last sentence. "It’s... a long story."
"I have time." Zura grinned. "Besides, you owe me. You didn’t even invite me to the wedding."
"It... It wasn’t that kind of wedding," Ethea replied calmly.
Zura raised a brow. "What kind of wedding doesn’t invite the bride’s best friend?"
"...I’ll tell you later," Ethea replied after glancing at Soren. "What about you? Have you got married yet?" She paused, staring at Zura. "...With your temper, I’m guessing probably not."

Zura’s lips twitched. "You got that right. Happy now?" She huffed and crossed her arms. "But I’m not the one at fault here, okay! I went on a few dates, you know. I really tried. But every single guy was either too scared to even speak a few words, or they walked around with their noses so high in the air they couldn’t even see the ground." She let out an exaggerated sigh. "So I decided to just stick to my job and wait for a fateful encounter instead."
Ethea smiled faintly. "That sounds like you."
"What’s that supposed to mean?" Zura narrowed her eyes, but there was no real bite behind it.
"Nothing."
"Urgh..."
’...Her hidden talent, Heart’s Insight, probably helped her.’ Soren guessed as he kept listening.

From what he understood, Heart’s Insight allowed her to sense the emotions and intentions of those around her, almost like reading their hearts. That explained why she could tell when someone was putting on a facade or hiding their true feelings. In a world full of political games and deception, that kind of ability was invaluable.

The same went for relationships. She could probably tell right away if someone was genuine or just putting on an act to impress her. That would explain why she had trouble finding a partner. Most people couldn’t hide their true selves from her, and the ones who tried only exposed themselves faster.

It also explained why she and Ethea got along so well. Ethea wasn’t the type to open up easily, but with someone who could see past her cold exterior, there was no point in pretending. Zura probably understood her better than most.

’And if I had to guess, it was definitely Zura who approached Ethea first and refused to give up until she got through to her.’ He smiled inwardly at the thought, imagining the scene. ’Yeah, that sounds about right.’

"And you, Mr. Everly." Zura suddenly turned to him, snapping him out of his thoughts. "What do you do? How did you manage to seduce my little ice block? You do look handsome, but she wasn’t the type to be swayed by looks."

"..." Soren fell silent at her question, pondering how to reply. Since he hadn’t confessed to Ethea yet, he feared that saying too much or the wrong words might make things awkward between them. He also didn’t want to assume anything about her feelings when he hadn’t even told her his own.

He took a quick glance at Ethea and found her watching him with an unreadable expression. She didn’t seem worried or uncomfortable. If anything, there was a hint of curiosity in her eyes, as if she was also waiting to hear what he would say.
"We’re still getting to know each other," Soren said carefully. "I wouldn’t say I seduced her. More like... we’re figuring things out as we go."
Zura raised a brow, clearly not satisfied with that answer. "Figuring things out? That’s vague."

Soren shrugged lightly, thinking perhaps it was better to just leave it at that. He couldn’t exactly pour his heart out in front of someone he just met, especially not about something so personal. Besides, confessing to Ethea was something he wanted to do properly.

Zura stared at him for a moment longer, then let out a sigh. "Fine. Don’t say it if you don’t want to." She gave him a grudging look, but when her eyes shifted to Ethea, her expression softened into a smile. "I’ll find out everything from her later anyway."
Soren let out a breath, relieved to move on from that topic. He then took the opportunity to steer the conversation elsewhere.
"So, you’re an instructor at Etenia Academy, right?"
Zura turned back to him and nodded with a proud smile. "Impressive, right?"
"Indeed, you must be incredibly talented to become an instructor there at such a young age." Soren praised her. But he was honest and speaking the truth.

Teaching at the continent’s best academy was not something just anyone could do. It required not only skill but also experience, patience, and a reputation that could withstand the scrutiny of students and faculty alike. To achieve that at twenty-two, or perhaps even earlier, was nothing short of remarkable.

chapters.title: Chapter 321: Dinner With a Friend [3]
paragraphs: "Talented?" Zura’s smile widened, but she waved a hand modestly. "Maybe a little. But mostly I just worked hard. The academy doesn’t care about your age or background. If you’re good enough, you get in. And thankfully, I was."

Soren subtly nodded, noting her humility. She was proud of her achievements, but she didn’t let it go to her head. That was a good sign, as people who were too full of themselves tended to be difficult to work with.
"So, you still haven’t answered my other question," Zura continued, turning back to him with a pointed look. "What do you do? And don’t give me a vague answer again."
Soren chuckled inwardly. "Well, I’m sure you’ve already guessed it by now, but yeah. I’m a chef. But I’m also a Hunter."
Zura’s smile widened at his confirmation. "So you’re really Bagdad’s Savior?!"
"Yes, I’m Chef Soren, Soren Everly." Soren gave a small nod. "Though I’d prefer if you didn’t call me that. It sounds more impressive than it actually was."

Zura leaned forward, her eyes gleaming with interest. "More impressive than it actually was? You won the Championship! Isn’t that more than enough? And I’ve even come across some rumors online suggesting you had a fight with the Outcasts."
Soren kept his expression composed, realizing she was testing him. He just chose to stay silent, but took a note to check the internet later.
"..." Zura kept staring at him, waiting for an answer. The silence stretched on, but she didn’t look away. If anything, her smile only grew, as if she was enjoying the challenge.
Before it could get too awkward, Ethea spoke up. "Zura."
"Hm?" Zura turned to her friend, her attention finally shifting.
"We actually wanted to ask you something," Ethea said.
Zura gasped dramatically and placed a hand over her heart. "Oh? So you’re here for business, not to see your best friend? I see how it is. Now that you have a husband, I’ve been replaced."
"...Pfft." Both Ethea and Soren couldn’t help but laugh at her over-the-top reaction. Ethea covered her mouth in order not to ruin her image.
Zura’s act crumbled immediately as she grinned. A moment later, they calmed down. "Alright, what do you want to ask?" Zura inquired as she took a sip of her tea.
"It’s about the transfer student we talked about before," Ethea replied. "Along with a ’gift’ to the academy."
"I see." Zura nodded in understanding. After all, they had talked about these matters before, and she had promised to lend a helping hand. Now, it was time to fulfill that promise.
"So, tell me," she said, setting her teacup down. "What exactly do you need from me?"

"Let me do it," Soren said, making a slightly solemn expression. He then explained everything, starting by introducing Ryan to their plan to give the Monolith of the Primal Axis to the Academy. He also included other details that they didn’t need any payment or compensation and just asked that the monolith be used freely by the students.
"...So, we wanted to help us with this." Soren finished his story.
"...Hmm." Zura fell silent, probably pondering the proposal. Her expression was unreadable as she stared at her teacup, turning it slowly between her fingers.

After a long moment, she looked up. "That’s... a lot to take in. Are you saying you want to give something like that? For free?" She glanced between the two of them, as if checking whether they were serious. "...You’re serious, huh."
Soren nodded. "So, what do you think?"

"...Hehe, what else can I say?" Zura grinned. "I’m in. I’ll help you with the monolith and make sure it gets to the right hands. As for the boy, Ryan, as long as he can pass the transfer exam, I’ll take him into my own class."
Soren blinked. "Your class?"

"That’s right." Zura nodded smugly. "Although I might not look like it, I’m a homeroom teacher of the third-year class. I took over them last year, and I’ve been doing well, so there’s no need to worry. If the boy passes the transfer exam, he’ll be in good hands."
’She’s a homeroom teacher, huh...’ Soren’s mind raced. ’Then? Could Nura be in her class too?’
"Zura, do you know a student called Nura?" Ethea, as if reading Soren’s thoughts, spoke up. "Nura Valmere, to be more exact."
Zura nodded. "I know her. Although she’s not in my class, I am her Fire Manipulation Class teacher. And... her condition is a bit special, so I teach her after classes too."
Soren and Ethea’s eyes lit up, and they exchanged a glance with each other.
"...Is she someone you know?" Zura asked, observing their reactions.
Soren nodded. "She is... my little sister."

"...What?" Zura’s eyes widened, her teacup pausing halfway to her lips. She set it down slowly, her expression shifting from surprise to something more serious. "Your little sister? But she told me her family was... well, she only mentioned her parents."
"...I heard she has amnesia?" Soren asked after hesitating for a moment. "Is she ok now? Can you tell me about her?"

"...First, tell me about yourself," Zura replied, taking a slightly interrogative tone. "Unless I am sure you’re her real brother, I can’t share anything about her. Even if Ethea is my best friend, I won’t break the rules. I hope you understand that."
"No worries, I understand it well." Soren nodded with a smile. "So, allow me to explain."
Zura nodded, indicating that he should go on.

"...Actually, I was born into the Valmere family." Soren started his story. But he kept unnecessary details, like his childhood, to himself and told her only what she needed to know. Like Nura actually being his half-sister, her real mother dying, how she got awakened and ended up bedridden, and even revealed that his marriage to Ethea had a connection to it.
"...That’s the gist of it," he finished.
Zura listened silently, her expression unreadable throughout. When he was done, she remained quiet for a moment longer, studying him.
"...So..." She finally opened her mouth, her eyes cold. "You’re telling me that her parents are pure scums who are manipulating your little sister?"
"No," Ethea cut in before Soren could reply. Her words were resolute, her expression more icy than either Soren or Zura had ever seen. "They are worse than scum."

chapters.title: Chapter 322: Dinner With a Friend [4]
paragraphs: "They’re worse than scum."

Zura fell silent at Ethea’s words. She easily noticed the disgust and hatred toward those two with her unique trait, but what surprised her more was the intensity of it. Ethea was never one to show such strong emotions, especially not toward people she barely knew. For her to react like this, there had to be more to the story than what Soren had told her.
She could also sense Soren’s state; he, too, held complex emotions toward his parents and was grateful to Ethea for speaking up, for saying what he couldn’t put into words himself.

’...She’s truly in love with him, huh?’ She thought to herself. It seemed like her worries about her husband being a bad person or that she had been tricked were completely unfounded. The emotions she sensed from Ethea were genuine, deep, and unwavering. And the same went for Soren. Although his feelings ran even deeper, he kept them tightly restrained, as if afraid that letting them show would somehow cause harm.
’...Interesting. It seems like there’s more to their story than they let on.’
With a smile, she leaned back and crossed her arms. "Alright, I believe you." She then locked eyes with Soren. "What do you plan to do? To save her, I mean."
"I want to know more about her condition first," Soren replied without hesitation. "Then I will find a way to cure her and free her from Valmere’s clutches."
"Oh, you think you can cure her?" Zura asked again, curiosity filling her features.

"Yes," Soren replied with confidence. "As long as I can meet her in person and learn everything about her condition, I’m sure I can find a way. It might take time, but I won’t stop until she is free."
Zura studied him for a long moment, searching for any sign of doubt or exaggeration. She found none. His words were sincere, his conviction genuine.
"...You really mean that," she murmured.
"I do."

"It’s great to hear that." Zura grinned and leaned forward. "You know what? I’ll definitely help you now. I took a liking to her anyway. She’s a bit awkward sometimes, but she’s sincere and tries her best. To think she would have such a tragic past..." She shook her head. "It makes me want to look out for her even more."
"Thank you." Soren bowed in gratitude.

Zura nodded and took another sip before starting. "I’m sure you already know about her ability, but I’ll fill in the details. She awakened the Blazing Sun Constitution. It’s an SS-rank flame constitution, incredibly rare and powerful. The problem is that it’s too powerful for a normal body, especially a fragile one like hers, to contain. The fire burns constantly inside her, like a miniature sun trying to escape. While it gives her immense power, it also slowly consumes her from within. If left unchecked, she wouldn’t live past eighteen."
Soren’s jaw tightened, but he didn’t interrupt.

"Right now, she’s stable because of an ice-related artifact her family, or Ethea’s father, to be more precise, provided. It can suppress the flames and keep them from going out of control. However, it is not a permanent solution; only a temporary measure."
She paused, letting her words sink in before continuing.

"As long as she wears it, she should be fine and can live longer, but only up to around twenty. And there’s also a drawback. While she can still use mana and her other affinities, the artifact prevents her from using her constitution entirely. And if she ever takes it off..." Zura paused. "The flames would surge instantly. She’d fall back to her previous state. Her body would be overwhelmed again, and it would become even harder to stabilize her the next time."
She let out a slow breath, her expression turning grim. "In fact, she could have been saved and living a healthy life by now. But only if..."
"...You mean," Soren instantly caught what she was implying and couldn’t help but clench his fists.

Zura nodded. "Yes. The Valmere family wasted precious time. The damage was still reversible in the early stages. However, they delayed too long, kept her concealed, and searched for solutions independently rather than seeking external assistance. And by the time they finally realized they couldn’t fix her themselves, the damage had already set in."
"..." Soren’s expression grew darker.
"Now that I know the full story," Zura said, her voice cold, "I can say it without hesitation too. Your former family, especially your parents, are indeed worse than scum.

"...Right," Soren replied after a moment, relaxing his fists. "They are indeed worse than scum. They’re selfish and greedy, and only care about benefits and reputation. Everything they do is calculated, weighed, and measured by how much it can elevate the Valmere name. Their children are nothing more than tools to them. If a child is useful, they’re kept close. If a child is broken or useless, they’re discarded without a second thought."

He paused, his jaw tightening. "My sister nearly died, and instead of getting her proper help, they hid her away like a shameful secret. They let her suffer because they were too afraid of losing their precious prodigy to someone else. They put their own interests over her life." His voice grew quieter, but no less sharp. "Even... Even mindless beasts know to shield their young from harm."
Ethea and Zura exchanged glances and turned back to him.

’...Soren.’ Ethea whispered. This was the first time he’d spoken so openly about his family, and the bitterness in his voice was unmistakable. She reached out and gently placed her hand over his clenched fist.
Soren took a deep breath and let the tension ease from his shoulders. He looked at Ethea and gave her a small nod, gently squeezing her hand in return. "Thank you, dear."
Zura watched them, a faint smile touching her lips.
’...They really look good together. But... Watching them like this is reminding me that I’m still very much single... Urgh...’
"Ahem..." She cleared her throat softly, bringing their attention back to the matter at hand. "What’s the plan?"
