And there’s also a drawback.
While she can still use mana and her other affinities, the artifact prevents her from using her constitution entirely.
And if she ever takes it off..." Zura paused.
"The flames would surge instantly.
She’d fall back to her previous state.
Her body would be overwhelmed again, and it would become even harder to stabilize her the next time."
She let out a slow breath, her expression turning grim.
"In fact, she could have been saved and living a healthy life by now.
But only if..."
"...You mean," Soren instantly caught what she was implying and couldn’t help but clench his fists.
Zura nodded.
"Yes.
The Valmere family wasted precious time.
The damage was still reversible in the early stages.
However, they delayed too long, kept her concealed, and searched for solutions independently rather than seeking external assistance.
And by the time they finally realized they couldn’t fix her themselves, the damage had already set in."
"..." Soren’s expression grew darker.
"Now that I know the full story," Zura said, her voice cold, "I can say it without hesitation too.
Your former family, especially your parents, are indeed worse than scum.
"...Right," Soren replied after a moment, relaxing his fists.
"They are indeed worse than scum.
They’re selfish and greedy, and only care about benefits and reputation.
Everything they do is calculated, weighed, and measured by how much it can elevate the Valmere name.
Their children are nothing more than tools to them.
If a child is useful, they’re kept close.
If a child is broken or useless, they’re discarded without a second thought."
He paused, his jaw tightening.
"My sister nearly died, and instead of getting her proper help, they hid her away like a shameful secret.
They let her suffer because they were too afraid of losing their precious prodigy to someone else.
They put their own interests over her life." His voice grew quieter, but no less sharp.
"Even...
Even mindless beasts know to shield their young from harm."
Ethea and Zura exchanged glances and turned back to him.
’...Soren.’ Ethea whispered.
This was the first time he’d spoken so openly about his family, and the bitterness in his voice was unmistakable.
She reached out and gently placed her hand over his clenched fist.
Soren took a deep breath and let the tension ease from his shoulders.
He looked at Ethea and gave her a small nod, gently squeezing her hand in return.
"Thank you, dear."
Zura watched them, a faint smile touching her lips.
’...They really look good together.
But...
Watching them like this is reminding me that I’m still very much single...
Urgh...’
"Ahem..." She cleared her throat softly, bringing their attention back to the matter at hand.
"What’s the plan?"

chapters.title: Chapter 323: Dinner With a Friend [5]
paragraphs: "Then... is there a way for me to meet her?" Soren asked, his tone shifting to something more serious. "It doesn’t have to be an official meeting. A private one would be ideal, but even if I could just see her from a distance, that would be enough for now. It would be better if no one else knew about it too."

Zura set her teacup down and considered his request. "A private meeting... that’s not impossible, but it won’t be easy either. The academy has strict rules about visitors, and I’m sure Nura’s schedule is closely monitored by the people her family hired to watch over her, especially her personal maid. She probably reports everything back to the Valmeres."
"I see..." Soren nodded in understanding. Since he lived with the Valmeres for a long time, he knew exactly how their household operated.

Most children in noble families were assigned personal maids or butlers from a young age. Almost every major house followed the same tradition, including the Valmeres, though they took it further than most. On the surface, they were caretakers, but in reality, they were watchers planted by the family to report everything their young master or lady did and keep them in check. Only children who were already considered useless or ’sinful’, like him, were exceptions.

Zura hesitated for a moment, then spoke again. "Actually, there’s something else you should know." She paused, choosing her words carefully. "Her... I mean, your ’parents’ are here, and they’ve been visiting her for the past week... Every single day."
"..." Hearing her, Soren fell silent again.
However, his reaction surprised Zura. "You don’t seem... surprised?"
Soren sighed and asked. "Have you seen them? Can you describe their appearances?"
Zura nodded and explained, including how happy Nura seemed when talking about her parents.
"Dear..." Ethea whispered, finally confirming why Soren acted that way yesterday.

"I saw a glimpse of mother yesterday when we arrived at the hotel," Soren explained to confused Zura. "But I thought it was someone else since her hair color was different. But now it all makes sense."
"You mean..." Zura muttered, her eyes widening.

"That’s right. My mother is pretending to be her real mother," Soren replied, his expression grim. "I have seen Nura’s real mother. She had natural red hair, so my mother dyed hers to match. And based on what you told me, it seems to be working.
"...I think her amnesia isn’t related to her condition," Ethea spoke up, looking at Soren. "They must have done something to her. Just like they messed with your memories."
"Yeah, you’re right." Soren agreed with her. "And it might be the same person who tampered with my memories."
"Do you know them?" Zura prompted.

"Unfortunately, no." Soren shook his head. "They must have made sure I couldn’t remember them. I could have been unconscious when it was done too, so I would never have seen their face or heard their voice. Either way, I have no memory of them. But... being able to tamper with someone’s memories to that extent... they would obviously prefer staying hidden."
Ethea and Zura agreed with his reasoning.

Individuals like that were rare, and anyone willing to use it on another person without consent was committing a serious crime. If their actions and identities were ever exposed, they would face severe punishment under awakened law. No one with half a brain would risk that kind of exposure.
But there was one question that Soren couldn’t shake from his mind.
"...How did my parents hire such an individual?"
His question made the two women pause too.
"Right..."
It was a valid concern.

Memory manipulation wasn’t a service you could just find in a back alley. The people who could do it were either tightly controlled by the Awakened Bureau or operating in circles far beyond the reach of a mid-tier noble family like the Valmeres. For Soren’s parents to have access to someone like that, they either had connections they shouldn’t have, or they had paid a price far higher than money.

Soren knew his family wasn’t righteous. They were ruthless, manipulative, and willing to do whatever it took to climb higher. He wondered if they had gone outside the law entirely. Perhaps they had connections to criminals, or worse, to organizations that dealt in things no respectable noble family should touch.
"...I think I know how," Ethea spoke up again, making the other two turn to her. "...It’s probably my father. He... must have helped them.
"!" Soren’s eyes lit up. He had almost forgotten about his father-in-law. ’She’s right. Since my father and hers were the ones who made the deal, they must have included these too.’
"...Wait." He froze, his eyes widening. "Ethea! Can your father do something like that? Manipulate memories, I mean."
"...I’m not sure," Ethea replied after hesitating for a moment. "But I’m certain he has connections to people who can."

Soren nodded but didn’t entirely rule out the possibility. While he hadn’t seen an ability related to mental manipulation, you could expect anything from that guy. ’...Wait. Doesn’t that mean he might be involved in Ethea’s altered memories too?’
It sounded plausible, but he decided to keep it for himself for now. They could discuss it privately later.
"So, are you gonna ask your father?" Zura, who was unaware of Ethea’s situation, asked.
"...I’ll consider it."
"Hmm." Zura nodded, reading her emotions. "Then, let’s postpone your meeting with her till your parents leave. Is that ok with you?"
Soren nodded. "It’s fine with me. But we should take care of the other matters soon. Ryan is going to arrive in a few days."
"Of course," Zura nodded. "I’ll talk with the Vice-Principal as soon as I get back and notify you. In fact, you might get a chance to ’encounter’ your sister during your visit to the academy."

"That would be perfect." Soren allowed himself a small smile. Then his expression turned serious again. "One more thing. Does the academy have anyone who specializes in memory-related abilities? Someone who could examine her condition without causing any harm?"
"There are actually a few people. However..."

chapters.title: Chapter 324: The Best Couple
paragraphs: "However..." Zura hesitated, her expression turning cautious. "They’re not easy to approach. The academy keeps an eye on anyone with that kind of ability. Memory manipulation is a sensitive subject, and like any other nation, the Empire doesn’t take it lightly. If we request an examination without a solid reason, it might raise questions. And if the Valmeres catch wind of it, they’ll know something is up."
"...But there’s a way, right?" Ethea asked, eyeing Zura.

Zura sighed helplessly and answered. "There’s one person. An old professor who retired from the academy years ago. She still lives nearby and occasionally takes private cases, but she’s very selective about who she helps. She doesn’t like nobles, and she definitely doesn’t like people who try to use her for selfish reasons or political games. If we approach her the wrong way, she’ll turn us away without a second thought. But... If we can convince her, she might even help us for free."
"You aren’t talking about Grandma Kanie, are you?"
"The one and only."

Soren tilted his head in confusion. Noticing this, Zura clarified. "She visits the academy from time to time and has worked for over a hundred years. She holds the title of Honorary Elder, and she’s now over a hundred and twenty years old. She treats every student like her own grandchild, always bringing sweets and telling old stories. That’s how she earned the nickname Grandma Kanie."

"I see," Soren nodded, genuinely impressed. "She sounds like a remarkable person. A hundred years of service... not many can do that. And to still care for the students after all that time, she must truly love what she does."

"Indeed." Zura nodded proudly. "In fact, I am one of her students! ...Well, I only got to take one lesson from her, but it was unforgettable. She has a way of making you see things differently, you know."
"Then, we should definitely reach out to her." Soren leaned forward slightly. "Can you help us arrange a meeting?"
"That... I can’t help." Zura replied apologetically. "Although I know she lives in the Empire, possibly nearby, I don’t know her exact address. You’ll have to find her on your own."
"Alright. Thank you, Lady Zura. You’ve already helped us more than enough." Soren said sincerely. "And I think we’ve covered everything we needed to discuss."
Zura smiled and leaned back. "Then, should we finally order dinner? I’m starving."
Soren let out a small laugh and apologized. "Sorry for keeping you. Please, go ahead and order whatever you like. It’s on us."

Zura shook her head. "This time is my treat; you can cover next time." She grinned and smiled mischievously. "Besides, you’re not planning to make me work and then just say thanks, are you? That won’t do. I expect a proper meal once all of this is over. And I want it cooked personally by you."
"Fair enough." Soren smiled. "I promise to make it worth your while.
"Good." Zura picked up the menu and pressed the button to call the waiter. "Now, let’s order. I wasn’t kidding about starving."
Ethea and Soren chuckled at her words, and as the waiter arrived, they placed their orders. The food arrived soon, and the three of them ate while chatting about lighter topics.

Zura shared stories about her students and their past; Ethea talked about some of the places they had visited during their travels, and Soren occasionally added his own comments. For a while, the heavy subjects from earlier were set aside, and the dinner became a warm moment between the three.
Just as Soren reached for his teacup, a familiar voice echoed in his mind.
’Master.’
Soren paused before continuing. ’What is it, Malakor?’
’...I sensed a familiar presence nearby.’
Soren’s expression didn’t change, but his grip on the cup tightened slightly. ’Who is it?’
There was a brief pause before Malakor answered. ’...Your mother.’
’!’ Soren froze. It was only for a split second, but it was enough. His heart lurched, and a cold weight settled in his chest. He forced himself to breathe, to keep his expression neutral.
’...Is she alone?’ he asked.
’No. She is with your... father and... a teenage girl.’
Soren’s eyes widened. ’Could it be?!’
He quickly set the teacup down, a little harder than he intended, and the sound drew both Ethea and Zura’s attention.
"Excuse me," he said, standing up. "I’ll be back in a moment.
He didn’t wait for their responses and swiftly left the room.
Zura turned to Ethea, raising her brow. "What’s up with him?"
"...I’m not sure," Ethea replied, though her eyes lingered on the door with a hint of concern. She had seen the shift in his expression, however brief it was. Something had happened.
Zura studied her friend’s face for a moment, her sharp senses catching the undercurrent of worry. "You’re lying. You have a guess."
Ethea didn’t deny it. She simply folded her hands in her lap and kept her gaze on the door. "He’ll tell me once he returns."
Zura sighed and leaned back. "You two are really something else, you know that?"
Turning back to her, Ethea nodded with a smile, recalled something from yesterday, and said, "We’re the best."
"...The best couple, huh?" Zura’s lips twitched. "No need to rub it in. Some of us are still single, you know."
"..." Ethea merely smiled, not correcting her misunderstanding.

But on second thought, it might not be a misunderstanding at all. While they weren’t actually the best couple, she deeply wanted them to be. Not just in name, not just in convenience, but in every way that mattered.

She wanted to stand beside him as his equal, his partner, the one person he could always rely on. She wanted to hold his hand without hesitation, lean on him when she was tired, wake up beside him every morning, and know that he was hers and she was his. She wanted to share his joys and sorrows, his victories and failures, his fears and dreams.
In short, she wanted to build a happy life together, a life where she could love him freely and be loved in return, without hesitation or fear.
But...
’...I can’t tell her any of that yet. Not before I tell him first.’

chapters.title: Chapter 325: Long Awaited Reunion
paragraphs: As soon as he left the private room, Soren activated Pebble Among the Stars to the fullest. With Aura Suppression, it would be almost impossible for anyone to notice his presence unless they were an Emperor or higher-circle Awakened, or had powerful detection abilities.
With Malakor guiding him, he moved through the hallways like a ghost and soon arrived at the big main hall.
’They’re coming out,’ Malakor notified him, and a moment later, three people came out from the other side of the hall.
’...If I freeze up, snap me out of it.’
’Understood.’

A middle-aged man with black hair in a luxurious tuxedo walked on the left. Beside him was a beautiful woman in a red dress, her wavy red hair cascading over her shoulders. And between them, holding both their hands, was a teenage girl with vibrant crimson hair, smiling radiantly.
"!" Soren indeed froze, his eyes widening the moment he saw their faces.
’Master!’ Almost immediately, Malakor’s voice cut sharply through his mind, snapping him back to his senses.
He thanked Malakor and immediately activated Advanced Appraisal on each of them. However, he only read their names to confirm their identities.
They... They were indeed his parents. And the girl between them...
’Nura...’ He called out her name in his mind, a faint smile touching his lips.

This was the first time he had seen her since she was taken away. Watching her walk around with her usual bright smile, he felt the weight he had carried for so long finally begin to ease. He had long waited for this moment after all, even dreamed of it, and feared it might never come. Yet now that the moment was here, he found himself rooted to the spot, unable to move or speak.
"Father! Mother! Thank you! They were really delicious!"
Nura beamed as she spoke, still holding their hands. The man and the woman smiled back at her, their expressions warm and doting, the picture of a happy family.
Soren’s chest tightened.

He was happy for his little sister. Truly. She was alive, healthy, and happy. But hearing her call those two people "Father" and "Mother" with such affection, watching them act like loving parents after everything they had done... it made his blood run cold beneath the surface.

He could and did tolerate it when they mistreated him, but they really crossed the line with Nura. They made her childhood as miserable as his, nearly killed her with their stupid greed, and now here they were, pretending to be the perfect parents as if none of it had ever happened.
Soren let out a sigh and continued to observe the trio as they made their way to the exit.

He followed at a distance, keeping his presence hidden, and listened closely to their every word. Nura talked about the food and that she wanted to eat together again, her words full of energy and enthusiasm. The two responded with warm laughter, playing their roles flawlessly. Anyone watching would think they were a close, loving family.
Soren’s jaw tightened, but he kept his expression blank.

They reached the front gates, where a familiar black car was already waiting. Aldric, the same gray-haired butler who had delivered his disownment notice months ago, stood by the rear door. He bowed slightly and opened it for them.
"Thank you, Grandpa Aldric!" Nura waved at the old man before climbing in.
"My Lady." Aldric nodded with a small smile.
Sevrin and Melina followed, and soon the doors were closed. The car pulled away smoothly, disappearing down the street.
Soren watched until it was out of sight. Only then did he turn and head back inside.
As he walked back, he assessed their status one by one, starting with his father, Sevrin.
Name: Sevrin Valmere
Race: Human
Age: 56
Status: Healthy
Rank: 6th Circle (Early Stage)
Current Mana Level: 1,105,009
Mental State: Calculating, Satisfied, Conceited
Abilities: Veil of Deceit
Affinities: Wind (Grade 6 - A Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Exploitative, Prideful
Potential: 6th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: Low

’Hmm...’ He squinted as he scanned the lines. He didn’t expect Sevrin to have broken through to the 6th circle, but considering his greedy nature, there’s no way he hadn’t just asked for Nura’s artifact in that deal. However, given his low mana for a 6th circle, it was obvious he used potions and treasures instead of working hard himself.
’...I should be able to beat him easily once I learn how to fly too.’ Soren speculated.

Unfortunately, cultivators couldn’t fly until they reached the 6th circle. It was one of the major milestones that separated the strong from the truly powerful. But a few individuals, those with secret techniques or rare inheritances, could learn faster. Fortunately, Soren was one of them.
The Glacial Emperor Scripture included a 5-star technique called Frost Wings, which allowed the user to manifest wings of ice and take to the air. He just needed to reach the 5th circle to learn it.
However, if it didn’t involve flying, he was confident in his strength.

At his current level, a 4th circle, he could freely create weapons from his ice affinity with ease. With the Frost Armor technique and constitution, his defense was solid enough to withstand blows from most of the 6th circle opponents. But flight would change everything. It would give him greater mobility, escape options, and another advantage in battle.
In fact, had it not been for the Anti-Mana Zone, he wouldn’t have been able to defeat the Leech, as he could have easily flown out of reach and worn him down from a distance.
’...No point dwelling on that now.’ Soren shook his head and refocused on the status windows in front of him.

He only glanced at mental state for a moment before shifting to learn about Veil of Deceit. He already knew what his father would feel even without the status window. He just wanted to know if his ability was like his father-in-law’s.
’...Huff.’
Fortunately, it wasn’t.
Veil of Deceit was only a mental illusion that made others perceive Sevrin as trustworthy. It didn’t let him control anyone or fully hide his true persona, only deceive them.

Still, Soren could imagine how many people he had fooled over the years with this ability. Business partners, nobles, even family members. Anyone who wasn’t careful would take him at face value and never suspect a thing.
’...He must have used it on Nura and me too.’

sentences.text: As soon as he left the private room, Soren activated Pebble Among the Stars to the fullest.
With Aura Suppression, it would be almost impossible for anyone to notice his presence unless they were an Emperor or higher-circle Awakened, or had powerful detection abilities.
With Malakor guiding him, he moved through the hallways like a ghost and soon arrived at the big main hall.
’They’re coming out,’ Malakor notified him, and a moment later, three people came out from the other side of the hall.
’...If I freeze up, snap me out of it.’
’Understood.’
A middle-aged man with black hair in a luxurious tuxedo walked on the left.
Beside him was a beautiful woman in a red dress, her wavy red hair cascading over her shoulders.
And between them, holding both their hands, was a teenage girl with vibrant crimson hair, smiling radiantly.
"!" Soren indeed froze, his eyes widening the moment he saw their faces.
’Master!’ Almost immediately, Malakor’s voice cut sharply through his mind, snapping him back to his senses.
He thanked Malakor and immediately activated Advanced Appraisal on each of them.
However, he only read their names to confirm their identities.
They...
They were indeed his parents.
And the girl between them...
’Nura...’ He called out her name in his mind, a faint smile touching his lips.
This was the first time he had seen her since she was taken away.
Watching her walk around with her usual bright smile, he felt the weight he had carried for so long finally begin to ease.
He had long waited for this moment after all, even dreamed of it, and feared it might never come.
Yet now that the moment was here, he found himself rooted to the spot, unable to move or speak.
"Father!
Mother!
Thank you!
They were really delicious!"
Nura beamed as she spoke, still holding their hands.
The man and the woman smiled back at her, their expressions warm and doting, the picture of a happy family.
Soren’s chest tightened.
He was happy for his little sister.
Truly.
She was alive, healthy, and happy.

But hearing her call those two people "Father" and "Mother" with such affection, watching them act like loving parents after everything they had done... it made his blood run cold beneath the surface.
He could and did tolerate it when they mistreated him, but they really crossed the line with Nura.
They made her childhood as miserable as his, nearly killed her with their stupid greed, and now here they were, pretending to be the perfect parents as if none of it had ever happened.
Soren let out a sigh and continued to observe the trio as they made their way to the exit.
He followed at a distance, keeping his presence hidden, and listened closely to their every word.
Nura talked about the food and that she wanted to eat together again, her words full of energy and enthusiasm.
The two responded with warm laughter, playing their roles flawlessly.
Anyone watching would think they were a close, loving family.
Soren’s jaw tightened, but he kept his expression blank.
They reached the front gates, where a familiar black car was already waiting.
Aldric, the same gray-haired butler who had delivered his disownment notice months ago, stood by the rear door.
He bowed slightly and opened it for them.
"Thank you, Grandpa Aldric!" Nura waved at the old man before climbing in.
"My Lady." Aldric nodded with a small smile.
Sevrin and Melina followed, and soon the doors were closed.
The car pulled away smoothly, disappearing down the street.
Soren watched until it was out of sight.
Only then did he turn and head back inside.
As he walked back, he assessed their status one by one, starting with his father, Sevrin.

chapters.title: Chapter 326: Long Awaited Reunion [2]
paragraphs: Sighing, Soren continued, stopping briefly at the hidden traits. The names were enough to tell him everything he needed to know. However, he still checked them out of caution.
’...As expected, nothing noteworthy.’
Unsurprisingly, even the investment value was low. Soren guessed his father must have hit his potential, or it was because of his nature. There was one similar case before.
’...Right, it was Ziso Vale who had high risk, low return value.’
The Authority had likely marked him as a poor investment because his character flaws outweighed any potential benefit. Sevrin seemed to fall into the same category too.
’...Not that I ever planned to invest in him anyway.’
He dismissed this window and moved on to his mother’s status window.
Name: Melina Valmere
Race: Human
Age: 52
Status: Healthy
Rank: 4th Circle (Mid Stage)
Current Mana Level: 165,600
Mental State: Content, Watchful, Dismissive
Abilities: Water’s Embrace
Affinities: Water (Grade 6 - A Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Chronic Fatigue, Keen Awareness
Potential: 5th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: Moderate

’...’ Soren wasn’t surprised by his mother’s low cultivation despite having the potential to reach a higher circle. She spent seven years bedridden after giving birth to him. Not to mention how uninterested she was in cultivating.

She had always preferred comfort and luxury over hard work, relying on others to protect her while she enjoyed the benefits of her position. Training, fighting, growing stronger; none of it mattered to her. What mattered was maintaining her image and living without effort.
Soren had learned that about her long ago.
However, her mental state suggested something more.

She was content, probably because her act as a loving mother was working. Watchful, likely scanning for any threats or prying eyes that might disrupt their carefully crafted image. And dismissive, which could mean she had already written off anyone she deemed beneath her notice.
Nodding inwardly, he read her ability’s description.

Water’s Embrace allowed her to breathe and move freely in water, as well as see through it without obstruction. It also enhanced her regeneration when she was submerged or near water, allowing her to recover from injuries and fatigue at an accelerated rate. It was a passive ability too.
’...Not bad,’ he admitted. It was definitely useful, especially for someone with her condition.
’Wait.’ He paused at the thought. ’...Why did it take her so long to get healed then?’

If her ability enhanced regeneration near water, she could have recovered faster. The Valmere estate had a private hot spring and several enchanted baths. They could have used those or found favorable locations to help her recover. Yet she had spent seven years bedridden, and no one had thought to try.
Soren frowned.

Either she didn’t tell them about that part of her ability or she simply never bothered to learn. Considering her nature, the latter was more likely. She probably only knew she could breathe and see underwater and never questioned if there was more to it.
Sighing, he moved on to her hidden traits. His eyes lingered on the first one.

[Description: A condition that causes persistent exhaustion and low energy levels. The afflicted tire easily and need more rest than most. Physical and mental exertion wear them down faster, and recovery is slower than normal.]
’...Chronic Fatigue, huh.’

It somehow explained why she often seemed tired, why she spent a lot of time resting, why she avoided anything that required real effort. But it also made him wonder. Was this a condition she had before giving birth to him? Or was it something that developed after?

If she had it from the beginning, then it would make sense why the birth took such a heavy toll on her. A body already weakened by chronic fatigue would struggle to recover from something as strenuous as childbirth. But then... why didn’t it happen with his three older siblings? She had given birth before him without any issues. So what was different that time?
He thought about it but couldn’t find a plausible answer.

And if it was the latter, then his birth might have really triggered it. Perhaps the strain of labor had permanently damaged her body, which never fully healed. Perhaps he really was the cause, at least in part.
Soren shook his head. It didn’t matter. Even if he had been the cause of her condition, that didn’t justify what they, she, had done to him.
With that in mind, he quickly scanned the rest, closed it, and moved on to the last window.

[Mana Pathways: 81% functional]

- Fragile Vessel

[Amnesia: Partial Memory Loss]
[Details: Fragmented memories, identity confusion]
[Origin: ???]
[Estimated Survival Without Treatment: 4-5 years]

Affinities: Fire (Grade 8 - SS Rank), Light (Grade 7 - S Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Radiant Soul
Potential: 8th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: SUPREME

’...Her core and pathways are damaged too.’ Soren frowned as he read through the lines. The same went for her body. However, it was understandable, since she had endured the constant strain on her constitution for months before the artifact was provided. The good thing was he had already heard about it and prepared a solution.
’However, I have to practice first.’
Although he had the plan and the recipe, he hadn’t tried it yet, as he didn’t have the necessary ingredients. And...
’...I only have three chances.’

The ingredients were rare and difficult to obtain, which was why he had asked Lord Asad for help. Even with the city’s resources, gathering this much was already a miracle. That’s why he couldn’t afford to waste a single attempt. Worse still, he didn’t have a fire affinity, which would make the preparation even harder.
’I’ll think about it later,’ he decided, pushing the concern aside for now. There was no point worrying about it until he had a proper workspace and time to practice.
’Hmm...’ His gaze shifted to the affliction section. ’...As expected.’
Their earlier guess was correct. Someone had indeed messed with her memories. Unfortunately, the origin was unknown this time too.
’...At least she has more time to live.’

chapters.title: Chapter 327: Radiant Soul
paragraphs: Although 4-5 years was actually small compared to Ethea’s less-than-a-year deadline, it was still a relief. It meant they had more time to prepare, to find a proper cure, and to make sure everything was ready before they acted. They wouldn’t have to rush and risk making mistakes.
’...But we still need to move quickly.’

Four years could pass faster than expected. And if something went wrong, if the artifact was damaged or taken from her, her condition would worsen again. There were also the manipulative Valmeres. So, they couldn’t afford to be complacent.
He swiftly moved to the mental state line.
’Hmm... Cheerful, I understand. But why uneasy and doubtful?’
It didn’t make sense at first, since she had been smiling the whole time.
’...Uneasy, too, can be somehow explained by what I heard. But doubtful...’
What was she doubting? Herself or... did she sense something?

If Nura was really starting to suspect them, even a little, that was good. It meant she wasn’t completely blind to the truth. But it also meant she was confused and uncertain, which made her vulnerable. If they noticed her doubt, they would double their efforts to keep her under control.
’I need to reach her soon.’
With that in mind, he scrolled down to read the details of her ability, hoping to learn more about the Blazing Sun Constitution. But the moment he tried to access it, the information came back blank.
’...Of course.’ He sighed in disappointment and moved on to the affinities. ’Oh!’

He expected her fire affinity to be high, but seeing an S-Rank Light affinity really caught him off guard. Because Awakened individuals with light affinities were exceptionally rare, occurring perhaps once in a thousand or even less. They were also usually stronger than most, simply because light was so versatile. It could be used for healing, defense, offense, and even support. Many believed light was the most balanced element, able to adapt to any situation.
’If she has both fire and light, then her potential is even greater than I thought.’
Two made a truly powerful combination.
’...This must be another reason why they hid her so desperately.’
He shook his head and scrolled to the next section.
[Radiant Soul]

[Description: The soul radiates a gentle warmth that naturally draws others toward them. Those in their presence feel at ease, comforted, and uplifted. Prolonged exposure can create a sense of attachment and trust in those around the user.]
’!’ Soren’s eyes lit up. ’This... explains a lot.’

It matched what Zura had said about Nura making friends easily despite her amnesia and awkwardness. It also explained why Zura herself had taken such a quick liking to her, and his parents didn’t notice anything off about her. It was all because of this trait.

Of course, she herself had always been a warm and friendly child. Even without the trait, she had a way of making people feel comfortable around her. Coupled with her cute appearance and charming smile, it was no wonder people were drawn to her. But this trait amplified it all. It made her presence almost magnetic, pulling people in whether they realized it or not.
But...
That was exactly what worried him.

On the surface, it seemed like a wonderful trait. People would naturally want to be around her, help her, and so on. But the more he thought about it, the more uneasy he felt. A trait like this could be a double-edged sword. If the wrong people got close to her, they could become obsessed, possessive, or manipulative. They might even end up harming her just to keep her close.
’...No.’ Soren thought as he considered it more carefully. ’The effect shouldn’t be that powerful.’

He guessed that those with high willpower or strong mental defenses would be unaffected, or wouldn’t even notice. It was a subtle influence, not mind control after all. So, most trained Awakened would simply go about their day without realizing anything was different. It would probably only be dangerous to ordinary people or those already prone to obsession.
’...And fortunately, it’s Nura who has this trait.’
Because even if she knew she had this trait, she wouldn’t use it to manipulate or take advantage of others. That was just who she was.
’...Still, I’ll keep an eye on it.’
He quickly read the last two lines, then closed the window.
’...Did you put a mark on them?’
He asked as he slowly stood up from the chair near the entrance.
’Yes.’ Malakor replied.
’Good.’ Soren smiled and made his way back to their room. ’Tell me if they leave the city.’
’Understood.’ Malakor replied.
’...I hope they leave.’ Soren thought to himself. ’That will make things a lot easier.’
He arrived at their room, took a deep breath, and pushed the door open.
Ethea and Zura turned toward him immediately, curiosity clear on their faces.
"Sorry," Soren apologized and took his seat. However, a certain someone kept staring so intensely at him that he couldn’t help but ’notice’.
"I saw them." He revealed honestly. "My parents and Nura."
Ethea and Zura’s eyes widened at his words.
"They must have come for dinner too." Soren continued. "And I overheard that my parents are leaving tomorrow."
"That... That is a good thing, right?" Zura said after a moment. "You must have gotten to see your little sister and learned such crucial information."
Soren nodded at her, squeezing Ethea’s hand to ease her. "That’s right. And just like you said, she looked healthy and happy. However... I still have to meet her in person."
"Don’t worry about that. Since your parents are leaving, it won’t be that difficult now." Zura reassured him. "So, let’s continue to eat and not let the food go cold."
Soren nodded and picked up his spoon.
The rest of the dinner passed in the blink of an eye. Zura paid the bill as promised, and they left the Golden Deer. Then, they exchanged addresses and contact information.
"Take care, you two." Zura smiled, waving cheerfully. "I’ll contact you tomorrow."
"Mmm. See you tomorrow." Ethea nodded subtly.
"Thank you, Lady Zura. Have a good night." Soren waved back with a faint smile.
"Yeah, good night to you too!"
Soren and Ethea watched Zura go, then turned and made their way back to the hotel.

He quickly read the last two lines, then closed the window.
’...Did you put a mark on them?’
He asked as he slowly stood up from the chair near the entrance.
’Yes.’ Malakor replied.
’Good.’ Soren smiled and made his way back to their room. ’Tell me if they leave the city.’
’Understood.’ Malakor replied.
’...I hope they leave.’ Soren thought to himself. ’That will make things a lot easier.’
He arrived at their room, took a deep breath, and pushed the door open.
Ethea and Zura turned toward him immediately, curiosity clear on their faces.
"Sorry," Soren apologized and took his seat.
However, a certain someone kept staring so intensely at him that he couldn’t help but ’notice’.
"I saw them." He revealed honestly.
"My parents and Nura."
Ethea and Zura’s eyes widened at his words.
"They must have come for dinner too." Soren continued.
"And I overheard that my parents are leaving tomorrow."
"That...
That is a good thing, right?" Zura said after a moment.
"You must have gotten to see your little sister and learned such crucial information."
Soren nodded at her, squeezing Ethea’s hand to ease her.
"That’s right.
And just like you said, she looked healthy and happy.
However...
I still have to meet her in person."
"Don’t worry about that.
Since your parents are leaving, it won’t be that difficult now." Zura reassured him.
"So, let’s continue to eat and not let the food go cold."
Soren nodded and picked up his spoon.
The rest of the dinner passed in the blink of an eye.
Zura paid the bill as promised, and they left the Golden Deer.
Then, they exchanged addresses and contact information.
"Take care, you two." Zura smiled, waving cheerfully.
"I’ll contact you tomorrow."
"Mmm.
See you tomorrow." Ethea nodded subtly.
"Thank you, Lady Zura.
Have a good night." Soren waved back with a faint smile.
"Yeah, good night to you too!"
Soren and Ethea watched Zura go, then turned and made their way back to the hotel.

chapters.title: Chapter 328: Investment Detected... [3]
paragraphs: Soren and Ethea returned to the hotel, and after helping Ethea bathe and change clothes, he laid her down on the bed. Ethea, as usual, went into her soul space to cultivate. As for Soren, he had received an investment notification earlier but saved it for later since he was outside touring with Ethea before dinner.
And now, it was finally time to check it.
After entering the bathroom and getting into the bathtub, he quickly summoned his status and accessed the latest message.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Bagdad City]
[Analyzing Investment...]

[Investment: You helped expose the Outcasts’ plot and prevented a political crisis between the Empire and the elves. You played a decisive role in neutralizing their forces, protecting key figures including Princess Roya and Chef Nuelia, and ensuring the festival could end without further bloodshed. You also won the championship while representing the city.]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the city of Bagdad has been spared from catastrophe. The city’s leadership, including Lord Asad, holds you in the highest regard and considers you the savior of Bagdad. The people may not know your name, but the city’s collective gratitude has taken root. Thanks to your actions, the city’s reputation and future remained intact.]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: MYTHIC]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Constitution Evolution: Everfrost Tyrant Body (A-Rank) → Glacial Emperor Constitution (S-Rank)]
[2. Ability Evolution: Core Purge (A-Rank) → Core Refinement (S-Rank)]
[3. Ability Unlocked: Civic Insight]
[4. Ability Unlocked: Beacon of Hope]
[5. Cooking Mastery +2]
[6. Memory Crystal x10]
[7. Gate Key Fragment]
[8. +50,000 Mana/Mana Capacity]
[9. +10,000 Mental Power/Mental Power Capacity]
[Integration initiated...]
Soren closed his eyes as the integration began.

The temperature dropped to a biting cold in an instant. Frost crept along the rim of the bathtub, spreading outward in thin, spiderweb patterns. A layer of ice coated the porcelain beneath him, thickening as the cold radiated from his body.

His muscles grew denser, fibers reinforcing themselves as his physique underwent a fundamental shift. His bones also evolved, becoming more resilient. The mana pathways improved greatly as well, enabling energy to flow more easily and quickly. His skin paled, taking on a faint, translucent quality like polished marble touched by winter. The veins beneath became faintly visible, carrying a soft blue glow that pulsed with his heartbeat.
Then the change reached his core.

The liquid mana he already possessed grew denser, each drop becoming more potent than before. At the same time, the remaining mana began to condense, joining the liquid pool at a faster rate than his normal cultivation would allow. The core itself expanded slightly, making room for more energy as its capacity increased. The protective barrier surrounding it thickened and reinforced itself, strengthening its defense against external interference.

His thoughts grew clearer and sharper, as if a fog he hadn’t even noticed had lifted. His mental defenses strengthened, and his perception of the world around him deepened. It was as if his mind and body were finally aligning, each reinforcing the other.
And finally, new knowledge flooded in.

Recipes, insights, and understanding poured into his consciousness. He saw the Glacial Emperor Constitution in his mind’s eye, its structure, its potential, and its limits. He understood Core Refinement, how it worked, and how to use it. The concepts of Civic Insight and Beacon of Hope settled into his thoughts.
Time passed with minutes feeling like hours.
[Integration Complete!]
Soren slowly opened his eyes.

The world came into focus with startling clarity, every detail sharper than before, from the faintest crack in the ceiling to the half-frozen dust particles floating in the air. His senses stretched outward without effort, encompassing the entire hotel room, then the hotel itself, then the street outside, until he could feel the presence of every person and every living thing within a wide radius.
’...Not bad.’ He thought to himself and recalled how far his senses used to reach before. This was at least twice as wide, maybe more.
He then blinked and looked around.
The whole bathroom was covered in ice. It coated the walls, the floor, the ceiling, and even his own body. A thick layer had formed around him, encasing his arms and legs like frozen armor.
’Let’s see...’

He stared at it for a moment, then the ice on his body began to crack. Thin lines spread across the surface, and then the whole layer shattered into countless tiny fragments. They hung in the air for a heartbeat before dissolving into snow that drifted downward without a sound.
Smiling, Soren raised his hand.

The ice coating the bathroom responded immediately. It receded like a tide, pulling back from the walls, the floor, and the ceiling, gathering into a single point above his palm. The sphere of frost spun slowly, condensing and compacting until it was nothing more than a small bead of water. He flicked his wrist, and the bead vanished into vapor, leaving the bathroom almost exactly as it had been before.
"...Amazing." He stared at his palm for a moment, flexing his fingers. Manipulating ice had always taken focus and effort before, yet now it responded as easily as breathing.
’Master,’ Malakor’s voice echoed in his mind immediately. ’Did you break through?’
Soren let out a short laugh. ’Something like that. My constitution advanced a little.’
’Congratulations then, Master.’ Malakor replied, a hint of genuine respect in his tone. After all, he witnessed everything with his own eyes. There’s no way this was just a ’little advancement’.
’Thank you.’

Soren stepped out of the bathtub and started filling it with water to wash away the snow and the impurities that had been expelled from his body during the integration. He watched as the magic bathtub did its work, the enchanted surface repelling dirt and grime on its own. Within moments, it looked as clean as it had been before he ever stepped inside.
’By the way, how is Ethea?’
’She is still sleeping,’ Malakor answered. ’You don’t have to worry. I sealed the whole room, so nothing from in here leaked outside.’
’You’re reliable as always,’ Soren chuckled, reassured. ’...You can rest now. I’ll take a shower and cultivate today.’
’...Understood.’

chapters.title: Chapter 329: What An Evolution...
paragraphs: After showering and changing clothes, Soren checked on Ethea and left the bedroom. In the living room, he took out a laptop, put it on the table, and sat down on the sofa.
But before getting into work, he decided to thoroughly check the returns. The first one was obviously the physical evolution. And man, what an evolution it was.

The passive alone was incredible. It was called Glacial Essence, and aside from the massive physical strength, it granted him immunity to cold and ice, and high resistance to most elements, especially water. In fact, it could be said he gained an affinity for water too, since he could now manipulate it to a certain extent, freezing it, shaping it, or turning it into mist with barely a thought. And of course, there was complete control over ice itself.
There were other benefits as well.

His health and mana regeneration doubled in normal environments and increased fivefold in cold environments. He wouldn’t feel any fatigue from cold either, no matter how low the temperature dropped. In fact, the colder it was, the more comfortable he felt.
’And it’s not just the outside,’ he thought. ’My heart, mind, skin, bones, muscles, blood, lungs, pathways... everything has been changed. I’m basically built for cold now.’
And again, all of it was just passive, the foundation of the constitution.

The active effects were where things got interesting. Unlike his other S-rank abilities, he couldn’t use the Glacial Emperor Constitution right away in its entirety. It had layers. The passive, as he thought, was the foundation layer. The active effects, however, unlocked progressively as he advanced through the circles.

Fortunately, he was already at the 4th circle. That meant the full passive had been integrated immediately, along with two active effects. The first was a carryover from his previous constitution, the frost armor that absorbed and reflected damage. The evolution enhanced it, making it capable of storing more energy and releasing it in a single devastating burst, or repairing and reinforcing the armor to extend its duration.
The second was entirely new, called Frozen Moment.

Once per day, he could freeze time briefly within a small radius. However, it wasn’t true time manipulation, just a flash-freeze so intense that it momentarily stopped all movement. But in that heartbeat, he could act freely, and usually it would be more than enough to turn the tide of a battle.

The rest of the effects were amazing too. Once he reached the 5th circle, he would unlock Winter’s Rebirth, which would allow him to recover from a critical injury, even near-death, once he unlocked all the effects. However, it had a month-long cooldown, so he had to be mindful when it triggered. It wasn’t something he could rely on in every fight.

At the 6th circle, there was Glacial Sovereign. He could summon a massive construct of ice, shaped like a giant or a beast, that would fight alongside him and obey his commands. Its strength would scale with his mana and mastery.
And finally, at the 7th circle, there was the Glacial Emperor’s Domain.

Soren wondered whether he could use a domain within a domain if he reached the 7th circle, but he quickly set the thought aside. There was still a long way to go till the 7th circle. Knowing what ’rewards’ were waiting for him was enough for now, as it would motivate him to work harder.
However, he learned something useful from this evolution.
If his constitution was like this, did that mean other S-rank and higher constitutions also came with layers and unlockable effects?
’...It seems like I have to research them more.’

With that in mind, he recalled the contents of Core Refinement. The ability had evolved from Core Purge, which had originally allowed him to purge foreign mana and toxins from his body. Now, it could purify harmful substances and convert them into usable energy. Poisons, curses, foreign mana... all of it could be refined and absorbed rather than simply expelled.
’This is perfect for dealing with people like Leech,’ he thought. ’Or anyone who tries to poison me or mess with my mana.’

The ability also worked on his own mana, purifying any impurities that accumulated during cultivation. More importantly, his core would now passively liquefy the mana over time. Since reaching the 5th circle required fully liquefying his mana, this would save him years of effort and smooth out his progress. Combined with his new constitution, his body was becoming a fortress that was nearly impossible to bring down from the inside.
He was more than satisfied with the evolution.
Next were Civic Sight and Beacon of Hope. They were more like Advanced Appraisal and Guardian’s Resolve, requiring no energy to use.

Civic Insight allowed him to sense the general well-being of a community or large group of people. It wasn’t mind-reading, though. It was more like feeling the collective mood of a population. He could tell if a city was thriving, struggling, or on the verge of unrest. It would be useful for understanding the places he visited and the people he interacted with.

Beacon of Hope was a passive aura that uplifted the spirits of allies within range. Those fighting alongside him would feel less fatigue and recover slightly faster. This would come in handy when leading a group or protecting others. It was kind of flashy, but in long battles or desperate situations, even a small boost could make the difference between victory and defeat.
’...And then comes cooking.’ He squinted. ’...If I get two more cooking mastery returns, I am certain that I can easily become a Senior Magic Chef.’
His insights and understanding of cooking had improved greatly. He could now tell where he had made mistakes during the competition and where he could have made better decisions.
’...Should I wait for Ethea’s investment returns before practicing the new recipes?’ He pondered and decided to think about it later. ’Let’s see...’
He opened his mental inventory and pulled out a Memory Crystal. According to its description, it could store a perfect memory of any single event, letting the user record and replay it at will.
The crystal was small and easily fit in the palm of his hand. He turned it over a few times, thinking about what to use it for.

’This could be useful for keeping records of important moments. Or for sharing memories with others.’ He thought. ’After all, saving them on a phone might be dangerous since they could be hacked or stolen.’
He put it back in the inventory and pulled out another item.

It was the Gate Key Fragment. A small, jagged piece of unknown dark metal, cool to the touch. Faint runes flickered along its surface, pulsing with a soft glow. According to its description, it could open a temporary portal to any location he had previously visited. However, it was a one-time-use item.
’An emergency escape route.’ He stared deeply at it. ’Or a way to get somewhere fast if we ever need to.’
He put it back in the inventory to keep it safe. He would save it for when the situation called for it.

’And the last two returns were mana, mental power, and their capacity improvements.’ He recalled the numbers. His mana had increased by fifty thousand, and his mental power by ten thousand. Both were significant boosts.
He summoned his status window to see the changes.
[PERSONAL INFORMATION]
Name: Soren Everly
Age: 23
Circle Rank: Fourth Circle (Late Stage)
Mental Cultivation: Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture — Stage 2: Soul Tempered Core Stage
Potential: ???
Hunter Rank: C
[CORE STATUS]
Mana Capacity: 459,860 / 650,000
Mental Power Capacity: 109740 / 160000
Core Stability: Stable
Pathway Integrity: Excellent
Affinity: Ice (Grade 7 - S Rank) | Wind (Grade 5 - B Rank) | Life Force (Grade 5 - B Rank) Darkness (Sealed) | ??? | ???
[INNATE ABILITIES]
• Hyper Regeneration (S-Rank)
• Glacial Emperor Constitution (S-Rank)
• Sovereign’s Fortitude (S-Rank)
• Limit Break (S-Rank)
• Indomitable Soul (S-Rank)
• Overlord’s Aura (A-Rank)
• Fire Resistance (C-Rank)
• Vital Harmony (A-Rank)
• Nature’s Eyes (B-Rank)
• Core Refinement (S-Rank)
[SPECIAL ABILITIES]
• Civic Sight
• Beacon of Hope
[UNIQUE ABILITIES]
[TECHNIQUES & SKILLS]
• Cooking Mastery (Advanced Lv. 9)*
Once he scanned them, only one word came to his mind.
’...Monstrous.’

His mana jumped over four hundred and fifty thousand, and his mental power was already over a hundred thousand. For a 4th circle, those numbers were absurd. Most 4th circle Awakened barely had a fraction of that. Even 5th circle cultivators would struggle to match him now.
After grinning for a bit, he dismissed all the windows and leaned back on the sofa.
’At this rate, reaching the 5th circle and 3rd stage in mental cultivation won’t take nearly as long as I thought.’
As long as he kept working hard and getting returns like these, he could easily break through by the time they reached the Tower.
He clenched his fists, determination settling into his chest. There was still much to do, but for the first time in a long while, the path ahead felt clear.
’One step at a time.’ He told himself. ’And soon, I’ll be strong enough to protect everyone I care about.’

• Core Refinement (S-Rank)
[SPECIAL ABILITIES]
• Civic Sight
• Beacon of Hope
[UNIQUE ABILITIES]
[TECHNIQUES & SKILLS]
• Cooking Mastery (Advanced Lv.
Once he scanned them, only one word came to his mind.
’...Monstrous.’
His mana jumped over four hundred and fifty thousand, and his mental power was already over a hundred thousand.
For a 4th circle, those numbers were absurd.
Most 4th circle Awakened barely had a fraction of that.
Even 5th circle cultivators would struggle to match him now.
After grinning for a bit, he dismissed all the windows and leaned back on the sofa.
’At this rate, reaching the 5th circle and 3rd stage in mental cultivation won’t take nearly as long as I thought.’
As long as he kept working hard and getting returns like these, he could easily break through by the time they reached the Tower.
He clenched his fists, determination settling into his chest.
There was still much to do, but for the first time in a long while, the path ahead felt clear.
’One step at a time.’ He told himself. ’And soon, I’ll be strong enough to protect everyone I care about.’

chapters.title: Chapter 330: Be Yourself and Listen to Your Heart
paragraphs: Soren took a few minutes to process everything and rest his mind. It also allowed him to rein in his overflowing confidence and steady himself. Getting stronger was good, but he couldn’t let it go to his head. Overconfidence had killed more Awakened than weakness ever had.
Once he felt calm and centered, he opened his laptop and got to work.
"Let’s see..." He whispered as he typed into the search bar. The results popped up almost instantly, and he clicked on the first article.
[How to Plan the Perfect Date: A Complete Guide]
He read through the tips, nodding occasionally.
’Locations matter... Consider her interests... Make sure the atmosphere is comfortable... Have a backup plan in case something goes wrong... Don’t overthink it, but don’t be careless either...’
He noted down the useful parts, then opened another article, then another. He furrowed his brows at some while smiling at others. Still, he could say one thing with confidence.
’...This is more complicated than I thought.’

And he knew the reason why. While he had some knowledge of romance and dating, it all came from the movies, TV shows, cartoons, and stories he read and watched. The problem was that almost all of them were fictional. They were designed to be dramatic rather than practical and mostly showed the process rather than the planning. So he couldn’t rely on them. However, he could always take inspiration from them.
He just needed to filter out the ridiculous or impractical parts and focus on what would actually work for them.
With that in mind, he kept going.

There were useful ones like ’10 First Date Ideas That Actually Work’, ’Signs She’s Interested: A Practical Guide’, ’Quiet and Romantic Date Ideas for Introverts’, ’What to Talk About on Your First Date’, and ’Why a Simple Walk Can Be the Best Date?’. He learned a few useful things from them.

However, there were also ridiculous ones like ’Confess with a Flash Mob’, ’Grand Gestures That Always Work’, ’How to Win Her Heart in 24 Hours’, and ’The Alpha’s Guide to Dominating a Date’. He dismissed each one without a second thought.

And then there were the... unethical ones. ’How to Manipulate Her Into Saying Yes’, ’Tricks to Make Her Fall for You’, ’Playing Hard to Get’, and ’The Art of Guilt-Tripping’. He dismissed them without hesitation as well, his jaw tightening each time. ’Who would even see this?’

But seeing the high number of views and comments, he realized a lot of people actually did. The thought left a bitter taste in his mouth. If this was the kind of advice people were getting, no wonder so many relationships were a mess.
In his opinion, even those strange titles he saw were better than these. At least they were honest about being ridiculous and somewhat useful too.

’Confess During a Monster Attack: A Love Story’ was absurd, but it wasn’t manipulative. ’Why Fighting a Dragon Together Is the Best First Date’ was impractical, but it made him wonder if the author was an emperor, since he could fight dragons on a date. Right, speaking of an emperor, there was a weird title called ’Love Tips from the Emperor of Darkness’.
He stared at that one for a moment, then clicked on it out of sheer curiosity.
The first lines read: "Step one: Conquer her kingdom. Step two: Claim her as your bride. Step three: Rule together in eternal darkness."
Soren closed the tab immediately.
’...Some things are better left unread.’
He ignored the absurd amount of views but took a peek at the comments. And... regretted it.
’Urgh, I won’t do it again.’ He shook his head and continued researching.
Once he was sure he learned enough about how to plan a date and what to do, he started researching how to confess.

The first one that came up was called ’How to Confess Your Feelings: 10 Tips for a Successful Confession,’ and it had some useful tips. He noted down these four: Pick the right moment, be honest and sincere, don’t pressure her for an answer, and respect her feelings no matter what.

He read a few more articles, but most repeated the same advice. Pick a good location, keep it simple, don’t overthink it, and be confident but not arrogant. They were all reasonable, but none of them really stuck with him.

There was one video that he really liked called ’Bring Your Story to Life: Confessions Inspired by What You Love’. The host was an older woman with a warm voice, and she talked about using inspiration from things you already love. Books, games, movies, stories, or even poems. She said that while most of those might seem impossible in real life, you could always adjust them to fit your situation. The key was to make it personal and meaningful, something that reflected who you were and what you felt.

As she spoke, Soren’s mind drifted. Without meaning to, he recalled his favorite animated movie: Last Dragon Rider. Near the end, the main character confessed his love to the heroine, his fiancée, while riding on his dragon’s back, soaring through the clouds at sunset. The sky was painted in shades of gold and pink, and the wind carried their laughter as they flew higher and higher. It was one of his favorite scenes.
’...Something like that.’
He didn’t have a dragon or know how to fly, but the feeling of that scene, the intimacy, the sense of freedom and connection, was what he wanted.
He finished the video, watched a few more videos from her channel, and found out she also wrote articles. He read some of them, and one caught his eye with just the title.
’Be Yourself and Listen to Your Heart.’

He clicked on it and started reading. The article itself was short. It just said the best confessions come from honesty and from genuinely knowing the other person. Trying to be someone else or following a step-by-step plan would only make things feel forced. It said the most important thing was to speak from the heart and trust that the other person would understand.
’Be myself, huh...’
He closed his eyes and leaned back.
’...I think I know what to do.’

chapters.title: Chapter 331: The Valmere Concern
paragraphs: "Huff..."

Sevrin stepped out of the bathroom, a towel draped around his shoulders and his hair still damp. He walked to his bed and reached for the hair dryer. However, before he could turn it on, he noticed a new message notification on his phone. He frowned and picked it up.
[Aldric: My Lord, please call when you’re free.]
Sevrin stared at the message for a moment. Aldric knew better than to bother him at this hour unless something important had come up.
He tapped the call button and waited.
"...My Lord," Aldric’s voice came through after two rings. "I apologize for disturbing you at this hour."
"It’s fine. What is the matter?"
"It would be better if we spoke in person, My Lord. I’ve discovered something important... related to him."
Sevrin raised a brow. "Him?"
"Yes. I would rather not say more over the phone."
Sevrin paused, then nodded. "Alright. Come to my room in ten minutes."
"Understood."

The call ended. Sevrin stared at the phone for a moment, then set it down and picked up the hair dryer. Whatever Aldric had found, it was enough to make him cautious. That alone was worth paying attention to.
Ten minutes later.
Sevrin sat on the sofa in the living area of his suite, a glass of wine in his hand. Aldric stood before him, posture straight, expression neutral as always.
"Speak," Sevrin muttered, taking a sip.
Aldric reached into his coat and pulled out a small tablet. He tapped the screen twice and held it out for Sevrin to see.
"Please look at this, My Lord."
The screen displayed two headlines. The first read: "Bagdad’s Savior: The Mysterious Chef Who Turned the Tide." The second read: "Golden Ladle Champion: The Dark Horse of Bagdad.
Sevrin frowned.
"Hmm?"

The face in the photo didn’t ring any bells at first. But as he kept looking, a strange sense of familiarity crept in. Something about the eyes, or the shape of the jaw, reminded him of someone he knew. Someone he hadn’t seen in a long time.
’He reminds me of...!’ His eyes widened, and he straightened on the sofa, nearly spilling his wine. He looked at Aldric, then back at the photo, then back at Aldric again.
"...Is this Soren?" he asked, his voice doubtful.
Aldric hesitated before replying. "The person’s name is indeed Soren, My Lord. However... his surname is Everly."
"Everly?" Sevrin frowned deeper. "Is this his new surname?"
"...I’m not sure," Aldric replied. "As you ordered before, we withdrew surveillance on him after the wedding. Since he was expelled from the family, you said he was no longer our concern."
Sevrin’s jaw tightened, but he said nothing.

"I tried contacting our people in Kalmira, but they couldn’t provide anything useful," Aldric continued. "And... I did some research on this person. He seems to be from Bagdad City since he represented it in the Golden Ladle Championship during the Empire’s annual Harvest Festival..." Aldric explained everything he had managed to uncover. And stopped at him winning the championship.
Sevrin listened in silence, his eyes narrowing.
"...An expert-level magic chef? And he won the championship?" He muttered the words slowly, as if tasting them. "That doesn’t sound like the Soren I remember."

Aldric nodded in agreement. "...He was unawakened when I went to deliver the disownment notice. And even if he somehow awakened, it would be impossible for him to change this much in just three months, let alone become an Expert Magic Chef capable of defeating Senior Magic Chefs and winning the championship."
"So... Are they different people then or not?" Sevran asked with growing irritation. "Didn’t you investigate this guy’s background?"

"We tried to, but we couldn’t," Aldric replied, taking on a solemn expression. "His records are sealed. Someone with significant authority has restricted access to his information. Every time we tried to dig deeper, we hit a wall. The only thing we managed to confirm is that he is now seriously injured due to the incident and will take at least three months to recover."
Aldric tapped the tablet and switched to another message posted by the Bagdad City’s personal channel.

"...Injured, huh?" Sevrin chuckled mockingly as he read the post. "Since it’s the official channel that posted this, it must be true. And since he won the championship representing their city, it’s likely they’re the ones protecting his information.
Aldric nodded in agreement. "What should we do then, My Lord?"

Sevrin pondered for a moment, his fingers tapping against the armrest. "While they seem like different people, we still need to be sure. Send more people to probe and investigate. Increase the watch on the academy as well. I want a record of everyone who enters and leaves, no exceptions. And send someone capable to Kalmira. I want a full report on his situation, dead or alive."
"Understood, My Lord." Aldric bowed slightly and, after a pause, added. "Should I cancel the trip back home?"
Sevrin paused, then shook his head. "No. Work is already piling up, and I can’t stay here any longer. But..." He glanced toward the other bedroom door. "Just in case, Melina stays here."
"Understood." Aldric bowed once more. "Then I will take my leave."
Sevrin waved a hand dismissively and picked up his wine glass. However, he froze as if recalling something important. "W-Wait!"
"Postpone sending people to Kalmira for now," Sevrin said, his tone shifting. "I’ll give you further instructions myself later."
"Understood. I will await your orders."
"Good. You may go."

Aldric bowed and took his leave, gently closing the door behind him. Sevrin stared at the closed door for a long moment, his wine glass still in hand. Then he let out a slow breath and leaned back on the sofa.

He then put the glass down and picked up his phone again. After hesitating for a moment, he typed ’Lord Darius’ into the search bar. His finger hovered over the call button, trembling slightly. He pressed it before he could change his mind.
The line rang five times before connecting.
Sevrin immediately straightened in his seat and spoke with uncharacteristic respect. "Lord Darius, I apologize for disturbing you at this hour. This is Sevrin, Sevrin Valmere."
A brief pause followed on the other end before a friendly voice replied.
"Ah, Mr. Valmere. It’s been a while..."
