chapters.title: Chapter 332: Preparations
paragraphs: "What’s the matter?" Darius asked. "Is there some kind of problem?"
"N-No, my lord!" Sevrin hurriedly replied. "It’s just... something came up that I wanted to inform you about. I thought you should know since it is somewhat related to you."
There was a pause on the other end. "...Go on."

Sevrin took a breath and explained what he had discovered. That there was a chef from Bagdad, the one who had won the Golden Ladle Championship yesterday, whose name was Soren Everly and who resembled his disowned son, and so forth.
He kept his tone respectful and measured, careful not to sound like he was wasting his time.
However, the voice sounded totally uninterested. "So...?"
"Ahem. I-I was just worried if they are the same person..." Sevrin trailed off, sure that Lord Darius understood what he was implying.
If they were indeed the same person and reached that status, not only would the Valmere be in trouble, but the Morvain would be affected as well. After all, it involved their ’precious’ young lady.
"...I can assure you that they are completely different," Darius replied indifferently. "And I hope you won’t disturb me with such trivial matters again."
"Yes, my lord. I understand. I apologize for disturbing you." Sevrin said quickly, keeping his voice steady despite the unease crawling up his spine. "Goodnight, Lord Darius."
"Goodnight, Mr. Valmere."
The line went dead.

Sevrin lowered the phone and stared at the screen for a long moment. His frown deepened as he replayed the conversation in his mind. ’Completely different.’ What exactly did that mean? Different people? Or the same person who had changed so much that he was unrecognizable?

He wanted to believe it was the former. That would be easier and more logical. But Darius wasn’t the type to say things without meaning. The casual dismissal, the word ’trivial,’ the way he had cut the conversation short without a second thought. It all felt deliberate, as if he knew more than he was willing to share.
’No... If Lord Darius says it’s trivial, then it’s trivial.’ He set the phone down and picked up his almost empty wine glass, draining it in one go. ’I won’t offend him by digging further.’
He picked up his phone again and sent Aldric a quick message.
[Cancel the Kalmira investigation. Focus on the academy and the city.]

He then put the phone down and leaned back on the sofa, closing his eyes. He still harbored the suspicion deep within his heart, but he chose not to act on it. Not until he had enough proof and power.

Fortunately, his ticket to rise was already secured. As long as he made sure nothing went wrong, the Valmere family would soon rise into the ranks of grand noble families like the Morvains. Maybe then, he wouldn’t always have to bow his head and behave like a damn dog around them.
He clenched his fists, then slowly relaxed them.
’No... I shouldn’t let my emotions cloud my judgment.’ He took a deep breath and exhaled, letting the tension drain from his shoulders.

Darius Morvain was a veteran, a ruthless man who survived decades in the cutthroat world of politics. Offending him would be the height of foolishness. Even thinking he could stand as his equal was premature.
’...One step at a time.’
He opened his eyes and glanced toward the window. The city lights flickered in the distance.
’First, the ticket’s success. Only then can we think about other things.’

In an unknown barren land, a man sat atop the corpse of a massive dragon. Its scales were black as night, and its body stretched across the wasteland like a fallen mountain. The man put his phone back in his pocket and gazed at the horizon.
’Master,’ a voice echoed in his mind. ’Why didn’t you tell him the truth directly?’
The man smiled faintly.
’What do you mean? I told him the truth.’ He leaned back on his hands and watched the clouds drift by. ’Heiscompletely different from his past self.’
’Besides,’ the man continued, ’even without my intervention, they’re bound to cross paths soon. I want to see how he handles it this time. And if he fails... well, that will be interesting too.’
’Keke, you are as mischievous as ever, Master~’
The man merely smiled, neither denying nor confirming.
’Anyway, let’s continue. We have to set the stage for what’s coming. There’s still much to do before the real game begins.’

With that, he stood up and dusted off his coat. The dragon’s corpse beneath him began to dissolve into particles of black light, fading into the void. Soon, nothing remained but the barren land and the man walking toward the horizon.
"Hmm...
Ethea’s eyes fluttered open. The morning light filtered through the curtains, casting a warm glow across the room. She blinked a few times, adjusting to the brightness, and turned her head.
Soren was already awake, sitting on the edge of the bed beside her. He smiled the moment he saw her eyes open.
"Good morning."
"Good morning," she murmured, her voice still soft with sleep.
"Did you sleep well?"
"Mm. I did."
"Good. Then let me help you..."

They went through their usual morning routine. Soren helped her wash up, brush her teeth, and change into fresh clothes. Today, however, he didn’t pick something random from her wardrobe. Instead, he walked over to the closet and pulled out a beautiful white dress.
It was the one he had picked for her before during their shopping. And it was actually Ethea’s request that he choose it.
"This one?" he asked, holding it up.
Ethea nodded. "Yes."

He helped her into it, carefully adjusting the fabric and smoothing out the wrinkles. The dress fit her as perfectly as before, its soft white folds cascading over her wheelchair like fresh snow. She looked elegant and ethereal, like something out of a fairy tale.
Soren stepped back a few paces and observed her, a gentle smile forming on his lips.
"You look beautiful."
"Thank you." Ethea smiled back. "Now, it’s your turn."
"Eh?" Soren blinked, caught off guard.
"Your clothes," she clarified, gesturing toward the closet. "I want to pick them for you."

"Oh, right, of course!" Soren nodded and glanced down at his simple shirt and trousers. They were comfortable and practical, but they weren’t exactly date material. Good thing she reminded him, or he might have forgotten it. "Alright, what do you have in mind?"

sentences.text: "What’s the matter?" Darius asked.
"Is there some kind of problem?"
"N-No, my lord!" Sevrin hurriedly replied.
"It’s just... something came up that I wanted to inform you about.
I thought you should know since it is somewhat related to you."
There was a pause on the other end.
"...Go on."
Sevrin took a breath and explained what he had discovered.
That there was a chef from Bagdad, the one who had won the Golden Ladle Championship yesterday, whose name was Soren Everly and who resembled his disowned son, and so forth.
He kept his tone respectful and measured, careful not to sound like he was wasting his time.
However, the voice sounded totally uninterested.
"Ahem.
I-I was just worried if they are the same person..." Sevrin trailed off, sure that Lord Darius understood what he was implying.
If they were indeed the same person and reached that status, not only would the Valmere be in trouble, but the Morvain would be affected as well.
After all, it involved their ’precious’ young lady.
"...I can assure you that they are completely different," Darius replied indifferently.
"And I hope you won’t disturb me with such trivial matters again."
"Yes, my lord.
I understand.
I apologize for disturbing you." Sevrin said quickly, keeping his voice steady despite the unease crawling up his spine.
"Goodnight, Lord Darius."
"Goodnight, Mr.
Valmere."
The line went dead.
Sevrin lowered the phone and stared at the screen for a long moment.
His frown deepened as he replayed the conversation in his mind. ’Completely different.’ What exactly did that mean?
Different people?
Or the same person who had changed so much that he was unrecognizable?
He wanted to believe it was the former.
That would be easier and more logical.
But Darius wasn’t the type to say things without meaning.
The casual dismissal, the word ’trivial,’ the way he had cut the conversation short without a second thought.
It all felt deliberate, as if he knew more than he was willing to share.
If Lord Darius says it’s trivial, then it’s trivial.’ He set the phone down and picked up his almost empty wine glass, draining it in one go. ’I won’t offend him by digging further.’
He picked up his phone again and sent Aldric a quick message.
[Cancel the Kalmira investigation.
Focus on the academy and the city.]
He then put the phone down and leaned back on the sofa, closing his eyes.
He still harbored the suspicion deep within his heart, but he chose not to act on it.
Not until he had enough proof and power.
Fortunately, his ticket to rise was already secured.
As long as he made sure nothing went wrong, the Valmere family would soon rise into the ranks of grand noble families like the Morvains.
Maybe then, he wouldn’t always have to bow his head and behave like a damn dog around them.
He clenched his fists, then slowly relaxed them.
I shouldn’t let my emotions cloud my judgment.’ He took a deep breath and exhaled, letting the tension drain from his shoulders.
Darius Morvain was a veteran, a ruthless man who survived decades in the cutthroat world of politics.
Offending him would be the height of foolishness.
Even thinking he could stand as his equal was premature.
’...One step at a time.’
He opened his eyes and glanced toward the window.
The city lights flickered in the distance.
’First, the ticket’s success.
Only then can we think about other things.’
In an unknown barren land, a man sat atop the corpse of a massive dragon.
Its scales were black as night, and its body stretched across the wasteland like a fallen mountain.
The man put his phone back in his pocket and gazed at the horizon.
’Master,’ a voice echoed in his mind. ’Why didn’t you tell him the truth directly?’
The man smiled faintly.
’What do you mean?
I told him the truth.’ He leaned back on his hands and watched the clouds drift by. ’Heiscompletely different from his past self.’
’Besides,’ the man continued, ’even without my intervention, they’re bound to cross paths soon.
I want to see how he handles it this time.
And if he fails... well, that will be interesting too.’
’Keke, you are as mischievous as ever, Master~’
The man merely smiled, neither denying nor confirming.
’Anyway, let’s continue.
We have to set the stage for what’s coming.
There’s still much to do before the real game begins.’
With that, he stood up and dusted off his coat.
The dragon’s corpse beneath him began to dissolve into particles of black light, fading into the void.
Soon, nothing remained but the barren land and the man walking toward the horizon.
"Hmm...
Ethea’s eyes fluttered open.
The morning light filtered through the curtains, casting a warm glow across the room.
She blinked a few times, adjusting to the brightness, and turned her head.
Soren was already awake, sitting on the edge of the bed beside her.
He smiled the moment he saw her eyes open.
"Good morning."
"Good morning," she murmured, her voice still soft with sleep.
"Did you sleep well?"
"Mm.
I did."
"Good.
Then let me help you..."
They went through their usual morning routine.
Soren helped her wash up, brush her teeth, and change into fresh clothes.
Today, however, he didn’t pick something random from her wardrobe.
Instead, he walked over to the closet and pulled out a beautiful white dress.
It was the one he had picked for her before during their shopping.
And it was actually Ethea’s request that he choose it.
"This one?" he asked, holding it up.
Ethea nodded.
"Yes."
He helped her into it, carefully adjusting the fabric and smoothing out the wrinkles.
The dress fit her as perfectly as before, its soft white folds cascading over her wheelchair like fresh snow.
She looked elegant and ethereal, like something out of a fairy tale.
Soren stepped back a few paces and observed her, a gentle smile forming on his lips.
"You look beautiful."
"Thank you." Ethea smiled back.
"Now, it’s your turn."
"Eh?" Soren blinked, caught off guard.
"Your clothes," she clarified, gesturing toward the closet.
"I want to pick them for you."
"Oh, right, of course!" Soren nodded and glanced down at his simple shirt and trousers.
They were comfortable and practical, but they weren’t exactly date material.
Good thing she reminded him, or he might have forgotten it.
"Alright, what do you have in mind?"

chapters.title: Chapter 333: Date [1]
paragraphs: "Hmm..." Ethea studied Soren for a moment and started picking clothes. "That long-sleeved white shirt. Yes, that. And... to match your appearance... let’s pick those brown trousers."

It took them more than twenty minutes to finish, but once they were done, Soren stood in front of the mirror and adjusted his collar. The white shirt fit him well, and the brown trousers complemented his hair and eyes. He strapped on the watch and slipped into the shoes, then turned back to face her.
"Well?"
Ethea looked him up and down, then gave him a thumbs-up. "You look handsome, dear!"
"Thank you." Soren smiled and walked over to her. He extended his hand, palm up, with a slight bow of his head. "Then, my lady, shall we?"
Ethea’s eyes lit up. She placed her hand in his, and he gave it a gentle squeeze before moving behind her wheelchair to push her out of the room.
They made their way through the hotel lobby and out onto the streets of Adamery City. The morning sun was warm, and the streets were already busy with people going about their day.
"So, where are we going?" she asked, tilting her head up to look at him.
Soren smiled down at her. "It’s... a secret."
Ethea narrowed her eyes and puffed out her cheeks in a small pout before looking away.

Soren felt as if he had been struck in the chest. He had seen Ethea in many states before, like calm, cold, angry, sad, determined, gentle, and so on. But... he had never seen her make this kind of expression. It was unexpectedly adorable, and in that brief moment, his mind went completely blank.
He shook his head quickly, snapping himself out of it. This was not the time to get distracted.

"Ahem." He cleared his throat and straightened his posture, adopting a more formal tone. "I’m really sorry, my lady. I can’t really tell you. However, if there is anywhere you wish to go, please do not hesitate to inform me. I shall do my utmost to fulfill your request."
"...You," Ethea looked up at him again, an amused smile playing on her lips this time, "sound like an old butler."
"Urgh!" Soren placed a hand over his chest in mock offense. "My lady, I am no butler. I am your humble knight, sworn to protect you and fulfill your every request. How could you wound me so?
"Hehe~" Ethea giggled at his words. "My apologies, Sir Knight. I meant no offense."
"None taken, my lady."
"Then... Can you really not tell me where we’re going?"
Soren made a surrendering expression. "...My lady, you need to eat properly to eat healthy. So our first destination is a pleasant spot to enjoy breakfast."
"Oh, I see." Ethea nodded thoughtfully. "Then I look forward to it."
They continued down the main street, weaving through the morning crowd.
The city soon became alive with activity. Vendors called out their wares, children ran past with laughter, and the smell of fresh bread wafted from open shop windows.

After a few minutes of walking, they arrived in front of a place built on top of a small stream. A wooden sign above the door read ’The Morning Dew’, with a soft golden glow spilling from its windows.
"This place is..." Ethea muttered, recognition slowly crossing her features.
"That’s right," Soren confirmed. "This is the Dew Drop, and Morning Dew is its new name."
Ethea stared at the building as memories flooded back. She remembered it vividly.

Back when she was a freshman, she saved a woman from thugs, and the woman had invited her to her little eatery to thank her. The food was indeed good, and the woman was kind, so Ethea kept coming back. The owner would always insist she eat more, saying she was too thin...
Those had been some of the few peaceful moments back then. However, it had been years since she came here.
"Dear..." She turned to Soren. "How did you know and find this place?
Soren turned to her, a mysterious smile playing on his lips. "It’s a secret."
Ethea stared at him for a moment, then let out a soft chuckle. "Did Zura tell you?"

"...Maybe," Soren replied, unwilling to admit that he had spent an entire hour the night before messaging Zura. Because then he would also have to reveal that he hadn’t slept at all, too busy planning every detail of their date down to the minute.
Ethea shook her head, still smiling. "You really went out of your way."
"Of course I did." He pushed open the door and wheeled her inside. "Now, let’s see if the food is as good as you remember."

The inside of the Morning Dew was just as Ethea remembered. Wooden tables, red lanterns hanging from the ceiling, and the dulcet sound of the stream flowing beneath the floorboards. A few customers were scattered around, but the place still had its peaceful atmosphere.

A middle-aged woman emerged from the back, wiping her hands on her apron. She looked up with a polite smile, ready to greet the new customers, but her eyes lingered on Ethea for a moment longer than usual. Something about her felt familiar to the woman, but she couldn’t quite place it.
"Welcome," she said warmly. "Table for two?"
"Yes, please," Soren replied. "By the window, if possible."
The woman nodded, led them to a table by the window, and handed him a menu. "Take your time. I’ll be back to take your order."
As she walked away, Soren glanced at Ethea. ’Does she work alone?’

’No,’ Ethea answered. ’She had a daughter a few years younger than me and would help her run the place. I guess she’s grown up now and is probably working or studying. Auntie Mehriban used to say she would let her daughter study at a nice place too, that she wanted her to have a better future than just running this eatery.’
Soren nodded, noting the name. ’She sounds like a good mother.’
’Mmm... She was always kind to me.’

Soren nodded and opened the menu. The selections were simple but well-crafted. Traditional breakfast dishes, homemade bread, fresh pastries, and a variety of teas. He scanned through the options, pondering what to eat.
"...Dear, what do you recommend?"

chapters.title: Chapter 334: Date [2]
paragraphs: "...What do you recommend?" Soren decided to ask the expert since this was his first time here. He handed her the menu in case it had changed.
"...Their honey bread is really good," Ethea replied as she scanned the menu. "And the herbal tea too. She used to make it with mint and a hint of lemon. It was my favorite."
She also recommended two light meals.
"Good, then we’ll order these." Soren smiled, and just as he was about to place his order, the door opened abruptly, and a figure stumbled in.
"S-Sorry!" The figure, a young boy, shouted, slightly out of breath. His messy red hair stuck up in every direction, and his shirt was half-tucked in.
The other customers looked up, and instead of being annoyed, they laughed out loud. From their words, it seemed like this was a regular occurrence.
"There he goes again."
"Third time this week."
"At this rate, Sister Mehriban is going to start charging you instead of paying, boy, haha!"
The woman in question emerged from the kitchen and let out a long sigh, massaging her temples. "You’re late again, Darian."
"I know, I know! I’m sorry!" Darian bowed repeatedly. "The bakery was packed, and then I tripped and-"
"Calm down first," she interrupted, waving a hand. "Catch your breath before you start explaining. And inside."
Darian froze, turned to the customers, bowed, and apologized for disturbing them before hurrying into the kitchen.
"Are you ready to order?" Mehriban asked, walking toward Soren and Ethea with a warm smile.
"Yes, we would like to..." Soren replied, listing everything Ethea recommended. Mehriban nodded and left. Then, Soren turned his attention to the floating windows in his vision.
Name: Mehriban Farhadi
Race: Human
Age: 53
Status: Healthy
Rank: 2nd Circle (Early Stage)
Mental State: Warm, Content, Observant
Abilities: Enhanced Taste
Affinities: Fire (Grade 2 - E Rank)
Hidden Talent / Traits: Culinary Intuition
Potential: 2nd Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: Low
’So she does have some talent in cooking...’
Name: Darian Dervish
Race: Human
Age: 15
Status: Healthy
Rank: Unawakened
Mental State: Energetic, Scatterbrained, Determined
Hidden Talent / Traits: Photographic Memory, Serendipity’s Fool, Uncommon Wisdom
Potential: 8th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: SUPREME
’Interesting,’ Soren thought as he read through the second window. ’8th circle potential and a Supreme investment value... And those traits...’

He glanced toward the kitchen where Darian had disappeared. The boy didn’t look like much on the surface, but potential was potential. With the right training and guidance, he could become someone formidable.
’Is something the matter, dear?’ Ethea asked, noticing his gaze lingering in a particular direction.
Soren turned back to her with a smile. ’The boy who just came in. He has the potential to become a Sovereign.’
’Oh,’ Ethea’s eyes widened slightly. She glanced toward the kitchen, then back at Soren. ’You used your ability on him?’
’Mm.’ Soren nodded. ’His name is Darian Dervish. He’s fifteen, unawakened, but his potential is estimated at the 8th circle.’
’That’s... impressive.’ Ethea admitted. ’What else did you see?’

’Three strange but powerful traits and talents,’ Soren continued. ’The first is a talent called Photographic Memory, which is self-explanatory from its name. The second is a trait called Serendipity’s Fool.’ He paused, read the description, and continued. ’It brings minor misfortunes that lead to frequent accidents and delays, yet it oddly offers a strange safeguard from serious harm, as if fate is preserving him for a larger purpose.’
’That... explains the late arrivals,’ Ethea murmured.

’And the tripping,’ Soren added with a small smile. ’The second one is the Uncommon Wisdom trait. He’s... scatterbrained, but every once in a while, he says something surprisingly deep. And apparently, those words tend to come true.’

’...’ Ethea was speechless for a moment at the odd combination. A boy with bad luck and bursts of wisdom, protected by fate for reasons no one could explain. It somehow sounded like something straight out of a story.

’You... plan to help him?’ Ethea asked, recalling how Soren started making donations and helping people out whenever the chance arose. Be it a beggar on the streets or a struggling traveler, he always found a way to lend a hand without making a big deal out of it.

Sometimes, the recipients wouldn’t even know it was he who helped them. She didn’t understand why he did it or whether he had always been like this, but she found herself admiring that part of him more and more.
And she could tell, through the bond they shared, that his intentions were genuine. He wasn’t doing it for recognition or reward. He simply helped because he could.

’I was just curious,’ Soren shrugged lightly. ’But if he really needs help, I will certainly help him out.’ He paused and, as if remembering something, asked out loud. "Right, dear. Do you want to talk about something else?"
Ethea smiled. "You know, you don’t have to ask permission to change the subject. We’re just talking."
"I know. I just wanted to make sure you weren’t bored."
"I’m not bored." She shook her head. "I’m actually enjoying this."
Soren nodded, relieved. "But... What should we talk about? Do you have anything in mind?"
Ethea tilted her head, thinking. "Tell me about your school days. You haven’t told me much about them."
"I didn’t?"
"Mm. Which school did you go to?" Ethea asked curiously. "Did you have friends?"
Soren paused, and Ethea noticed a brief flicker of hesitation in his expression. "If it’s uncomfortable to talk about, then-"
"No, no." He waved a hand. "It’s fine. It’s just... it might sound boring to you since it was mostly uneventful."
"I doubt that." Ethea smiled. "You’re not a boring person."
Soren let out a short laugh. "Alright, but don’t say I didn’t warn you."
"I’m listening."

"Then, where should I start..." Soren began, but before he could find his next words, Darian appeared from the kitchen carrying a tray. He was moving fast, too fast, and as he approached their table, his foot caught on the edge of a rug.
"Here’s your ord-ah!"

The tray tilted dangerously, and for a split second, it looked like everything was about to spill. But then the teacups wobbled, tipped, and somehow landed back upright. The tea that had already spilled over the rims froze mid-air, suspended as if time itself had stopped, then slowly reversed course. The liquid flowed backward, defying gravity, and settled neatly back into the cups without a single drop wasted. The honey bread slid across the tray but stopped just at the edge. The whole thing righted itself as if an invisible hand had caught it.
"W-WHOA!" Darian watched with wide eyes, his mouth hanging open. "A-Amazing..."
"Be careful next time," Soren warned, but kept his tone gentler.

Darian blinked, then seemed to realize what he had just done. His face flushed red, and he bowed his head in shame. "I-I’m so sorry! I didn’t mean to! I-" He cut himself off, took a breath, and then, to Soren and Ethea’s surprise, he carefully and skillfully arranged the cups and plates on the table. His movements were precise and practiced, a stark contrast to the clumsiness he’d shown until now. "Please enjoy. And again, I’m really sorry for the trouble."
Soren told him not to worry too much.
Darian smiled and turned to leave, but stopped two steps later. Looking back, he asked curiously. "Umm... excuse me, but... are you an Awakened?"
Soren raised a brow but nodded.
"You were really amazing just now." Darian’s eyes sparkled with genuine admiration. "Do you think... Do you think I can become like you if I awaken?"
"...You will." Soren smiled. "If you work hard enough."
"Mmm!" Darian nodded enthusiastically, his earlier embarrassment forgotten. "I will definitely work hard. I am going to enter the Etenia Academy too!"
Soren laughed, and the others who were listening also chuckled. Darian frowned, looking around at the amused faces. "W-What? I’m really going to! I’ve been studying hard and everything, you know!"
"Haha, keep dreaming, boy."
"Right, unless you awaken a powerful ability, the academy won’t even look at your application."
"The entrance exam alone will be more than enough for you. I bet you will end up flat on your face before it even begins, haha"
"Haha!"
"Urgh..." Darian’s face fell, his enthusiasm crumbling. His shoulders slumped as he stared at the floor, unable to find a comeback.
"You can do it."
"!" Darian froze and slowly looked up, surprised to see Soren’s sincere expression.
"...I trust you."
"Y-You do?"
"Mm. But..." Soren trailed off, his gaze falling behind Darian.
Darian blinked. Then he noticed the other customers were looking at something behind him too, some of them smirking, others shaking their heads. A cold feeling crept down his spine.
He turned around slowly.
Auntie Mehriban stood there, arms crossed, foot tapping against the wooden floor.
"Bwah-!"
Before he could finish his yelp, her hand shot out and caught him by the ear. "Enough bothering the customers. Come help me with the dishes."
"Ow, ow, ow! Auntie, please, I was just-"
"Shut up."
"O-Ok, but please l-let go of my ear!"
Mehriban finally let go, and Darian quickly ran back into the kitchen, rubbing his ear and muttering under his breath.

"This kid is going to be the death of me." Mehriban watched him go with a sigh, then turned back to Soren and Ethea. "I apologize for the disturbance. He means well, but as you can see, he’s a handful. Still, thank you for being patient with him."

Hidden Talent / Traits: Photographic Memory, Serendipity’s Fool, Uncommon Wisdom
Potential: 8th Circle (Estimated)
Investment Value: SUPREME
’Interesting,’ Soren thought as he read through the second window. ’8th circle potential and a Supreme investment value...
And those traits...’
He glanced toward the kitchen where Darian had disappeared.
The boy didn’t look like much on the surface, but potential was potential.
With the right training and guidance, he could become someone formidable.
’Is something the matter, dear?’ Ethea asked, noticing his gaze lingering in a particular direction.
Soren turned back to her with a smile. ’The boy who just came in.
He has the potential to become a Sovereign.’
’Oh,’ Ethea’s eyes widened slightly.
She glanced toward the kitchen, then back at Soren. ’You used your ability on him?’
’Mm.’ Soren nodded. ’His name is Darian Dervish.
He’s fifteen, unawakened, but his potential is estimated at the 8th circle.’
’That’s... impressive.’ Ethea admitted. ’What else did you see?’
’Three strange but powerful traits and talents,’ Soren continued. ’The first is a talent called Photographic Memory, which is self-explanatory from its name.

The second is a trait called Serendipity’s Fool.’ He paused, read the description, and continued. ’It brings minor misfortunes that lead to frequent accidents and delays, yet it oddly offers a strange safeguard from serious harm, as if fate is preserving him for a larger purpose.’
’That... explains the late arrivals,’ Ethea murmured.
’And the tripping,’ Soren added with a small smile. ’The second one is the Uncommon Wisdom trait.
He’s... scatterbrained, but every once in a while, he says something surprisingly deep.
And apparently, those words tend to come true.’
’...’ Ethea was speechless for a moment at the odd combination.
A boy with bad luck and bursts of wisdom, protected by fate for reasons no one could explain.
It somehow sounded like something straight out of a story.
’You... plan to help him?’ Ethea asked, recalling how Soren started making donations and helping people out whenever the chance arose.
Be it a beggar on the streets or a struggling traveler, he always found a way to lend a hand without making a big deal out of it.
Sometimes, the recipients wouldn’t even know it was he who helped them.
She didn’t understand why he did it or whether he had always been like this, but she found herself admiring that part of him more and more.
And she could tell, through the bond they shared, that his intentions were genuine.
He wasn’t doing it for recognition or reward.
He simply helped because he could.
’I was just curious,’ Soren shrugged lightly. ’But if he really needs help, I will certainly help him out.’ He paused and, as if remembering something, asked out loud.
"Right, dear.
Do you want to talk about something else?"
Ethea smiled.
"You know, you don’t have to ask permission to change the subject.
We’re just talking."
"I know.
I just wanted to make sure you weren’t bored."
"I’m not bored." She shook her head.
"I’m actually enjoying this."
Soren nodded, relieved.
"But...
What should we talk about?
Do you have anything in mind?"
Ethea tilted her head, thinking.
"Tell me about your school days.
You haven’t told me much about them."
"I didn’t?"
"Mm.
Which school did you go to?" Ethea asked curiously.
"Did you have friends?"
Soren paused, and Ethea noticed a brief flicker of hesitation in his expression.
"If it’s uncomfortable to talk about, then-"
"No, no." He waved a hand.
"It’s fine.
It’s just... it might sound boring to you since it was mostly uneventful."
"I doubt that." Ethea smiled.
"You’re not a boring person."
Soren let out a short laugh.
"Alright, but don’t say I didn’t warn you."
"I’m listening."
"Then, where should I start..." Soren began, but before he could find his next words, Darian appeared from the kitchen carrying a tray.
He was moving fast, too fast, and as he approached their table, his foot caught on the edge of a rug.
"Here’s your ord-ah!"
The tray tilted dangerously, and for a split second, it looked like everything was about to spill.
But then the teacups wobbled, tipped, and somehow landed back upright.
The tea that had already spilled over the rims froze mid-air, suspended as if time itself had stopped, then slowly reversed course.
The liquid flowed backward, defying gravity, and settled neatly back into the cups without a single drop wasted.
The honey bread slid across the tray but stopped just at the edge.
The whole thing righted itself as if an invisible hand had caught it.
"W-WHOA!" Darian watched with wide eyes, his mouth hanging open.
"A-Amazing..."
"Be careful next time," Soren warned, but kept his tone gentler.
Darian blinked, then seemed to realize what he had just done.
His face flushed red, and he bowed his head in shame.
"I-I’m so sorry!
I didn’t mean to!
I-" He cut himself off, took a breath, and then, to Soren and Ethea’s surprise, he carefully and skillfully arranged the cups and plates on the table.
His movements were precise and practiced, a stark contrast to the clumsiness he’d shown until now.
"Please enjoy.
And again, I’m really sorry for the trouble."
Soren told him not to worry too much.
Darian smiled and turned to leave, but stopped two steps later.
Looking back, he asked curiously.
"Umm... excuse me, but... are you an Awakened?"
Soren raised a brow but nodded.
"You were really amazing just now." Darian’s eyes sparkled with genuine admiration.
"Do you think...
Do you think I can become like you if I awaken?"
"...You will." Soren smiled.
"If you work hard enough."
"Mmm!" Darian nodded enthusiastically, his earlier embarrassment forgotten.
"I will definitely work hard.
I am going to enter the Etenia Academy too!"
Soren laughed, and the others who were listening also chuckled.
Darian frowned, looking around at the amused faces.
"W-What?
I’m really going to!
I’ve been studying hard and everything, you know!"
"Haha, keep dreaming, boy."
"Right, unless you awaken a powerful ability, the academy won’t even look at your application."
"The entrance exam alone will be more than enough for you.
I bet you will end up flat on your face before it even begins, haha"
"Haha!"
"Urgh..." Darian’s face fell, his enthusiasm crumbling.
His shoulders slumped as he stared at the floor, unable to find a comeback.
"You can do it."
"!" Darian froze and slowly looked up, surprised to see Soren’s sincere expression.
"...I trust you."
"Y-You do?"
"Mm.
But..." Soren trailed off, his gaze falling behind Darian.
Darian blinked.
Then he noticed the other customers were looking at something behind him too, some of them smirking, others shaking their heads.
A cold feeling crept down his spine.
He turned around slowly.
Auntie Mehriban stood there, arms crossed, foot tapping against the wooden floor.
"Bwah-!"
Before he could finish his yelp, her hand shot out and caught him by the ear.
"Enough bothering the customers.
Come help me with the dishes."
"Ow, ow, ow!
Auntie, please, I was just-"
"Shut up."
"O-Ok, but please l-let go of my ear!"
Mehriban finally let go, and Darian quickly ran back into the kitchen, rubbing his ear and muttering under his breath.
"This kid is going to be the death of me." Mehriban watched him go with a sigh, then turned back to Soren and Ethea.
"I apologize for the disturbance.
He means well, but as you can see, he’s a handful.
Still, thank you for being patient with him."

chapters.title: Chapter 335: Date [3]
paragraphs: Soren and Ethea reassured Mehriban and finally started eating their breakfast. And this time, Mehriban personally brought the meals, probably fearing Darian might ruin everything again.
"So you attended a nearby ordinary school and hid the fact that you were from the Valmere family?" Ethea asked as Soren began his school-life story.

"Yes," Soren nodded. "However, it didn’t last long. After they learned I was a Valmere, my classmates were curious at first. Some tried to befriend me, probably hoping to get close to a ’noble’. But once they realized I was just a Valmere in name and considered the family’s embarrassment, they slowly distanced themselves. Fortunately, they didn’t treat me badly or bully me. They just... ignored me."
Ethea nodded, listening intently. She didn’t interrupt, letting him speak at his own pace.

"But there were some who didn’t change," Soren continued, a faint smile touching his lips. "They kept treating me like a regular classmate, as if nothing had changed. I was already used to being ignored, so I wasn’t affected by the ones who pulled away. But the ones who stayed... they surprised me. It made me realize that not everyone cares about family names or status. Some people just treat you like a person, and that’s it."
"They sound like good people," Ethea commented, secretly grateful he had found kindness in a place where he could easily have been alone.

Soren nodded. "They were." He paused, a faint smile crossing his lips as if reliving a memory. "In fact, I became close friends with two of them. They were the ones who refused to let me sit alone during lunch or work by myself during group projects. They kept dragging me into their circle, and after a while, the rest of the class just got used to having me around. Eventually, they started treating me like a normal classmate too."
"Oh!" Ethea’s eyes lit up. "Are they your best friends?"
"...Yeah, let’s go with that." Soren chuckled.
"Can you tell me how you became friends? What did you do?"

"Mm..." Soren nodded and answered her questions one by one. "Actually, one of them was my deskmate. His name is Harmen. He was what you’d call a social butterfly. Always talking and always surrounded by people. I honestly have no idea how we became best friends, since we were complete opposites at the time. But now that I think about it, it’s probably because he kept talking to me. Even when I gave him short answers, he never gave up."
"He sounds persistent." Ethea laughed as it reminded her of a certain someone. "Right, what about the second one?"

"The second one was a quiet girl who sat behind us. Her name is Edith. She was the opposite of him, more like me. She barely spoke unless someone spoke to her first. However, she always shared her notes whenever I missed class or was late. In fact, she was the one I had to fight for the first spot in every exam."
"Oh," Ethea raised a brow, "who won then?"
"Well... let’s say fifty-fifty. Sometimes she won, and sometimes I did. And we both had subjects we were good and bad at. But in the overall ranking," Soren smirked, "I always came out on top.
Ethea giggled. "There must be a reason, right?"
"Well... she wasreallybad at PE... really bad..."
Ethea tilted her head. "How bad?"

"...At the bottom of the class." Soren chuckled. "And Harmen always used to make fun of her for it. He’d tease her every time she tripped or made a mistake." He paused, shaking his head. "But the truth is, he was only good at PE. Academically, he was a lost cause. If not for Edith and me, he would have never passed a single exam."
"...She didn’t tease him back? And also helped him?" Ethea asked in surprise.

"...A few times," Soren answered. "She’d remind him who was actually at the bottom of the class when it came to grades. But she never held it against him. She just... helped him anyway. That’s the kind of person she was. But then again, Herman wouldn’t let her have peace if she didn’t help him. He’d follow her around all day, complaining about how unfair exams were and how he was going to fail and end up working some dead-end job."
Ethea laughed. "He sounds dramatic."
"He was," Soren said with a fond smile. "But he was also loyal and protective. If anyone ever gave us trouble, he’d be the first to step in. Even if it meant getting detention for a week."
"..." Ethea stayed silent this time, knowing there was some story behind it.

"Anyway, thanks to the two of them, my school life was actually pretty good," Soren continued. "I wasn’t alone anymore. We studied together, ate together, got into trouble together. In fact, we even worked part-time together."
"I see. Then are you still in contact with them?"
Soren paused, then shook his head. "Before the wedding, I severed all contact with my past acquaintances. But I still remember where they live and their old numbers."
"I want to meet them," Ethea said without hesitation. "Once everything settles down, let’s look them up. I want to thank them for taking care of you."
Soren blinked, caught off guard by her straightforwardness. Then a warm smile spread across his face. "Alright. We’ll do that.
Then his smile widened as he recalled something. "Actually, there’s something else I haven’t told you about them."
"Oh?" Ethea leaned forward slightly, curious.
"Harmen and Edith are childhood friends. They grew up together, neighbors, actually. Their families have known each other for years."
"That explains why they were so close," Ethea said, nodding. "So, what are they doing now?"
Soren paused, a mischievous glint flickering in his eyes. "That’s a secret."
Ethea blinked, then frowned slightly. "You’re doing it again."
"Doing what?"
"That."

"...I promise I’ll tell you later. But speaking of secrets..." Soren leaned forward slightly, lowering his voice. "You never told me you had a best friend like Lady Zura. I had to find out from her directly."
Ethea paused, then let out a soft sigh. "I suppose I should have mentioned her."
"It’s fine." Soren smiled. "I’m just glad you have someone like her."
"Mmm." Ethea smiled. "Then... do you wanna hear about how I met her as well?"
"Sure." Soren leaned back, giving her his full attention. "I’d love to."

chapters.title: Chapter 336: Whispering Forest [1]
paragraphs: "Thank you, we really enjoyed it."
"I’m glad you did." Melina smiled warmly as she cleared the table. "You’re welcome back anytime."
"We’ll keep that in mind," Ethea replied with a small nod.
As Soren stood up and moved behind Ethea’s wheelchair, the kitchen door swung open, and Darian popped his head out. He waved enthusiastically, nearly knocking over a stack of plates in the process.
"B-Bye! Come again! I’ll try not to spill anything next time!"
Soren chuckled and gave him a small wave in return. "We’ll hold you to that."
With that, he wheeled Ethea out of The Morning Dew and back onto the street. The morning sun had risen higher now, casting long shadows across the ground.
"Where are we going next?" Ethea asked as Soren took out the car. "Somewhere far?"
"Yes," Soren nodded as he gently picked her up. "It’s a place you know very well."
"Is it famous?"
"Yes," Soren buckled her in. "Think of a movie theater, but a magical version."
"Magical theater..." Ethea pondered for a moment, and then her eyes lit up. "The Adamery Illusion Theater?"
Soren nodded with a grin.

"Oh! What are we going to experience?" Ethea asked, catching herself before she said ’watch’. At an illusion theater, you didn’t watch the story, but lived in it. The immersion was so complete that it was no different from reality. The only downside was that you always knew you were inside a story. No matter how real it felt, a small awareness always lingered in the back of your mind that none of it was truly happening.
"It’s a new one," Soren said. "Called The Whispering Forest."
"The Whispering Forest?" Ethea repeated, her interest piqued.
"It’s a mystery mixed with adventure," Soren revealed with a smile. "I heard it’s one of the best ones they’ve created recently."
"..." Ethea fell silent, her gaze becoming softer as she looked at him. ’He chose it based on my preferences...’
"...Thank you, dear."
Soren glanced at her briefly, a small smile on his lips. "You’re welcome."

They arrived at the theater a short while later. The building was a massive dome with silver panels that shimmered under the sunlight. Soren parked the car and helped Ethea out, then wheeled her inside, where a staff member led them to the private chamber Soren had booked in advance. It was a small, dimly lit room with two plush reclining seats in the center, each one designed like a capsule that would fully immerse the user in the illusion.

The staff then explained everything they needed to know, including the rules, setting, process, and how to start and exit the story. They listened quietly until he finished, then wished them a pleasant experience and took her leave.
Soren then gently laid Ethea down in one capsule before settling into the other beside her. He reached over and took her hand.
"Ready?" he asked.
Ethea squeezed his hand. "Ready."

The capsules hummed softly as the illusion magic activated. A gentle warmth spread through their bodies, and the world around them blurred. Soren felt his mind go blank for a moment, a strange emptiness settling over his thoughts like fog.
’Urgh...’
Soren felt a headache hit him as he slowly opened his eyes. However, he found himself surrounded by pitch darkness; even with his night vision, he was unable to see a thing.
’...’ He squinted and tried to move. ’...Am I tied up?’

His body wouldn’t budge. Something sticky and strange was wrapped tightly around him, binding his arms to his sides and his legs together from below his neck all the way down to his ankles. He tried to speak, but a strip of cloth stretched across his mouth, muffling any sound he could make.
’...I guess I’m the captive character.’

Sighing inwardly, thought about what to do. He could feel that he could use his mental power if he really tried it and perhaps even break through the illusion. However, where was the fun in that? He paid a lot of money to experience this story, and breaking it on the first scene would be a waste.
So he decided to play along and see where it would take him.

’But... Where is Ethea?’ He asked himself, as he recalled the setting they were given before starting. ’The staff said there are five main characters. Three are part of an adventurer party, and two are secret characters with hidden roles. The three’s mission is to uncover the secret of the Whispering Forest while saving the kidnapped children.’
He wondered which one he was.
’Hmm... Let’s think about my situation.’
He was being held captive in the dark, tied up and gagged... he wasn’t one of the kidnapped children, was he?
’...No. That can’t be right.’
He was too old for that, unless the illusion had altered his appearance to match the role.
’Hmm... What should I do then?’

Soren paused as strange sounds filtered into his ears. They were faint and distorted, like voices speaking through water. He couldn’t make out any words, just fragmented noises that didn’t sound human.
’What is that?’
The sounds continued, growing louder and clearer with each passing moment.
’...Hmm. I must be in the Whispering Forest. And these must be the whispers the story is named after.’
He focused on the sounds, trying to make sense of them. They were still disjointed, but slowly, words began to emerge from the noise.

However, he still couldn’t understand anything, just speculate. That’s why he decided to wait and see while getting used to the whispers. Perhaps he could learn a thing or two or discover the forest’s secret that way. His only regret was not experiencing this with Ethea, and he hoped they would reunite soon.

Meanwhile, right outside the Whispering Forest, four people stood at the edge of the treeline. The forest loomed before them, its trees tall and twisted, their branches reaching out like grasping fingers. A faint breeze carried sounds that made the hairs on the back of their necks stand on end. Whispers drifted from between the trees, low and eerie, curling around their ears even though they hadn’t set foot inside yet.
"Is this the place?" A red-haired woman asked while trying to hide her uneasiness.
The plain-clothed man beside her nodded, his face pale and drawn. His hands trembled slightly as he clutched the hem of his worn tunic. "Y-Yes, Mrs. Adventurer."
The knight beside the woman frowned before asking, "How many children have been taken?"
"S-Seven..."

He could feel that he could use his mental power if he really tried it and perhaps even break through the illusion.
However, where was the fun in that?
He paid a lot of money to experience this story, and breaking it on the first scene would be a waste.
So he decided to play along and see where it would take him.
’But...
Where is Ethea?’ He asked himself, as he recalled the setting they were given before starting. ’The staff said there are five main characters.
Three are part of an adventurer party, and two are secret characters with hidden roles.
The three’s mission is to uncover the secret of the Whispering Forest while saving the kidnapped children.’
He wondered which one he was.
’Hmm...
Let’s think about my situation.’
He was being held captive in the dark, tied up and gagged... he wasn’t one of the kidnapped children, was he?
That can’t be right.’
He was too old for that, unless the illusion had altered his appearance to match the role.
’Hmm...
What should I do then?’
Soren paused as strange sounds filtered into his ears.
They were faint and distorted, like voices speaking through water.
He couldn’t make out any words, just fragmented noises that didn’t sound human.
’What is that?’
The sounds continued, growing louder and clearer with each passing moment.
I must be in the Whispering Forest.
And these must be the whispers the story is named after.’
He focused on the sounds, trying to make sense of them.
They were still disjointed, but slowly, words began to emerge from the noise.
However, he still couldn’t understand anything, just speculate.
That’s why he decided to wait and see while getting used to the whispers.
Perhaps he could learn a thing or two or discover the forest’s secret that way.
His only regret was not experiencing this with Ethea, and he hoped they would reunite soon.
Meanwhile, right outside the Whispering Forest, four people stood at the edge of the treeline.
The forest loomed before them, its trees tall and twisted, their branches reaching out like grasping fingers.
A faint breeze carried sounds that made the hairs on the back of their necks stand on end.
Whispers drifted from between the trees, low and eerie, curling around their ears even though they hadn’t set foot inside yet.
"Is this the place?" A red-haired woman asked while trying to hide her uneasiness.
The plain-clothed man beside her nodded, his face pale and drawn.
His hands trembled slightly as he clutched the hem of his worn tunic.
"Y-Yes, Mrs.
Adventurer."
The knight beside the woman frowned before asking, "How many children have been taken?"
"S-Seven..."

chapters.title: Chapter 337: Whispering Forest [2]
paragraphs: "S-Seven," the villager replied nervously, then bowed deeply. "P-Please, save them."
The knight placed a hand on the villager’s shoulder. "I can’t promise anything, but we’ll try our best."
"T-Thank you!"
The knight waved and led his party into the forest, the red-haired woman using a fire spell to light the way.

The villager watched them go, and the moment they were out of his sight, his fearful expression melted away, replaced by a mysterious smile. The next second, his body slowly turned to mist and disappeared.
A minute passed in silence, broken only by the faint whispers drifting from the forest.

Then a figure emerged from the treeline. A woman, dressed in dark leathers with a mask covering the lower half of her face. She moved without a sound, her eyes fixed on the spot where the villager had vanished.
’So I was right,’ she thought, her gaze narrowing. ’He was not one of them.’
"Elea!"
The red-haired woman came stomping back through the underbrush, the knight close behind her. Both looked annoyed, though the knight’s irritation was more controlled.
"Why did you disappear again?" the red-haired woman demanded. "We told you to stay with the group."
Elea shook her head. "Nothing. Just checking something."
"Checking what?" the knight asked.
"Nothing important," she replied, turning away from the spot where the villager had disappeared. "Let’s not waste time. We have children to save."
"Yeah," The red-haired woman frowned. "The sooner we finish, the faster we can go home. I really hate these kinds of places, you know.
The knight nodded in agreement. "Stay close. We don’t know what’s waiting for us in here."

The three of them moved deeper into the forest, their footsteps muffled by the thick carpet of fallen leaves. The whispers grew louder with every step, brushing against their ears like cold fingers. The red-haired woman kept her hand near her weapon, and the knight’s eyes scanned the darkness ahead.
Elea walked behind them, silent as always. But her mind was elsewhere.

’He must be a hidden character,’ she thought, recalling the staff’s explanation before they entered. Since her party members were created by the illusion, they couldn’t be him. ’But where do I find him?’

She glanced around at the twisted trees and the shadows that seemed to shift when she wasn’t looking. The forest was vast, and the whispers made it hard to think clearly. If not for her character’s superior senses and perception, she couldn’t even see five meters ahead. If Soren was somewhere in here, finding him wouldn’t be easy.
’However, since this is a story, I’m sure we’ll encounter him soon. I just have to keep observing and make sure not to miss him.’
And, considering Soren’s personality, he was probably looking for her too. So, they might meet sooner than she expected.
’Yeah...’
She allowed herself a small smile behind her mask, then quickened her pace to catch up with the others.

The three of them pressed deeper into the forest, the whispers growing louder with every step. It wasn’t long before they encountered trouble. Strange black creatures emerged from the shadows, their bodies shifting and twisting like smoke. They had no faces, only glowing red eyes and claws that tore through the air with a sickening screech. The knight drew his sword, the red-haired woman summoned flames to her palms, and Elea melted into the shadows, her daggers flashing.

The fight was brief but intense. The creatures dissolved when struck, but more kept coming, as if the forest itself was trying to push them back. The whispers also intensified, affecting their minds, sometimes cursing them and sometimes trying to allure.

After what felt like hours, they stumbled into a small clearing where the whispers softened to a gentle hum. There, hovering above a cluster of glowing mushrooms, was a tiny fairy. She was no bigger than a hand, with translucent wings and eyes that shimmered like liquid silver.
"Travelers," the fairy said, her voice like wind chimes. "You shouldn’t be here. The forest doesn’t welcome strangers."
"We’re looking for the missing children," the knight said. "Do you know where they are?"
The fairy tilted her head. "...The children are safe. For now. But the one who took them... he is not what he seems."
"Who is he?" Mona asked. "Some kind of monster?"
The fairy’s wings drooped. "We don’t know his name. We only know he wears many faces. He was once one of us, but he was cast out. Now he seeks to claim the forest for himself."

The fairy gave them a few more clues, hints about the forest’s history, why the children were kidnapped, and so on. She also warned them of the whispers, telling them not to trust everything they heard.
Then she vanished in a puff of light with an ominous line saying he knows they’re here.
With no choice, they kept walking, but they saw no sign of Soren or any other human. The forest stretched endlessly, and the whispers never stopped.
Elea’s mind raced as she kept thinking. ’...He might appear at the end. Or perhaps he’s one of the kidnapped children.’ She paused, a new thought forming. ’Or... he might be the evil one himself.’
She considered the possibility. The fairy had said the enemy wore many faces. What if Soren’s role was the antagonist? It would be a twist, but not impossible.
She shook her head. ’No. The villain is probably the villager who brought us here. And... Fairy isn’t exactly trustworthy either.’

Not to mention her sudden appearance, but also her seemingly helpful nature despite warning them they shouldn’t be here. In fact, the fairy seemed to be manipulating them, feeding them just enough information to keep them moving forward without actually telling them anything useful.
’Classic misdirection,’ She thought. ’Give them a vague warning, a few crumbs of truth, and let them think they’re making progress on their own.’
She also made a mental note to keep an eye on any other "helpful" creatures they encountered. The forest was clearly designed to confuse and mislead, and she wasn’t about to fall for it.
’I just hope I can meet him soon. It’s boring without him...’

chapters.title: Chapter 338: Whispering Forest [3]
paragraphs: ’A... little more...’
’...Finally!’

Soren twisted his body one last time, the sticky webbing finally loosening enough for him to pull his arms free. He ripped the gag from his mouth and gasped for air, his lungs burning from the effort. The webbing clung to his clothes and skin, but he ignored it and focused on his surroundings.

Strangely, even without his sight, he now could sense everything around him. He guessed it must be because of his character or the forest itself. But more importantly, thanks to listening to the whispers for more than an hour, he managed to piece things together and almost figured out the truth. Including the fact that Ethea might be heading right into a trap.
’I have to find her fast.’ He thought. ’But first...’

He turned his head slowly, following the whispers’ guidance. Around him, hanging from the ceiling like grotesque ornaments, were dozens of cocoons. They were wrapped in the same sticky webbing that had bound him, and he could sense faint life forces inside them.
’...I have to free them.’
However, there was one big problem.
’...’ He raised his head, looked far above, and saw them. A cluster of glowing red eyes, dozens of them, staring down from the darkness. ’Gulp...’
Despite knowing this was fake, he still couldn’t help but swallow.
’I think... they should add a horror tag to this story.’

If it were someone with a weaker heart, they might have screamed or fainted on the spot. Fortunately, he had faced far worse things in reality, so a giant spider-like monster in an illusion wasn’t going to break him. Still, the sight of those unblinking, cold eyes made his skin crawl.
’...Let’s just save them later.’
He decided after a moment’s thought and forced himself to look away.
’Let’s focus on the whispers...’

He closed his eyes and let the voices wash over him. They were clearer now, no longer the fragmented noise he had heard when he first woke up. Many of them still overlapped and intertwined, but he could pick out individual threads if he concentrated enough.
’...this way...’
’...follow...’
’...closer...’

He opened his eyes and started moving. The whispers guided him through a narrow crack in the wall, barely wide enough for him to squeeze through. He had to twist and turn, the rough stone scraping against his shoulders, but eventually, he stumbled out into open air.
His sight, which had been useless in the darkness, suddenly began to clear; the surroundings started to take shape. And the first thing he saw was the massive structure he had just crawled out of.
’...Is this... a tree?’

It was enormous. The trunk alone was wider than a big house, its bark dark and gnarled, stretching up into the canopy so high he couldn’t see the top. Roots the size of buildings twisted into the ground, and between them, he could see the faint glimmer of webbing.
’I see...’

He had been inside that tree the whole time. And it was definitely the lair of the monster and the place where the ending, or perhaps the final battle, would take place. However, for that to happen, the other characters had to find their way here first.
’...I think I might be the one who brings them here.’
He nods at his conclusion and looks at his body.
’...Unfortunately, this body is weak. I can’t fight, I can’t run fast, and I definitely can’t take a hit.’
If he got hit badly and died, he would be kicked out of the story.
’...Hah.’ He let out a quiet sigh. Of all the roles he could have gotten, he ended up as a helpless child. But then, despite everything, his lips curled up.
’...Well, it’s a challenge. And I like challenges.’
With that, he started moving, following the whispers through the dark forest.
"Urgh... Damn it!" Mona cursed. "We are really lost!"
"..." The knight, Theo, sighed helplessly but couldn’t refute her. "Let’s keep moving."
Elea watched them from behind, her ears twitching at every sound. The forest was still noisy, full of whispers and rustling leaves, but she had long learned to filter through it.
’Hmm?’
Suddenly, she froze as she heard something else, heading straight toward them, probably running.
"Something’s coming," she warned.
"Not again," Mona groaned, raising her hands as flames flickered to life around her fingers.
Theo drew his sword and stepped in front of the group. "Be on guard."
They formed a tight formation, backs to each other, weapons ready. The footsteps grew louder, closer, and Mona prepared to fire.
But Elea’s eyes widened when she saw the figure first. "Stop!"
She shouted at Mona.
"W-What?" Mona froze, barely stopping herself from shooting. "Damn it, Elea!"

Before Elea could answer, two red eyes appeared in the shadows. They grew brighter, closer, until they took shape. A small boy stumbled into view, his black skin blending with the darkness, his red eyes wide and unfocused. He looked similar to the black monsters they had been fighting, but something about him was different.
He tripped over a root and fell to his knees, breathing in ragged gasps.
"It’s... a child?" Theo lowered his sword slightly, confusion replacing his earlier tension.
Mona stared, her flames flickering uncertainly. "Is that... not one of the monsters?"
"No." Elea stepped forward, her eyes fixed on the boy. "He’s not."
The boy lifted his head, his red eyes meeting hers. There was something familiar in them, something that made her heart skip.
"...Soren?"
The boy’s expression lit up, but to Mona and Theo, it looked extremely eerie.
"W-Who are you!" Mona demanded, taking a few steps back and intensifying her flames.
"!" The boy froze and turned toward her, opening his mouth. "Gnh... ngh... ah..."
"?" Mona and Theo made confused faces, while their wariness grew.
The boy himself looked the most confused, as his voice sounded broken, like words that had been crushed before they could leave his throat. He tried again, his face scrunching with effort.
"Ah... gnh... nnh..."
Nothing coherent came out. Just those same shattered noises, over and over.
Mona furrowed her brows. "What’s wrong with him?"
The boy stopped trying to speak. His brow furrowed, and his lips pressed into a thin line, frustration flickering across his face before something like embarrassment replaced it.
"He can’t speak," Elea said, stepping between the boy and Mona. She knelt down to his level and met his eyes. "Are you one of the ’kidnapped children’?"
The boy looked at her for a long moment, then nodded.
’Dear, I finally found you.’
’Mm... Me too.’
Ethea’s lips curled up behind her mask, and her heart, which had been pounding since the moment she saw him, finally began to settle.
Mona let her flames die down, though her expression remained wary. "Okay, so he’s a kid. Fine. But where are the others?"
Theo glanced at her, then back at the boy. "Can you show us the way?"
The boy turned to him and nodded. But then his expression shifted. He pointed behind him and frowned, his small face scrunching with something that looked like urgency.
"...Monsters are coming." Elea translated. "A lot of them."
Mona cursed again and flicked her fingers, a large circle of flames surrounding the four of them.
"...die... humans..."
"...kill... them... kill..."
"...keke.. kke..."
The whispers intensified, and countless monsters emerged from the trees, surrounding them from all sides.
’Even though this is an illusion,’ Elea said, ’let me protect you this time, dear.’
She winked at the stunned boy and vanished into thin air.
"Boy, get behind me!"
The knight stepped forward and swung his sword. A wave of light erupted from the blade, cutting through more than ten monsters in a single blow. They dissolved into mist, but more took their place.

Mona was even more impressive. She raised her hands, and a storm of fire erupted from the circle. The flames danced and twisted, incinerating any monster that came too close. She also sent lances of fire into the darkness, each one hitting its mark with deadly precision.

And Elea... one moment she was beside him, and the next she was behind a group of monsters, her daggers flashing. They fell before they could even turn around. She moved like a shadow cutting through the horde with an elegance that made it look effortless.
’...She’s cool.’
The boy smiled. But more than that, he was happy to see her walking and moving around freely.
’...I will make it happen for real too... I swear.’
He tightened his fists and watched as the trio fought, and after what felt like hours, they finally managed to kill all the monsters. They took a few minutes to rest.
"Now," The knight, Theo, turned to him, "please take us to where other children are."
The boy nodded and started walking, leading them through the Whispering Forest. The others trailed beside him, alert for any sign of danger.
’Dear... do you want me to carry you?’
’!’ The boy nearly tripped over his own feet, catching himself on a tree root just in time. He shot her a look, his red eyes wide with embarrassment. ’N-No, I’m fine.’
’...Pfft!’

And Elea... one moment she was beside him, and the next she was behind a group of monsters, her daggers flashing.
They fell before they could even turn around.
She moved like a shadow cutting through the horde with an elegance that made it look effortless.
’...She’s cool.’
The boy smiled.
But more than that, he was happy to see her walking and moving around freely.
’...I will make it happen for real too...
I swear.’
He tightened his fists and watched as the trio fought, and after what felt like hours, they finally managed to kill all the monsters.
They took a few minutes to rest.
"Now," The knight, Theo, turned to him, "please take us to where other children are."
The boy nodded and started walking, leading them through the Whispering Forest.
The others trailed beside him, alert for any sign of danger.
’Dear... do you want me to carry you?’
’!’ The boy nearly tripped over his own feet, catching himself on a tree root just in time.
He shot her a look, his red eyes wide with embarrassment. ’N-No, I’m fine.’
’...Pfft!’

chapters.title: Chapter 339: Whispering Forest [4]
paragraphs: ’...Pfft!’
Ethea couldn’t help but laugh at his reaction.
Soren gritted his teeth and turned forward, hastening his pace.
"Be careful," Theo warned, killing a sneaky monster that had crept too close. "There might be more hiding in the shadows."
"Nnh..." Soren nodded and kept leading the way. ’What happened to you, Ethea?’
’I woke up in a village in...’

While exchanging thoughts through their bond, they walked for several more minutes. The forest grew darker and denser, the whispers growing louder with every step. Then, through a gap in the trees, they saw it.

The massive tree loomed before them, its trunk wider than a house and its branches stretching into the sky like grasping claws. Webbing hung from the branches, glistening faintly in the dim light, and at the base of the trunk, a small opening led into the hollow interior.
Soren stopped and pointed.
"That’s where the children are..."
Ethea translated for him again.
"You mean, they are inside?" Mona’s already dark expression darkened even further. "Seriously?"

Theo studied the massive tree grimly. "...It makes sense. A place like that would be easy to hide and defend. If we go in without a plan, we’ll be walking right into a trap." He sighed and looked at the boy. "...We can’t even know what we’re dealing with."
"Gnh..." Soren raised his hands and made a series of quick signs. Ethea ’watched’ carefully, then nodded and turned to the others.
"He says the inside is pitch black. You can’t see anything unless you have special senses. And based on the webbing and the red eyes he saw, the creature is likely a spider type."
"Huh?" Mono and Theo made stunned expressions. "Since when did you know sign language?"
"More importantly," Ethea ignored their comment and continued, "the fairy had lied to us."
"Huh?" The two froze again. "What do you mean?"

Ethea sighed and explained. "You remember what she said, right? Most of them were fabricated to lead us into a trap. The boy told me that he heard about it while trapped. Furthermore, I suspect that she’s the great evil that wore many faces, or at least the one behind all of this. The monsters we fought till now are probably her servants or creations."
"Why do you think so?" Theo asked curiously.

"Think logically," Ethea said. "Fairies are supposed to be powerful, pure-hearted, and fiercely protective of nature. If she were truly one of them, she would have fought against the monsters herself and done her best to save the children. Or at the very least, she would have joined us in our mission. Instead, she only appeared at a rather convenient time, gave us a half-hearted warning, and and then vanished before we could ask anything useful."
Mono and Theo froze, realization slowly crossing their features.
"Besides," Ethea continued, "didn’t you sense it yet? The gaze that’s been watching us."
"W-What?"
"She never left." Ethea stared far above at the tree. "She has been watching us from the beginning."
"...The whispers... disappeared?
Theo tightened his grip on his sword, his eyes scanning the darkness. "That’s not a good sign."
"...Hehehe~"
A laughter echoed through the clearing. It was soft and melodic, but it carried an edge that made the hairs on the back of their necks stand on end.
"A-Above us..."
The branches shifted, and a familiar tiny figure descended slowly, her translucent wings catching the firelight.
"I should have known you’d figure it out eventually," she said, her voice dripping with amusement mixed with mockery. "You’re smarter than the last ones. And..."
Her gaze falled onto Soren. "Lucky too."
Ethea didn’t hesitate. A dagger flashed from her hand, spinning toward the fairy. Mono reacted a second later, a fireball roaring from her palm.
The fairy twisted in the air, dodging both with a mocking laugh. The dagger and fireball shot past her, disappearing into the darkness above.
Then the fireball exploded.

The flash of light revealed something massive. A white spiderlike creature clung to the underside of the branches, its body bloated and pale, its legs long and spindly. Countless threads connected it to the fairy, thin and glistening like silk.
Mono’s breath caught. "What the hell is that?!"
The fairy smiled, her form flickering.
"Hehehe, it’s too late~"

The fairy snapped her fingers. Threads shot out from the darkness, wrapping around them all. They were thin and sticky, almost invisible until they touched skin, and they tightened instantly, binding them in place.
"W-What the-" Mona struggled, but the more she moved, the tighter the threads became. "Get off!"
Theo tried to cut them with his sword, but the blade bounced off harmlessly. "They’re reinforced. I can’t cut them."
The fairy giggled, floating higher. "Struggle all you want. The more you move, the tighter they get. You’ll be wrapped up like the others soon enough."

Mona’s eye twitched. Her face twisted with irritation, then outright annoyance. "Oh yeah? Wrapped up like the others?" Her voice grew louder, and her body began to glow. "Then let me show you what happens when you try to wrap up a PYROMANCER!"
"BOOOM!"

Her entire body erupted in flames. The heat was intense, so intense that the threads around her evaporated instantly, turning to ash before they could even smoke. Mona stood in the center of a blazing inferno, her hair whipping around her like fire itself.
Theo followed her lead. Golden light surged from his body, enveloping him. The threads binding him sizzled and dissolved, unable to withstand the radiance.
Meanwhile, Ethea had already vanished. In the split second the fairy’s attention was on Mona, she slipped out of the threads, grabbed Soren, and melted into the shadows.
Swoosh!

Ethea appeared above the fairy, her dagger slicing downward. The fairy’s eyes widened, and she twisted in the air, barely avoiding the blade. Threads shot from her fingertips, lashing toward Ethea like whips, but Ethea vanished again, reappearing beside Mona and Theo.
The fairy smirked and spun around, ready to attack again. At the same time, one spider eye swiveled toward the base of the tree and caught sight of a small figure slipping through the entrance.
’...I see.’
The fairy’s lips curled into a wide grin, but she didn’t move to stop him. Instead, she kept staring at the reunited trio, her laughter echoing through the clearing.
"Let’s put an end to this! Hehehe!"
Swoosh!

She vanished in a blur of light, and the massive spider above them dropped from the branches, its pale body crashing down toward the trio like a falling boulder. Its legs, long and spindly, stabbed into the ground, sending dirt and debris flying in every direction.
Theo’s eyes widened, and he slammed his sword into the ground.
"Aegis of Dawn!"
A golden barrier erupted around them, a dome of shimmering light that stopped the spider’s fangs just inches from Mona’s face.
"Inferno Lance!"

Mona thrust both hands forward, and a spear of white-hot fire shot from her palms. It struck the spider’s abdomen and exploded, but when the smoke cleared, the creature was still standing, its hide burned in places but otherwise unharmed.
Ethea slashed at its leg, but her daggers couldn’t pierce the hide. The spider swatted her away, and she flipped mid-air, landing on her feet.
Their expressions turned grim.
This wasn’t going to be easy.
’Finally back!’
Soren collapsed to the ground as he slipped through the crack in the wall. He lay there for a moment, catching his breath, then pushed himself up and looked around.
’...I can see now?’
Strangely, the darkness inside the tree didn’t seem as thick as before. Shapes were forming in the shadows, edges becoming visible where there had only been blackness moments ago.

He slowly moved toward one of the cocoons he could reach with his current height. It was smaller than the others, barely the size of a child. He pulled out the dagger Ethea had slipped him earlier and carefully cut through the webbing.
The cocoon split open, and a body tumbled to the floor.
Soren froze.
The figure on the ground was thin and twisted, its skin black and cracked, its limbs bent at unnatural angles. It looked exactly like the monsters they had been fighting.

He stared at it for a long moment, then looked down at his own hand. He then recalled how Ethea described him. Red eyes, pitch-black skin, and a body that looked almost identical to the black monsters they had faced.
’...Am I... already dead?’
"...Was this your plan?" A mocking voice echoed behind him. "If so, then you really disappointed me. After all..."
Soren turned around to face the fairy. Countless thoughts crossed his mind, but something told him that the voice wasn’t talking to him, but to the original character he was embodying.
"...I was born from you."

Soren squinted, pieces clicking together in his head. ’I think I understand it now... Who my character is... Why could I hear those whispers without being affected... Why the monsters didn’t seem that hostile to me, perhaps even... afraid.’
"Admit it, you’ve failed. The forest is now mine. Everything you tried to protect belongs to me now. So why don’t you just surrender? It will be easier that way."
’...’ Soren ignored her and looked down at his hand, at the dagger, to be more precise, a crazy idea popping up in his mind. ’...I think I am the real fairy.’
