chapters.title: Chapter 340: Whispering Forest [End]
paragraphs: Soren learned a lot. In fact, he might have pieced the whole story together.

Actually, the forest was once a magical place, protected by a powerful fairy and watched over by spirits. It was a sanctuary where both humans and spirits could coexist in peace. The fairy was kind and gentle, beloved by all. She kept the balance, ensured the forest thrived, and welcomed travelers who sought refuge within its borders.

But then the humans grew greedy. They wanted more land and resources. They began cutting deeper into the forest, ignoring the spirits’ warnings. The spirits retaliated, and both sides lost lives in the process. Thus began the cycle of violence.

The fairy tried to stop it, but she was caught in the middle. To the humans, she was no different from a spirit, and therefore an enemy. To the spirits, she was too soft on the humans, and therefore a traitor.
Eventually, for reasons he hadn’t uncovered yet, she met her end.

However, her death shattered the balance. Her grief, her anger, her betrayal seeped into the forest’s magic, twisting it. The spirits who had once protected the forest and the humans who died in it became the black monsters, trapped in an endless cycle of pain.

The whispers were their voices, crying out for help, forgiveness, peace, freedom, revenge, and so on. It was them who guided Soren through the darkness. It was them who showed him the truth. They were the ones who had been waiting for someone to listen.

As for the fake fairy before him, she was a monster born from the fairy’s death, wearing her face, using her voice, but twisted by centuries of hatred and pain. She lured travelers into her web, fed on their suffering, and used their souls to grow stronger.
’...And to solve this problem... To put an end to this vicious cycle of suffering and hatred...’
Soren raised the dagger.
’I, the last remnant of her soul, have to die.’
With a smile at the fake fairy, Soren stabbed himself.
Everything went black in an instant; the whispers, the forest, the fairy’s scream, all swallowed by silence. Then, from somewhere far away, a gentle voice reached him.
’...Thank... you...’
Soren opened his eyes and found himself back in the real world. He sat up slowly and let his senses adjust. Then, he got out of the capsule and looked at Ethea through the glass.
’...She looks like she’s having fun.’
Her lips were curled up, and her expression held a softness he rarely saw when she was awake. She must be really enjoying the story.
’I’m glad...’
His own lips curled up before he could stop them. He stood there for a moment, watching her, then turned and walked toward the sofa to wait for her to wake up.
’...I wonder if I guessed it correctly?’

Actually, he wasn’t 100% sure about his guesses, but knowing he had no other way of contributing, he just chose the option that seemed most logical. The story had given him fragments, and he had pieced them together as best as he could. Whether it was the right answer or not, only the ending would tell.
He sat down and waited.
Fifteen minutes passed.
"...Click."
Ethea’s capsule finally opened.
Soren hurriedly stood up and walked over.
"D-Dear?"
Ethea called out, adjusting back to reality.
"Welcome back," Soren said, smiling. "Did you have fun?"
"...Mmm." Ethea blinked. "I did. But... where did you disappear to?"
"Well, I..." He paused, then leaned down to pick her up. "Let’s talk about this on the way."
"Alright."

With that, they left their private room, and after thanking the staff for the experience and giving their feedback, they took their leave. Surprisingly, they were one of the five groups who managed to reach the hidden ending, so they received a reward from the theater. They decided to check the contents later and headed straight to their next destination.
"...So the villager that guided you was actually the last descendant of the humans who broke the pact?" Soren asked as Ethea explained to him her side of the story.

"Mm." Ethea nodded. "He wasn’t the villain I suspected him to be. He was just a cursed human who had to pay the price for his ancestors’ sins. He couldn’t enter the forest, but he couldn’t leave either. And later, he became the evil fairy’s puppet, forced to sacrifice children and people to keep the cycle going."
"Then, I guess it’s a good thing he got freed, huh."

"...Perhaps," Ethea replied. "But what I understood from this story is that no one is actually innocent. The humans, the spirits, and even the real fairy. The humans were obviously foolish and greedy, cutting deeper into the forest without thinking about the consequences. The spirits were no better. They retaliated with the same cruelty, killing indiscriminately instead of seeking a peaceful solution. And the fairy..." She paused. "She was incompetent... She tried to stop the conflict but couldn’t commit to either side or think of a solution. She tried to save everyone yet ended up saving no one."
"Haha," Soren chuckled. "I wonder how she would feel if she heard that."
"...I told her."
Soren blinked. "What?"
So he guessed wrong, then?

"That’s right." Ethea nodded, oblivious to his blunder. "There was still a part of her real self left inside the evil fairy. She appeared after we defeated her and thanked us for freeing all the trapped souls. That’s when I told her she was incompetent. I also told her she was stupid for having so much power but being unable to use it correctly. She could have just blocked humans from entering, set rules, or even sealed the whole forest. But no, she let everyone walk all over her and then acted surprised when everything fell apart."
Soren stared at her for a moment, then burst out laughing. "You really don’t hold back, do you?"
"She needed to hear it," Ethea said calmly. "And... she agreed with me."
"Haha." Soren wiped away a tear and added. "I wonder if the story writer would laugh or cry if they heard how you treated their tragic villain."
"The truth is the truth." Ethea shrugged. "In fact, they should practice a lot more before writing another story. The pacing was uneven in the middle, and some of the clues were too obvious."
"Fair enough." Soren shook his head, still smiling. "I’m just glad you enjoyed it."
"...I did." Ethea looked at him, her expression softening. "Thank you for planning this, dear."
"Mmm. By the way, what do you think about cruising?"
"Huh? Cruising?"
"That’s right," Soren smiled. "We are going to cruise on Starfall Lake."

So he guessed wrong, then?
"That’s right." Ethea nodded, oblivious to his blunder.
"There was still a part of her real self left inside the evil fairy.
She appeared after we defeated her and thanked us for freeing all the trapped souls.
That’s when I told her she was incompetent.
I also told her she was stupid for having so much power but being unable to use it correctly.
She could have just blocked humans from entering, set rules, or even sealed the whole forest.
But no, she let everyone walk all over her and then acted surprised when everything fell apart."
Soren stared at her for a moment, then burst out laughing.
"You really don’t hold back, do you?"
"She needed to hear it," Ethea said calmly.
"And... she agreed with me."
"Haha." Soren wiped away a tear and added.
"I wonder if the story writer would laugh or cry if they heard how you treated their tragic villain."
"The truth is the truth." Ethea shrugged.
"In fact, they should practice a lot more before writing another story.
The pacing was uneven in the middle, and some of the clues were too obvious."
"Fair enough." Soren shook his head, still smiling.
"I’m just glad you enjoyed it."
"...I did." Ethea looked at him, her expression softening.
"Thank you for planning this, dear."
"Mmm.
By the way, what do you think about cruising?"
"Huh?
Cruising?"
"That’s right," Soren smiled.
"We are going to cruise on Starfall Lake."

chapters.title: Chapter 341: Date [4]
paragraphs: "Starfall Lake..." Ethea repeated the name as memories rushed back. Although it was best to visit it at night, she knew how crowded and noisy it could get. She realized why they were going now and couldn’t help but smile at his consideration. ’Day view isn’t that bad either.’

They spent the next half hour on the road, passing through the busy streets of Adamery before merging onto a highway that led toward the eastern edge of the city. The buildings grew taller and more spaced out, then gradually gave way to open sky and greenery.
Eventually, they reached the entrance to Starfall Lake Park, a famous magical park with a massive holographic sign that read "Welcome to Starfall Lake - Where Stars Meet Water."
Soren pulled into the parking structure and found a spot on the second level. After helping Ethea into a wheelchair, they made their way toward the lakeside promenade.
"...Whoa."
Soren exclaimed as the view opened up before them.

Starfall Lake stretched across the horizon, its surface shimmering with countless tiny crystals that glittered beneath the water like fallen stars. A wide boardwalk framed the lake, lined with magic lamps, cafes with outdoor seating, and docks where boats of various sizes bobbed gently on the water.

Starwing birds circled overhead, their silver-tipped wings catching the sunlight, while lunar turtles surfaced near the docks, their crystal-covered shells gleaming as tourists leaned over the railings to take photos.
"Amazing, right?" Ethea asked, taking in the scenery herself.
"Indeed," Soren nodded. "I can’t seem to take my eyes off it."

"I get what you mean." Ethea smiled. "The night view is even better. The crystals glow brighter after dark, and the stars reflect perfectly on the water. It really does look like the sky has fallen into the lake."
"Then let’s come back at night next time," Soren suggested.
"I’d love that."
"Then it’s settled."

With that, they soon arrived at the dock and rented a nice enchanted boat. It was small but more than enough for the two of them. It had cushioned seats, a retractable canopy for shade, and a self-sailing enchantment that allowed it to glide across the water without needing to be rowed. It even had a small table in the center for snacks and drinks.
Soren helped Ethea into the boat first, making sure she was settled comfortably before getting in himself.
"Captain, we are ready to sail!" He announced playfully.
"Oh?" Ethea raised a brow, amusement flickering in her eyes. "Then, first mate, prepare to set sail."
"Aye, Captain!" Soren grinned and tapped the control panel. The enchantment kicked in, and the boat glided smoothly away from the dock and out onto the simmering water.
"Where to, Captain?"
"Hm..." Ethea surveyed the lake with mock seriousness. "To the center, first mate."
"As you command."
"PFFT!"
They both laughed out loud at the same time.
"Haha..."
The laughter faded a bit later.

Soren then moved from his seat to sit beside Ethea. He wrapped an arm around her, pulling her close, and she leaned into him without hesitation. They enjoyed the boat’s gentle sway and the water lapping against its sides, neither feeling the need to fill the silence with words.
It was only after a while that Ethea broke the silence. "Do you know the legend behind this lake?"
"No?"

"...They say an actual star fell here. Long before the city was built, probably during the apocalypse, a meteorite crashed into this spot. It was said to have been a fragment of a dying star, carrying a piece of its light with it. When it hit the ground, it shattered into countless tiny fragments, and the impact formed the lake. The crystals in the water are the remnants of that star, still glowing even after all these years."
"Hence the Starfall name, huh," Soren smiled. "Do you think it’s actually true, though?"

"... Since I’ve not seen it with my own eyes, I can’t be sure," Ethea replied. "But the crystals in the water are real enough. They’ve been here longer than anyone can remember, and no one has ever been able to explain where they came from. Some say they’re a natural mineral unique to this region, but the legend is more popular."
"Yeah, people tend to believe stories over real facts," Soren chuckled. "It’s more fun that way for them."
"Right," Ethea agreed. "At least we know it is safe, or else this place wouldn’t have been a tourist destination but a restricted zone."
"...Let me check something," Soren muttered and used his ability while staring at the lake. ’Oh! It worked.’
Name: Starfall Lake
Classification: Natural Formation
Origin: Meteorite Impact

Description: A meteor crash formed a lake, shattering the fragment into the crater floor. As the pieces dissolved, their minerals infused the water, giving it a faint luminescence and creating a unique ecosystem.
Atmospheric Mana: Rich / Stable
Effects:
- Minor Healing: Prolonged exposure to the water accelerates natural recovery by a small margin.
- Mana Clarity: The ambient mana around the lake is unusually pure, making it an ideal spot for meditation and mana recovery.
’Huh? You can use appraisal like that too?’ Ethea asked, watching him.

’Yeah, I can use it on places too, but not always,’ Soren explained. ’And... it seems like the legend is actually true. A meteor impact did, in fact, create this lake. And...’ He shared the effects with her before using it on a crystal.
Name: Meteorine
Type: Unique Mineral
Origin: Meteorite Fragment
Description: A crystalline mineral formed from a shattered meteor.
Properties:
- Mana Conduction: Excellent conductor of mana, valuable for crafting and enchantment.
- Luminescence: Glows faintly at all times, brighter in darkness or high-mana environments.
- Energy Storage: Can store a small amount of refined mana. When shattered, the stored energy releases in a single burst.
He quickly scanned it and shared it with Ethea.
’...Dear. I think we should experiment with that ability of yours a lot more.’ Ethea suggested after a moment of silence. ’We might discover a lot of things that way.’

’Don’t worry, since it doesn’t have any cooldowns or consume energy, I am always using it,’ Soren said casually. ’On people, items, food, anything that I can get a read on. It’s almost become a second nature at this point.’
’I see...’ Ethea whispered. ’Now it makes sense...’
Why he was so aware of his surroundings, why he noticed small details others missed, why he seemed to know things without being told. And...
’He’s become like this because of me...’
While it was good to be cautious and observant, she couldn’t help but worry about the toll it might take. Because he would never be able to fully relax.

paragraphs: "By the way, do you want to check what we got as a reward earlier?" Soren suggested. "I’m really curious."
"Of course," Ethea said, nodding. "I almost forgot about it."
Soren then took out the large box and opened it.
"Whoa!"
Two of them exclaimed at the same time.

Inside the box were six beautifully crafted figurines, each one depicting a character from the story. Theo, in his golden armor, his sword raised. Mona, with flames swirling around her hands. Elea in her masked assassin gear, daggers crossed. The boy with red eyes and pitch-black skin, holding a tiny dagger. And the fairy hovering in the air, smiling.

"So this is how I looked?" Soren muttered as he picked up the boy’s figurine. Although it looked somewhat cute and eerie at the same time, he could say it certainly, "...I really resembled a monster, huh."
Ethea picked up the character she played as, her lips curling up. However, her gaze soon moved over to the other, last figurine. "Is this the second hidden character?"

Soren followed her gaze. The sixth figurine was smaller than the others, almost hidden in the box’s corner. It depicted an old man in a worn cloak, his face weathered and tired. He was sitting on a wooden stump, his hands resting on a cane, his eyes closed as if in deep thought.
"Huh?" Soren’s eyes widened as he picked it up. "...I never met him. What about you?"
"Me neither," Ethea shook her head. "Perhaps he would appear in another hidden ending?"

"Right, there must have been some conditions to meet him," Soren muttered and didn’t forget to use appraisal. But it showed nothing noteworthy, just a simple figurine. "Anyway, coupled with the memory crystals we got, this can be considered a special trophy from our little adventure."
"Hehe, you’re right." Ethea laughed. "Let’s visit it again sometimes."

"Alright, I’ll add it to the list too." Soren nodded enthusiastically. "But this time, let’s ’play’ in a comedy or school life. No, in fact, let’s try it all one after another. Tomorrow, we can try again."
"Cool, but let’s just make it once a week. I think it will be more than enough. We have other things to do after all."
"Ah, right. Once a week then.

They continued chatting about which stories they wanted to try next, occasionally pointing out interesting sights on the shore as their boat drifted lazily across the water. The conversation flowed easily, and before they knew it, an hour had passed.
"We should head back," Soren said, glancing at the time. "It’s almost lunch."
"Mm." Ethea nodded. "I’m getting a little hungry."
Soren guided the boat back to the dock and helped Ethea out. After returning the boat and collecting their belongings, they headed back to the car and drove to the hotel for lunch.
"Whoa..." Ethea stared at the table speechlessly. "You... When did you prepare all of this?"

The table was filled with an assortment of dishes. Small cakes with cream and berries, tarts with glazed fruit, flower-shaped chocolates, and pastries dusted with powdered sugar. In front of them sat a large bowl of steaming magic chicken soup and his original meal.

Soren sat down beside her. "In the morning. I wanted to make things you like. I haven’t cooked sweets for you lately, so this time I went all out. There’s the honey cake, the berry tarts, the cream puffs..."
Ethea looked at the spread, then at him. "You made all of this? For me?"
"Mm. It wasn’t that hard. I’m an Expert Magic Chef, remember?" He smiled. "Now, let’s eat before the food gets cold."
"Here, try this first." Soren picked up a spoonful of soup and held it out to her, waiting patiently.

"..." Ethea’s heart swelled, filled to the brim with a warmth that spread through her chest and left her breathless. She wanted the day to end. She wanted it to end so she could finally tell him how much she loved him, so she could stop holding it in and let the words out. But she also wanted it to stretch on forever, because every second with him felt like something she wanted to keep.
"...Thank you."
She accepted the spoonful, the rich broth settling in her chest alongside everything else. ’...Gulp.’
"...It’s tasty as always." She smiled at him.

Soren’s expression brightened as he sighed in relief. He’d been really worried about messing it up since he’d cooked it in a hurry after returning from the lake. But now, it seemed like he’d worried for nothing.
He picked up another spoonful and tasted it himself, and fortunately, it tasted as he intended. However, he realized he used the same spoon again a moment later. ’...Let’s pretend I didn’t notice.’
He told himself while checking Ethea’s expression.
’...Smiling. Hmm...’
His lips curled up, and he ignored the small voice in his head telling him to be careful. He scooped another spoonful and held it out to her.
Ethea accepted it, her eyes never leaving his. She didn’t say anything, but something in her expression made his heart beat a little faster.
Then, before he could pull the spoon back, she reached out and gently took it from his hand. She scooped up a spoonful of soup and held it out toward him.
Soren blinked, caught off guard by her sudden move. "Y-You don’t have to-"
"I know." Ethea cut him off gently while pushing the spoon closer. "But I want to."
"..." Soren stared at her and realized he couldn’t refuse those eyes. He leaned forward and accepted the spoonful.
The soup was warm, but the smile on her face was warmer. He chewed slowly, swallowing both the broth and the feeling rising in his chest.
"...It’s good," he said.
"Of course it is." Ethea’s smile widened. "You made it."
"...Right." Soren chuckled, hiding the fact that it tasted even better than earlier somehow. Perhaps it was because she was the one feeding him this time...
"Here," she scooped another spoonful and held it out again.

"..." Soren obediently leaned forward and accepted it. Then he took the spoon back and returned the favor. They went back and forth like that, feeding each other between bites, until the soup was nearly gone.
"...Shall we move on to the sweets?"

chapters.title: Chapter 343: Date [6]
paragraphs: Once they finished dinner, two of them headed back outside.

Soren drove them to a magic ice rink on the other side of the academy district, a popular spot maintained year-round by ice-affinity enchantments and users. The rink was indoors, with a high glass ceiling that let in natural light and a temperature cool enough to keep the ice frozen but not comfortable for visitors.

Soren put Ethea into an enchanted sled designed for the rink, with smooth runners and a padded seat that kept her stable. He pushed her out onto the ice, and together they glided across the surface, weaving between other skaters and leaving faint trails behind them. Ethea held onto the sides of the sled, laughing as they picked up speed, and Soren grinned behind her. He used his new powers to the max, moving through the crowd with ease. Other skaters gave them room, some smiling at the sight of the couple enjoying themselves.

After they had their fill of the ice, they moved to another room where they could play with snow. They built a snowman, with Soren rolling the snow into balls and stacking them together, while Ethea used her mental power to assist him, like shaping the smaller details he couldn’t quite get right with his hands. She smoothed the surface, carved the eyes and smile, and even added a little scarf made of packed snow.
"...It looks cute, right?" Soren muttered as he stared at their masterpiece.
"Mm..." Ethea hummed in response. "But... Something doesn’t feel right."
"Huh? What is?" Soren raised a brow. "Did we miss something? I am sure a snowman was supposed to look like this."
"...He doesn’t have a partner." Ethea glanced at him, her expression thoughtful. "We should make another one. So he won’t be lonely."
Soren stared at her for a moment, then smiled. "Alright. Let’s make a snowwoman for him."

So they built another one, side by side with the first. This time, Ethea made sure to add the ears, and Soren gave her a matching scarf. When they were done, two snow figures stood together in the middle of the room, holding hands.
"There," Soren said. "Now they’re together."
Ethea smiled. "Much better."
"...We should take a picture." Soren quickly pulled out his phone and handed it to one of the staff members. "Could you take a few pictures of us?"

The staff member nodded and snapped a few photos. Soren and Ethea posed beside their creations, Ethea in her wheelchair and Soren standing behind her, both of them smiling. They also took a few more with different positions and poses.
"Thanks," Soren said, taking his phone back. He glanced at the photos and nodded, satisfied. "These turned out well."

They stayed a little longer, enjoying the snow room before finally deciding it was time to leave. As for their next destination, it was a museum of living paintings, a magic gallery tucked away in the entertainment district of Ademary. They had to use a Teleportation Gate to get there, so it didn’t take long.
The paintings moved within frames, telling stories with and without words. Some showed landscapes that shifted with seasons; others depicted figures who waved at passersby or danced in endless loops.

However, the most impressive ones were the works of a famous Magic Artist from the Empire known as Rahim the Eternal. His creations could talk, answer questions, and even carry on brief conversations with visitors. They were like echoes, fragments of mana and paint that carried limited knowledge and impressions of the people they depicted.

One showed a merchant who would haggle with anyone who approached, offering imaginary goods at imaginary prices. Another depicted a young woman who would sing a soft melody if asked, her voice fading into silence when the song ended. The most striking was a portrait of an old soldier who would tell stories of battles long past, his eyes distant and his voice heavy with memory.

"According to Sir Rahim’s interview," Soren muttered as he finished his research online. "This soldier was a veteran of five wars, two of which were among humans. He survived all of them. But according to Sir Rahim, the man never called himself a hero. He called himself a murderer and nothing more, and asked him to paint him as such."
Ethea looked back at the painting. The soldier’s expression held complex emotions: regret, guilt, grief, and even a trace of happiness. "He must have suffered more emotionally than physically."
"...Right." Soren nodded. "And Sir Rahim said it was one of the hardest paintings he ever created. The man sought no glory; he only wanted people to understand the true cost of war."
"...War," Ethea muttered and fell silent, her expression unreadable.
"...Ethea? Is something wrong?" Soren asked anxiously as she continued staring blankly.
"...No. It’s nothing." She shook her head and turned away. "Just... reminded me of something.
Soren didn’t press. He simply nodded and placed a hand on the back of her wheelchair. "Let’s keep moving."

They continued through the gallery, but Ethea became quieter after that. Soren wanted to ask what troubled her, but decided to wait until she was ready to talk about it herself. Besides, he might be just overthinking again. Perhaps she didn’t like wars, and the painting had stirred unpleasant thoughts.
Fortunately, she recovered her spirits just before the final exhibit.
"I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to worry you."
"No, it’s alright." Soren shook his head. "Anyway, are you ready to move to our next destination?"
"Huh? Already?"

"What do you mean, already. It’s already evening, and if we depart now, we’ll arrive there before the sunset." Soren explained. "That will be our last stop. And... There’s something important I want to tell you there."
"!" Ethea’s heart skipped a beat. She looked at him, searching his expression, but he had already turned away, guiding her wheelchair toward the exit.
’...Something important?’
A thousand possibilities ran through her mind. But deep down, she already had a guess. And the thought of it made her heart beat faster.
’...I can’t wait to hear it.’

Soren drove them to a magic ice rink on the other side of the academy district, a popular spot maintained year-round by ice-affinity enchantments and users.
The rink was indoors, with a high glass ceiling that let in natural light and a temperature cool enough to keep the ice frozen but not comfortable for visitors.
Soren put Ethea into an enchanted sled designed for the rink, with smooth runners and a padded seat that kept her stable.

They built a snowman, with Soren rolling the snow into balls and stacking them together, while Ethea used her mental power to assist him, like shaping the smaller details he couldn’t quite get right with his hands.

"...It looks cute, right?" Soren muttered as he stared at their masterpiece.

Something doesn’t feel right."
"Huh?

chapters.title: Chapter 344: The Truth Is...
paragraphs: "We are here."
Soren parked the car near a tall, elegant tower at the edge of the Western Ademary. It was a circular platform with glass walls and a domed roof.
"What is this place?" Ethea asked curiously as they got out of the car. "...It feels a bit familiar."
Soren paused and looked at her with the same mysterious smile. "You’ll find out soon."
"...Alright." Ethea narrowed her eyes but didn’t press further. She had gotten used to his teasing anyway. "Let’s go in then."
The lobby was spacious and modern, with polished floors and distinctive interior design. A receptionist looked up as they approached.
"Welcome to Freedom Wings. How may I help you?"
"We have a reservation. Under Everly."

The receptionist checked the system, and once they passed the verification process, they instructed them on what to do next. "Just take the lift to the top floor. Someone will be waiting for you there."
"Thank you."
Soren wheeled Ethea to the lift, pressed the button for the highest floor, and watched the doors close as the lift began to rise.
"...We are going to fly, right?" Ethea guessed, glancing at him.
"Haha, I really can’t hide anything from you, huh?" Soren chuckled. "I guess you found out because of the logos and posters on the walls?"
"Mm... If I’m not mistaken, they were called sky gondolas." Ethea answered. "I have tried them a few times before, actually, so I recognized them right away."
"Oh..." Soren blinked, then rubbed the back of his neck. "Then I guess this isn’t as special as I thought."
"No. It’s still special." Ethea gently placed her hand on his. "Because this time, I’m with you.
Soren looked at her, his expression softening. "...Right."

Soon, the lift chimed, and its doors slid open. They stepped out onto a wide platform where several sky gondolas floated in place, waiting at their docks. A staff member approached them with a polite bow.
"Mr. and Mrs. Everly? Right this way, please."

He led them to a gondola at the far end. It looked like a futuristic boat with a curved hull and no roof, but a faint shimmer in the air revealed a protective barrier around it. The Freedom Wings logo was embossed on its sides, a pair of stylized wings spread wide.
Soren lifted Ethea inside and settled her onto the cushioned seat, then climbed in after her. The staff member explained the basic controls and everything else they needed to know, then stepped back.
Soren nodded at the staff and pressed the start button on the control panel. The gondola rose from the platform without a sound, carrying them smoothly into the evening sky.
"...It’s beautiful as ever," Ethea murmured, her eyes fixed on the city below.

The buildings stretched out beneath them, their lights flickering to life as the sun dipped lower. The sky had turned a deep orange, fading into purple at the edges. From this height, Adamery looked like a painting, every street and tower carefully arranged.

"... Beautiful indeed." Soren smiled; however, his eyes were fixed on Ethea, not the view. He had brought her up here to show her the horizon, but now that they were in the air, he could only watch her. The dusk light softened her expression, and the sight of her enjoying the moment took his breath away. To him, nothing on the ground or in the sky came close.
"...Ethea, do you remember Harman and Edith?"
Ethea turned toward him and nodded.

"...They got married three years ago." Soren paused, his gaze drifting toward the horizon before he continued. "And a year after that, they had a daughter... She has Harmen’s sunny smile and Edith’s bright eyes and looks just like a little ball of sunshine."

"I was really happy for them when I found out." Soren continued in a gentle tone. "Harmen, a father. I never thought I’d see the day. He was always the irresponsible one, the one who couldn’t take anything seriously. But now he’s got his own family and home. Someone waiting for him when he comes back."
He turned to look at Ethea. "It... It made me want the same thing."

Ethea’s breath caught in her throat. The way he was looking at her, the weight behind his words. She knew what he meant. She had known for a while now that he felt the same way she did. But hearing him say it, even indirectly, made her heart race.
"...Soren," she began.
But Soren shook his head. "Wait. Let me finish.
He took a breath, then reached over and gently took her hand.

"But... That was just a wishful dream at the time," he admitted. "I was too busy trying to survive. Between work and doing whatever I could to help my sister, I didn’t have room for anything else. So I buried that wish deep down and told myself it wasn’t the right time.
He turned back toward her, a fond, faintly self-deprecating smile curving his lips as the evening wind caught his hair.
"But fate has a strange way of upending everything, doesn’t it? Because then came the day you entered my life. And... that buried wish suddenly didn’t feel so impossible anymore."
Ethea’s breath caught. She opened her mouth to speak, but Soren gently squeezed her hand, silently asking her to wait just a little longer.

"I know our marriage was never something either of us chose for ourselves at the start, thrust upon us by circumstances completely beyond our control... And I told you that I made a promise that night, right? That I would support and protect you till the end of my life... I meant every word of it. And..."
He paused, his thumb brushing lightly against the back of her hand.

"A lot happened after that promise. I awakened. I almost died more times than I can count. I fought enemies I never imagined I’d face. I traveled to places I never thought I’d see. And... through it all, I managed to keep my promise."
"But somewhere along the way, keeping that promise stopped feeling like a duty. It started feeling like a choice. One I would make again and again, no matter what."
He lifted her hand and pressed it against his chest, over his heart, like he wanted her to feel it beating faster than it should.
"Ethea... Actually, I have been lying to you for a long time... No, I’ve been lying to myself."
"The truth is..."
He stared at her for a long moment, then spoke the words he had been holding back for far too long.
"I love you, Ethea."

chapters.title: Chapter 345: Idiot [2]
paragraphs: "I love you, Ethea."

The words lingered between them before the wind and fading sunset light carried them away. Soren kept his gaze fixed on Ethea, waiting, his heart pounding beneath her palm as he searched her eyes for any hint of what she was feeling.
"..." Ethea stared back at him and said nothing for a long moment. Her expression was unreadable, but her hand, still pressed against his chest, kept trembling.
Then slowly, her lips parted.
"...You idiot."
Soren blinked. "H-Huh?"
"You absolute idiot." Her voice cracked, and before he could react, tears welled up in her eyes and spilled down her cheeks. "I’ve been waiting... I’ve been waiting so long to hear you say that."
Soren’s breath caught. "E-Ethea..."

"I... I love you too!" She forced out the words, her voice cracking. "I love you, Soren. I’ve loved you for so long I can’t even remember when it started. And you... you just kept calling it a promise, a duty. I thought... I thought you didn’t..."
She couldn’t finish; the tears wouldn’t let her.
Soren didn’t waste another second. He pulled her into his arms, holding her tightly against him, and buried his face in her hair.
"I-I’m sorry," he whispered. "I’m sorry it took me so long."
Ethea shook her head against his chest. "Just... just don’t stop saying it. Please."
"Ok." He pulled back just enough to look at her, his own eyes glistening now. "I love you. I love you, Ethea. I’ll say it as many times as you need to hear it.
"Hehe," she laughed through her tears, a broken, beautiful sound. "Then, say it again, please."
"I love you."
"Again."
"I love you."

"Hehe~." She pulled him back into the hug, her arms wrapping around him as tightly as they could. She finally felt the last piece of the wall she had built around her heart crumble away, and she let herself feel everything she had been holding back. "I love you too."

Above the city’s glowing expanse, suspended in the amber wash of twilight air, they held each other as the world below faded into irrelevance. The gondola’s magic barrier kept the wind’s bitter edge at bay, leaving only the warmth of his shoulders beneath her hands and the racing cadence of his heart beneath her fingertips.
’...’ Soren shifted his weight slightly, adjusting his hold to ensure she rested comfortably against his chest without putting any strain on her body. ’Hmm...’

However, just like Ethea, he too felt the last lingering doubts in his mind dissolve into nothing, finally allowing himself to accept that he was no longer an unwanted burden discarded by his past, but someone who truly had a home in the arms of the woman holding him so tightly.
"...We really came a long way, didn’t we?" Soren murmured softly after some time, his voice full of affection he no longer tried to hide.
"Mm... We did." Ethea replied, pulling herself back a little. "I’m really glad we did."

"...Me too." Soren smiled and raised his hand, gently wiping away the last traces of tears from her cheeks. His thumb lingered there for a moment, tracing the curve of her cheekbone before slowly pulling away.

They fell silent, their eyes locking in a long, breathless moment as every unspoken feeling from the past few months seemed to compress into the tiny space between their faces. Slowly, as if guided by an overwhelming trust that needed no words, Ethea’s eyelashes fluttered shut, her chin tilting upward just enough to invite him closer.

Soren’s eyes widened, his heart almost leaping out of his body as the sudden realization of what was about to happen surged through him, but he swallowed down the sudden spike of nervousness, slid his hand gently behind her neck to support her, and lowered his head to press his lips against hers.
The kiss landed naturally, carrying no lingering hesitation or doubt as her lips softened against his, yielding completely to his touch.

Soren’s fingers tangled into the long, silken strands at the back of her head, anchoring her with a protective pressure that promised he wasn’t going anywhere. He then leaned further into the kiss, deepening it just enough to let her feel every ounce of the devotion he had carried in silence, pouring all the love he had held back into this one act.

A breathless sigh escaped Ethea’s throat against his mouth, her hands sliding up from his chest to wrap around his shoulders, her fingers tightening into the fabric of his shirt. The guarded edge that had defined her existence for so long melted away, leaving an unreserved surrender that matched his own.
"Huff... Huff..."

When he finally pulled back, he shifted only a fraction of an inch, resting his forehead against hers as their slightly erratic breaths mingled. Opening his eyes, Soren found Ethea gazing up at him, her dark lashes still wet with tears, her ice-blue eyes now carrying a radiant warmth that lit up her entire face. A flush crept across her pale cheeks, taking away any remaining trace of her former composure and leaving her looking happier than he had ever seen her.
"I really..." Soren murmured, his thumb slightly stroking the side of her neck where her pulse hammered rapidly against his palm, "I really love you, Ethea."
Ethea let out a soft chuckle, her lips curling into a smile that reached all the way to her eyes as she leaned upward to press another quick kiss against his mouth.
"I know," she whispered softly, her fingers resting gently against the nape of his neck. "And I will spend the rest of my life making sure you never doubt mine."
Soren tightened his grip around her waist, lowered his head, and kissed her again, lingering for a few seconds before pulling back just far enough to meet her gaze.
"You don’t have to prove anything to me, Ethea. You... You’ve already given me more than I ever thought I was allowed to have. And for that, I will be grateful for the rest of my life."

"And I will spend the rest of my life making sure you never doubt mine."
Soren tightened his grip around her waist, lowered his head, and kissed her again, lingering for a few seconds before pulling back just far enough to meet her gaze.
"You don’t have to prove anything to me, Ethea.
You...
You’ve already given me more than I ever thought I was allowed to have.
And for that, I will be grateful for the rest of my life."

chapters.title: Chapter 346: Date [End]
paragraphs: Soren and Ethea stayed in each other’s arms, neither pulling away. The gondola drifted lazily through the night sky, and above them, the stars had come out in full force. Thousands of them, scattered across the darkness like diamonds on black velvet.
They enjoyed the view without a single word. No words were needed between them now, after all.
However, in reality, it was taking everything they had not to combust on the spot.
’I... I can’t believe I actually said it.’ Soren mumbled to himself. ’...I really confessed to her. And she... she loves me too... Hehe...’
Giggling like a fool, he glanced down at Ethea, who was still nestled against his chest. Her eyes were on the stars, but there was a faint blush on her cheeks that hadn’t been there before.
’...She’s embarrassed too.’
The thought made him want to laugh, but he held it in. Instead, he let his gaze drift upward, joining her in watching the stars.

The night was peaceful, the city below was breathtaking, and the woman he loved was in his arms. Although he couldn’t find a dragon to fly them through the sky like in his favorite childhood movie, this moment felt just as magical.
Ethea shifted again, this time turning her head so she could look at him properly. "...You’re smiling."
"Am I?"
"Mm. You’ve been smiling for the past ten minutes."
"Can you blame me?" He stared right into her eyes. "...I have a pretty good reason after all."
"...Right." Ethea’s cheeks turned into a shade of pink again, but she didn’t turn away. "And for what it’s worth, I don’t think I’m going to stop smiling anytime soon either."
"Then, let’s just keep smiling."

They spent the rest of the ride in comfortable silence, watching the city lights flicker below, and the stars twinkle above. The gondola drifted slowly, following its preset route through the night sky and eventually returned back to the station where they had started.

After disembarking and thanking the staff, they returned straight back to the hotel. Soren quickly prepared dinner, and they ate together, talking about the date and other stuff. Ethea was worried about Zura since they planned to talk today, but Soren reassured her, saying he had already warned her they wouldn’t be available today. He also told her that Ryan and his family would arrive tomorrow or the day after.
By the time they finished eating, bathing, and changing, it was almost past ten o’clock.
Soren put her gently into bed before climbing beside her. He then pulled the covers over both of them and wrapped an arm around her waist, pulling her close.
"Goodnight, Ethea." He planted a gentle kiss on her forehead. "I love you. Have sweet dreams."
"...I love you too."
’...Soren,’ Ethea mentally spoke a moment later; however, her tone sounded a bit hesitant and solemn.
’Hmm? Is something wrong?’ Soren asked attentively.
’...I think... I think I’m going to have a breakthrough tonight.’ Ethea explained. ’Probably as soon as I attempt to.’
’Oh,’ Soren replied, his tone calm despite the sudden gravity of her words. ’Then don’t hold back. I’ll be right here the whole time.’
’...You’re not surprised?’ Ethea asked, sounding surprised herself.

’I was already expecting it and made preparations.’ Soren explained. ’And I’m worried a lot and am afraid something might go wrong. But now I’m more than ready. In fact, I feel like I can do anything right now. So leave the rest to me and just focus on your breakthrough.’

’...’ Ethea went silent. A moment later, Soren felt a familiar sensation: a pair of lips pressing against his. It lasted only a heartbeat before she pulled away, and by the time he opened his eyes, she had already closed hers. ’...Thank you. I’m starting now.’
’Good luck...’

Soren watched her for a moment longer, and his expression slowly turned solemn. While he didn’t lie about making preparations or feeling like he could take the whole world, he knew better than to be complacent. Anything could happen during and after her breakthrough, and only when he was fully focused and in top condition would he be able to deal with them.
So he hoped for the best and prepared for the worst.
Time passed.

Minutes bled into hours as he stood vigil over her. He didn’t let his guard down even for a second, repeatedly using Advanced Appraisal on her every few breaths to monitor her condition, tracking every subtle shift in her mental state and power.
’Hmm?’

Suddenly, his eyes widened, and he moved away from Ethea. The next moment, her body slowly lifted off the bed, floating into the air as if carried by invisible strings. Her hair drifted around her shoulders, and her skin began to glow with a faint silver light.

Before Soren could process it, the light vanished as darkness swallowed the room. It lasted for only a fraction of a heartbeat before pinpricks of brilliance ignited across it, clustering into swirling nebulae and rivers of starlight. The walls, ceiling, and floor seemed to dissolve entirely, transforming the chamber into a vast cosmos centered around her floating form.
’...Is she breaking through?’ Soren frowned and checked her status to be sure. ’...She is.’
If so...

’Was my breakthrough like this too?’ He couldn’t help but ask himself. Unfortunately, he was in his soul space and didn’t know what happened outside at the time. ’...Let’s focus on her. I can think about it later.’
He pushed the thought aside and kept his eyes on Ethea, watching as the stars around her continued to swirl and contract.
’...It must be related to the technique she cultivates.’ He guessed and sent a message to Malakor to be ready at all times.

A few minutes passed, and the room slowly returned to its previous state. The stars faded, the darkness receded, and Ethea’s body descended gently back toward the bed. Soren reached out and caught her before she could land too hard, cradling her in his arms. He laid her down carefully, brushing a strand of hair from her face.
Then he felt it.
Through their bond, he sensed a new presence. Something dark and malicious was moving inside her, rising from deep within and clawing its way toward the surface.
’The curse!’

chapters.title: Chapter 347: Curse Strikes Again
paragraphs: ’The curse!’

Without hesitation, Soren activated their bond ability to the fullest, pulling the malicious energy to himself. The moment it entered his body, the pain hit. It was a lot worse than last time, a searing agony that tore through his chest and spread outward, racing through his limbs and up into his skull in the span of a single breath.

His mind nearly went blank for a moment. His body convulsed as well, and he bit his tongue hard enough to draw blood to stay conscious while keeping his mouth shut so he wouldn’t make a sound. Ethea was still unconscious, probably digesting her breakthrough, so he didn’t want to disturb her.
Fortunately, he had his evolved constitution, Sovereign’s Fortitude, Hyper Regeneration, Indomitable Soul, and Core Refinement.
Whoosh-!

Those four, along with everything else useful, activated at once, each responding to the threat accordingly. The first thing that was affected was obviously the pain. Sovereign’s Fortitude made it bearable, and its trauma clarity effect helped him clear his thoughts and sharpen his mind.

Core Refinement began breaking down the curse at the same time, drawing it inward and slowly converting it into raw mana that his body absorbed without resistance. His frozen pathways and core held firm, enduring every strike the curse threw at them while Hyper Regeneration repaired whatever damage slipped through.

The curse also pushed into his mind, searching for cracks in his consciousness. Indomitable Soul held the barrier, and the moment the hostile energy made contact, Soul Anvil Counter activated. It caught the intrusion, compressed it, and crushed it, converting the energy into a boost for his own mental output.
’...’ Soren couldn’t help but chuckle in relief. ’...It’s working.’

He then leaned back against the headboard, keeping one hand on Ethea’s. His eyes stayed on her, watching for any change in her condition, but his shoulders finally relaxed. There was nothing more he could do. The abilities were handling the curse on their own, and they were doing a better job than he had expected.
So he sat there and watched, monitoring her through their bond and his Appraisal while the curse continued to fight a losing battle inside him.
’...Let’s see how far they can go.’

He wanted to see whether his abilities could handle the curse on their own, how long it would take, and how much of the curse he could convert into usable mana. It was useful information. If this worked, he could plan for future encounters with the curse.
[Ding!]
’Oh, I guess it’s about time.’
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Ethea Everly]
[Analyzing Investment...]

[Investment: You prepared and shared magic meals specifically tailored to the target’s preferences and dietary needs. You used rare ingredients/elixirs with restorative properties to support her recovery and stabilize her condition. You also played a crucial role in helping her settle a long-standing score with one of her past enemies. Furthermore, you provided the foundation and support she needed to break through to the next stage of her mental cultivation, ensuring her breakthrough was stable and successful...]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target’s physical condition has improved significantly. Her core stability has increased, her mana pathways have strengthened, and her overall vitality has risen. The successful breakthrough to the second stage of her mental cultivation has also elevated her mental power...]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: SUPREME]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Mental Power +30,000]
[2. Cooking Mastery +2]
[3. Soul-Nourishing Concoction x3]
[4. Myriad Pathway Nutrient Fluid x5]
[5. Sovereign Vitality Elixir x5]
[6. Recipe Unlocked: Nature’s Embrace]
[7. Recipe Unlocked: Soul-Warming Broth]
[8. Advanced Caretaking Knowledge]
[9. Mirror of the Self]
[10. Spirit Puppet]
[Integration initiated...]
’Huff...’

Soren took a deep breath, his heartbeat quickening as the integration began. His first thought was to worry. What if it intervened with the curse’s attack? What if the process disrupted his abilities while they were still fighting against the malicious energy?
However, he soon realized that he had nothing to worry about.

The returns were only mind-related this time, except for the items. So he simply stayed still and let the integration pass, accepting the new knowledge, recipes, and mental power as they settled into his mind. And soon, a familiar message appeared in his vision.
[Integration Complete!]
’Huff...’
He let out a relieved sigh.
Sensing a movement, he opened his eyes and looked down to his side, at Ethea, to be more exact. Her fingers twitched against his hand, her eyelids fluttered, and then, slowly, she opened her eyes.
Their gazes met.

"...Congratulations on your breakthrough, dear!" Soren smiled and leaned over to brush a strand of hair from her face. But before his fingers could reach her, Ethea’s hand shot up and grabbed his wrist. Her grip was weak, but her eyes were sharp, fixed on his face with an intensity that made him pause.
"...You’re doing it again." She muttered, sounding a little angry but mostly worried and sad.
Soren didn’t try to pull his wrist free. Instead, he softened his expression and gently turned his palm to cradle her hand.

"There’s no need to worry. I’m more than powerful enough to handle it now." He explained, and, noticing she still didn’t look convinced, added. "Well, if I wasn’t, I would be spitting blood or on the verge of losing consciousness by now. "
Ethea studied his face, searching for any sign of pain or strain. Finding none, she asked. "...Are you really sure?"
"I’m sure." He nodded. ’If you don’t believe me, you can check through our bond. And I’m using all my abilities to handle it too.’
’Alright.’ Ethea closed her eyes immediately and opened them a few seconds later. ’...But I’m still worried.’
’You don’t have to be.’ Soren squeezed her hand. ’I told you, didn’t I? I’m strong enough now. The curse can’t hurt me as it did before.’
Ethea still didn’t look convinced. ’...You always say that. And then you push yourself too far.’
’This time it is really different. I’m not pushing myself at all. In fact, my abilities are handling it on their own.’
Ethea stared at him for a long moment. Then, slowly, her posture relaxed. ’...Fine. But if you start feeling worse, you tell me immediately and... share it with me.’

chapters.title: Chapter 348: Spirit Puppet
paragraphs: ’...Alright.’ Soren nodded helplessly. ’But... We should still be careful. We don’t know if another gate is gonna open again or if more assassins are lurking around.’

’...Right.’ Ethea blinked in agreement. If something like that happened again, not only they, but the whole city would be in trouble. Although Ademary was one of the most powerful places in the empire, you could expect anything from them. She still remembered how they attacked the academy before. ’...Dear, is Malakor on guard right now?’
’Yes, I asked him to be ready just in case.’ Soren confirmed her guess. ’He’s keeping an eye on the whole city and will alert us if anything happens.’
’I see...’ She sighed in relief. ’That puts me at ease.’
’Me too. And while we are at it, let me check your condition.’ Soren suggested and appraised her again. ’Let’s see...’
Name: Ethea Everly
Status: Stable (Recovering / Critical)
[Rank: 7th Circle [Crippled / Regressed]]
[Mental Cultivation: Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra — Stage 2: Soul Tempered Core Stage]
[Current Mana Level: 0 (Sealed)]
[Current Mental Power: 65547 / 150000]
[Core condition: 77% destroyed...]
[Mana pathways: 31% functional...]
[Physical Condition:]
- Paralysis
- Chronic Pain (Level 3/10 - Managed / Temporarily Soothed)
- Nerve Damage
[Authority Status: Frost Sovereign - Sealed/Dormant]
[Affliction Detected:]
[Curse: Eclipse’s Corrosion - Grade: Eighth Circle]
[Details: ???]
[Effect: ???]
[Origin: ???]
[Estimated Survival Without Treatment: 10 months]
[Abilities: Unshackled Soul (S-Rank), Sovereign Swordsmanship (SS-Rank), ? (SSS-Rank), (Absolute Zero)]
[Affinities: Ice (Grade ?), , ]
[Mental State: Alert, Concerned, Relieved]
[Investment Value: MYTHIC]
[Potential: Immeasurable]

’Oh, there’s some good progress.’ He smiled and shared her status with her. ’By the way, I think you should use the chance to cultivate and ride the momentum of your breakthrough for as long as possible. It’ll help stabilize your new stage and push you further.’
’But first, take this.’ He reached out to his inventory and handed her a vial of Soul-Nourishing Concoction. ’It will help you greatly.’
’...Alright.’ Ethea agreed. ’Can you... help me sit up then?’
’Of course.’ Soren carefully helped her into a more comfortable position, propping pillows behind her back to keep her steady. Once she was settled, he uncorked the vial and held it out to her.
Ethea took it and drank it in one slow sip, her expression tightening briefly as the liquid went down. Then she closed her eyes and began to cultivate.
’...Malakor, did you notice anything suspicious?’
’I haven’t so far, Master,’ Malakor replied.
’Good. Keep watching. If anything changes, let me know immediately.’
’Understood.’
With that secured and Ethea gone back to cultivating, he decided to check out his rewards.
’Thirty thousand mental power?’ He raised a brow but smiled in satisfaction. ’My guess turned out to be true, huh.’

He was also satisfied with the rest of the returns. His stock of elixirs and medicine multiplied again. He also learned two new recipes: one to improve life force and the other to boost mental power. Surprisingly, he also learned more about caretaking. He guessed that if he took an exam for professional nursing or caretaking, he would pass with flying colors.

’And with the cooking mastery returns, I can call myself a true Senior Magic Chef.’ His understanding of cooking deepened even further, and now, he could easily make food that had long-lasting effects on those who ate it, or even permanent effects if the ingredients were potent enough and the dish was prepared with the right techniques.
’I can practice those recipes for my sister with ease now, too.’
However, what caught his attention most were the last two items: Mirror of the Self and Spirit Puppet.
’...Hmmm. The mirror reveals a person’s true self,’ he read through the description carefully. ’And its true worth is detecting possession, mind control, or anyone hiding behind illusions.’

He nodded slowly. That was incredibly useful, especially after everything they had been through with the Puppeteer. If someone was being controlled or if a person wasn’t who they appeared to be, this mirror would help them reveal it.
’And the Spirit Puppet...’ He moved on to the next item. ’Oh... Hmm... I see...’
His lips curled up as soon as he finished reading its description. ’This is gonna be a perfect gift to Ethea. I am sure she will like it too.’

Smiling, he closed the windows and focused back on his body. The curse was still inside him, trying to tear him apart, but Soren could feel it wouldn’t last much longer. Just a few more minutes and it would be gone.
’...Hmm?’ Soren furrowed his brows, and the next second, his eyes widened. ’Again?!’

In Ethea’s body, the curse erupted once more, with even more ferocity than before. Fortunately, he hadn’t let his guard down, so he managed to react in time, using their bond to pull the surge of corruption out of her and into his own body.
Whoosh-!

The new wave of curse crashed straight into the one still lingering inside him, combining into a violent force that tore through his chest. It lashed out at his heart, lungs, and core all at once, driving a gasp from his throat. His vision flickered, and he buckled forward, coughing up a spatter of blood onto the floor.
Even then, he refused to close the connection. The curse was still pouring out of her in a stream, making it impossible to take it all in one pull, so he held his ground and bore the brunt of it.
’Urgh...’

Gritting his teeth against the burn in his chest, he unstoppered an elixir vial with his thumb and swallowed the contents in one gulp. He ignored the sting in his throat as the liquid spread through his body, keeping the siphon locked open while the potion increased his recovery speed.
"!" On the bed, Ethea’s eyelids snapped open. She gasped, her gaze locking directly onto the crimson on his lips as her pupils shrank to tiny points. "S-Soren!"

She couldn’t move her body, but her hands shot out and grabbed his arm, her fingers digging into his sleeve with what little strength she had. Her eyes squeezed shut as she reached through their bond to check his condition. What she found made her breath hitch. The curse was pouring into him like a flood, several times stronger and more violent than before, and he was taking it all.
’S-Stop! Soren, stop it, please! It’s too much!’

We don’t know if another gate is gonna open again or if more assassins are lurking around.’

Although Ademary was one of the most powerful places in the empire, you could expect anything from them.

’Yes, I asked him to be ready just in case.’ Soren confirmed her guess. ’He’s keeping an eye on the whole city and will alert us if anything happens.’

chapters.title: Chapter 349: Goodnight...
paragraphs: ’...Soren, please, stop it. It’s too much!’
Soren finally heard Ethea’s voice and turned toward her. ’D-Don’t worry. I can endure it. I was just caught off guard earlier, that’s all.’
’Still!’ Ethea’s fingers dug into his sleeve. ’You don’t have to take all of it. Let me handle some. I can-’
’No.’ Soren cut her off decisively. ’I said I love you, right? That also means I don’t want you to get hurt or be in any more pain. So let me handle this, ok?’
’...’ Ethea wanted to say something, but seeing his firm expression and the overflowing emotions in his eyes, she swallowed them back. ’...Alright.’

’Thank you.’ Soren smiled and took a deep breath before closing his eyes. However, he used his right hand to gently pry her fingers from his sleeve and intertwine them with his own, holding on as if to reassure her that everything would be okay. ’...And you can continue cultivating; I will tell you when it is over.’

’...Ok.’ Ethea replied and lay back down. However, she kept looking at him instead of going back to cultivate. Well, how could she not? She loved him too, so she didn’t want him to get hurt and be in pain either. Especially because of her.

Yet, logically, she knew this was the best option they had too, and she might have overreacted a bit. His abilities were more suited for handling the curse, and she was still... a cripple. If she tried to interfere, she’d only make things worse.
But... She couldn’t help it. Especially after hearing those words, after finally saying them back, after everything they had been through to get here.

’...No, Ethea. You have to get it together. Love isn’t all about clinging to each other and sharing every burden. It’s also about trusting each other to handle what they can, and being there for them when they can’t.’

She took a deep breath and forced herself to look away. If she wanted to truly help him, if she wanted to stand beside him as an equal rather than a burden, she needed to get stronger. She needed to overcome her own limitations or find a way to support him that didn’t rely on her broken body. Only then could she protect him the way he protected her, and only then could they move forward together.
So she closed her eyes, steadied her breathing, and returned to her cultivation. But even as she focused on her own progress, her hand never let go of his.
Time passed slowly.

Soren kept his focus inward, monitoring the curse as it continued its assault. Every few minutes, it would surge, trying to break through his defenses, and every time, he pushed it back with the help of his abilities. He also used the chance to cultivate mentally.
This continued for more than half an hour and then stopped.

The last remnants of the curse dissolved, purified, and were absorbed into his core. Soren opened his eyes to find his body drenched in sweat, and his clothes clinging to his skin. The bedsheets beneath him were stained with blood and grime, and he could feel a layer of dirt covering his skin from the purification process.
’...I need to wash up.’
He carefully pulled his hand away from Ethea’s, making sure not to startle her. He then slipped out of bed and made his way to the bathroom, grabbing a fresh set of clothes on the way.

The shower was quick but thorough. He scrubbed away the sweat and grime, letting the warm water wash it all down the drain. When he was done, he dried himself off, changed into clean clothes, and returned to the bedroom.
He walked over to the bed and gently placed a hand on Ethea’s shoulder.
"Ethea... It’s over."
A moment passed, and her eyes fluttered open. "...Are you ok, now?"
"Yes, better than ever," Soren grinned. ’I got rid of all the curse, so don’t worry.’
"That’s good." Ethea sighed in relief. She checked it before opening her eyes just now, but hearing it from him made her feel a lot better.
"Ethea." He squeezed her hand one last time before letting go. "...Give me a moment. I need to clean up."
"Alright." Ethea blinked and raised her hands.

Soren chuckled and leaned down. He picked her up carefully and placed her in her wheelchair, then quickly stripped the soiled bedsheets and wiped down the floor. Once everything was clean, he lifted her again and laid her back down on the fresh sheets.
"There. Good as new."
Ethea settled against the pillow, her eyes still on him. "...You should rest too.
"I will." He climbed into bed beside her and pulled the covers over them both before hugging her. "Goodnight, Ethea."
"...Soren."
"Yes?"
"I... We’re... now... lovers too, right?" Ethea’s cheeks turned a soft shade of red as she forced the words out.
Soren tilted his head, a bit caught off guard by the question. "Y-Yes. I mean... since we’re married and confessed our love... we are lovers now. Or... should I say a loving couple?"
"...Then... I... I want to do what normal loving couples do... like... like goodnight ki... s.s..."
Her voice trailed off, growing quieter with each word until it was barely above a whisper.
’...Gulp.’

For a moment, he just stared at her, frozen by the sheer vulnerability she was showing him. Then he took a deep breath, reached out slowly, and gently cupped her cheek. His thumb traced the curve of her cheekbone, feeling the warmth of her skin beneath his fingertips.
"...Ethea."
She looked up at him, her ice-blue eyes wide and perhaps a little expectant.
"I love you. And I will do my best to make you happy for the rest of our lives."

Then he leaned in, closing the distance between them, and pressed a soft kiss to her lips. It was gentle and unhurried, as if he was trying to tell her everything he felt without a single word. When he finally pulled back, he rested his forehead against hers.
"...Goodnight, my love."
"Mm... G-Goodnight to you too... my love..."

chapters.title: Chapter 350: Eternal Bond
paragraphs: "...my love."
Soren felt a familiar warmth as her lips brushed against his, light as a feather. Unfortunately, it only lasted for a moment.
They stared at each other as the silence stretched between them. Then, slowly, matching smiles spread across their faces.
"...Hehe."
"...Pfft."

They both laughed, and Ethea leaned forward, burying her face against his chest, her shoulders still shaking. Soren wrapped his arms around her and held her close, gently resting his chin on top of her head.
They stayed like that for a while, neither wanting to move. Eventually, their breathing evened out, and their eyes drifted closed.
[Ding!]
Soren’s eyes snapped open. He was in his mental space, sitting cross-legged on the familiar floor of his consciousness.
’Already complete?’
He muttered to himself and watched as messages came one after another.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Ethea Everly]
[Analyzing Investment...]

[Investment: You shared your past and allowed her to understand the life you lived before her and the burdens you carried. This gave her the trust she needed to share her own past, and you listened without judgment, supporting her through memories she had kept buried for years... You finally confessed your true feelings for her, giving her the words she had been waiting to hear and the courage to confess her own. When her curse erupted during her breakthrough, you took the full brunt of it into yourself and neutralized it...]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target has fully recovered her mental state. The trauma and loss she had buried for years have been confronted and overcome, and the walls she built around her heart have crumbled. She found the courage to confess her own feelings, and the bond between you has deepened beyond measure. Your souls and fates are now deeply connected, bound to each other for as long as you both shall live.]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: MYTHIC]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Curse Resistance (S-Rank)]
[2. Ability Evolution: Soul-Binding Symbiosis → Eternal Bond]
[3. Ability Evolution: Guardian’s Resolve → Guardian’s Devotion]
[4. Ability Evolution: Advanced Appraisal → Eyes of Truth]
[5. Aeternum]
[Integration initiated...]

’Whoa!’ Soren’s eyes lit up as soon as he saw the returns. However, before he could process it, his eyelids grew heavy. His thoughts slowed, his vision blurred, and he felt himself sinking. He tried to focus and force himself to stay conscious, but it was already too late as his consciousness slipped away.
His eyes closed, and the world faded to black.
When they opened again, he found Ethea tucked against his chest, her hair spread across the pillow, and sunlight streaming through the curtains above them.
Soren blinked a few times, his mind still groggy. ’...When did I fall asleep?’

He glanced down at Ethea and, strangely, he felt as if he could feel her heartbeat alongside his own, as if there was something invisible connecting them, linking them together in a way that hadn’t been there before.
’...Wait. I remember it now. I fell unconscious after the integration started.’

At the same time, he noticed new information in his mind, along with changes in his body and soul. He took a deep breath to collect his thoughts and closed his eyes again. He spent a few minutes sorting out these changes and powers, and when he finished, a smile appeared on his face. ’A-Amazing...’

Even for a Mythic-grade investment, the returns exceeded his expectations. The first thing that caught his attention was a new ability called Curse Resistance. As the name suggested, it granted him a passive resistance to all forms of curse-based afflictions. Curses that would normally take hold and fester would now struggle to even latch onto him, and those that did would be significantly weakened and easier to purify.
But that wasn’t all. The ability came with two active effects.

The first was called Curse Reflection. Once per day, he could activate it to reflect any curse that was currently affecting him back onto its caster. The reflected curse would be amplified, hitting the original caster with double the potency. It was a perfect counter against anyone who relied on curses as their primary weapon.

The second was called Curse Detection. By focusing his senses, he could now perceive the presence of curses on people, objects, or locations within a certain radius. Not only would he know if a curse existed, but he would also gain a general understanding of its nature, severity, and how it was cast. It would make tracking curse-users and identifying afflicted individuals much easier.
Without hesitation, he used it on Ethea right away.

A golden light mapped itself across his mind, tracing the contours of her body and soul. The black rot of the curse that plagued her breakthrough had long disappeared. Yet, as he looked closer, something subtle caught his attention.
’...Hmmm.’

Frowning, he focused on that faint trace. Yet the moment his perception brushed against it, he felt a deep terror surge through him, so overwhelming that his mind recoiled on instinct. The trace vanished at the same time, and no matter how many times he tried, he couldn’t find it again.
’...It seems like I’m still too weak to see it clearly.’

Sighing in disappointment, he decided to leave it alone for now and instead decided to use it on himself. He was curious how it would work on him and whether the curse really disappeared and wasn’t hiding inside him.
He suddenly froze, his mouth opening and closing. Then, his eyes lit up, and he quickly summoned his status window.
[PERSONAL INFORMATION]
Name: Soren Everly
Age: 23
Circle Rank: Fourth Circle (Late Stage)
Mental Cultivation: Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture — Stage 2: Soul Tempered Core Stage
Potential: ???
Hunter Rank: C
[CORE STATUS]
Mana Capacity: 495,860 / 650,000
Mental Power Capacity: 159740 / 180000
Core Stability: Stable
Pathway Integrity: Excellent
Affinity: Ice (Grade 7 - S Rank) | Wind (Grade 5 - B Rank) | Life Force (Grade 5 - B Rank) Darkness (Sealed) | ??? | ???
[INNATE ABILITIES]
• Curse Resistance (S-Rank)
• Hyper Regeneration (S-Rank)
• Glacial Emperor Constitution (S-Rank)
• Sovereign’s Fortitude (S-Rank)
• Limit Break (S-Rank)
• Indomitable Soul (S-Rank)
• Overlord’s Aura (A-Rank)
• Fire Resistance (C-Rank)
• Vital Harmony (A-Rank)
• Nature’s Eyes (B-Rank)
• Core Refinement (S-Rank)
[SPECIAL ABILITIES]
• Eternal Bond
• Guardian’s Devotion
• Amplification
• Civic Sight
• Beacon of Hope
[UNIQUE ABILITIES]
[TECHNIQUES & SKILLS]
• Cooking Mastery (Expert Lv. 1)
[Affliction Detected:]
[Curse: Fortune’s Frown — Grade: Fourth Circle]
[Details: Small misfortunes occur more frequently, and major conveniences are less likely to happen...]
[Origin: ???]
[Estimated Duration: Permanent unless dispelled or transferred]
[EQUIPMENT]
• Tether Bond (Bound to: Ethea Everly)
• Hunter’s License (Standard - Grade C)
• Ring Of Boundless Void
• Aeternum (Bound to: Soren & Ethea Everly)

’I see. It’s called Fortune’s Frown, huh?’ He squinted at the details, and it matched the feeling he got from curse detection. It was basically a bad-luck type curse. However, despite being a 4th circle curse, its origin was hidden. ’Which means... It’s probably the same person who cursed Ethea.’

They might have cursed him after he dealt with Ethea’s curse yesterday. That would make the most sense; however, there was a chance it was someone else, and someone powerful, who did it. However, the chances were low since he hadn’t offended anyone personally. Well, there were a few people, like the head of the Vale family, his own family, or perhaps someone from the Outcasts.
’...What should I do about it?’

He pondered whether to use Curse Reflection and send the curse back at its damn caster. However, he decided against it for now. He wanted to test the ability itself first, to see how well it could suppress the curse on its own. Since the duration was listed as permanent unless dispelled or transferred, he could afford to wait and observe. If it proved too troublesome, he would use Curse Reflection then.
Nodding to himself, he decided to check his status while he was at it, and the first thing he noticed was the increase in his mental power and mana.
’It’s probably because of Ethea’s curse.’ He guessed. Core Refinement refined about half of it while he used the rest to cultivate his mind.
The only other changes were the evolutions of his two special abilities and a new artifact bound to him and Ethea. He first focused on Guardian’s Devotion, which evolved from Guardian’s Resolve.

Before, it had been a passive ability that doubled his physical defense and mental fortitude whenever he took a defensive stance to shield Ethea, along with a counter effect that slowed attackers. Now, the evolution had strengthened those effects and added something new.

He couldn’t be mentally controlled, charmed, or compelled to abandon her. Any attempt to do so would automatically fail and trigger a backlash against the attacker. On top of that, he could now place a temporary mark on Ethea that allowed him to teleport to her side once per day instantly. The mark would last until used or until the next sunrise, and he didn’t have to renew it if he chose not to use it before then.

’...This is a pretty good evolution. However, I can resist something like that even without this effect. After all... my heart already belongs to her, and there’s nothing in this world or any other that could make me abandon her.’

’Whoa!’ Soren’s eyes lit up as soon as he saw the returns.
However, before he could process it, his eyelids grew heavy.
His thoughts slowed, his vision blurred, and he felt himself sinking.
He tried to focus and force himself to stay conscious, but it was already too late as his consciousness slipped away.
His eyes closed, and the world faded to black.
When they opened again, he found Ethea tucked against his chest, her hair spread across the pillow, and sunlight streaming through the curtains above them.
Soren blinked a few times, his mind still groggy. ’...When did I fall asleep?’

He glanced down at Ethea and, strangely, he felt as if he could feel her heartbeat alongside his own, as if there was something invisible connecting them, linking them together in a way that hadn’t been there before.
’...Wait.
I remember it now.
I fell unconscious after the integration started.’
At the same time, he noticed new information in his mind, along with changes in his body and soul.
He took a deep breath to collect his thoughts and closed his eyes again.
He spent a few minutes sorting out these changes and powers, and when he finished, a smile appeared on his face. ’A-Amazing...’
Even for a Mythic-grade investment, the returns exceeded his expectations.
The first thing that caught his attention was a new ability called Curse Resistance.
As the name suggested, it granted him a passive resistance to all forms of curse-based afflictions.
Curses that would normally take hold and fester would now struggle to even latch onto him, and those that did would be significantly weakened and easier to purify.
But that wasn’t all.
The ability came with two active effects.
The first was called Curse Reflection.
Once per day, he could activate it to reflect any curse that was currently affecting him back onto its caster.
The reflected curse would be amplified, hitting the original caster with double the potency.
It was a perfect counter against anyone who relied on curses as their primary weapon.
The second was called Curse Detection.
By focusing his senses, he could now perceive the presence of curses on people, objects, or locations within a certain radius.
Not only would he know if a curse existed, but he would also gain a general understanding of its nature, severity, and how it was cast.
It would make tracking curse-users and identifying afflicted individuals much easier.
Without hesitation, he used it on Ethea right away.
A golden light mapped itself across his mind, tracing the contours of her body and soul.
The black rot of the curse that plagued her breakthrough had long disappeared.
Yet, as he looked closer, something subtle caught his attention.
’...Hmmm.’
Frowning, he focused on that faint trace.
Yet the moment his perception brushed against it, he felt a deep terror surge through him, so overwhelming that his mind recoiled on instinct.
The trace vanished at the same time, and no matter how many times he tried, he couldn’t find it again.
’...It seems like I’m still too weak to see it clearly.’
Sighing in disappointment, he decided to leave it alone for now and instead decided to use it on himself.
He was curious how it would work on him and whether the curse really disappeared and wasn’t hiding inside him.
He suddenly froze, his mouth opening and closing.
Then, his eyes lit up, and he quickly summoned his status window.

’I see.
It’s called Fortune’s Frown, huh?’ He squinted at the details, and it matched the feeling he got from curse detection.
It was basically a bad-luck type curse.
However, despite being a 4th circle curse, its origin was hidden. ’Which means...
It’s probably the same person who cursed Ethea.’
They might have cursed him after he dealt with Ethea’s curse yesterday.
That would make the most sense; however, there was a chance it was someone else, and someone powerful, who did it.
However, the chances were low since he hadn’t offended anyone personally.
Well, there were a few people, like the head of the Vale family, his own family, or perhaps someone from the Outcasts.
’...What should I do about it?’
He pondered whether to use Curse Reflection and send the curse back at its damn caster.
However, he decided against it for now.
He wanted to test the ability itself first, to see how well it could suppress the curse on its own.
Since the duration was listed as permanent unless dispelled or transferred, he could afford to wait and observe.
If it proved too troublesome, he would use Curse Reflection then.
Nodding to himself, he decided to check his status while he was at it, and the first thing he noticed was the increase in his mental power and mana.
’It’s probably because of Ethea’s curse.’ He guessed.
Core Refinement refined about half of it while he used the rest to cultivate his mind.
The only other changes were the evolutions of his two special abilities and a new artifact bound to him and Ethea.
He first focused on Guardian’s Devotion, which evolved from Guardian’s Resolve.
Before, it had been a passive ability that doubled his physical defense and mental fortitude whenever he took a defensive stance to shield Ethea, along with a counter effect that slowed attackers.
Now, the evolution had strengthened those effects and added something new.
He couldn’t be mentally controlled, charmed, or compelled to abandon her.
Any attempt to do so would automatically fail and trigger a backlash against the attacker.
On top of that, he could now place a temporary mark on Ethea that allowed him to teleport to her side once per day instantly.
The mark would last until used or until the next sunrise, and he didn’t have to renew it if he chose not to use it before then.
’...This is a pretty good evolution.
However, I can resist something like that even without this effect.
After all... my heart already belongs to her, and there’s nothing in this world or any other that could make me abandon her.’
